title: Getting started with Nexi
summary: How to move around, how to be sure you are on the newest version, and what to do when a screen looks wrong.

p: The left rail is the module list — Production, HR, Payroll, Maintenance, IT, Irrigation, Inventory, Packaging, Logistics, Fleet, CRM, Security, Quality, Licenses, Projects, Administration. Click one and you land on that module’s cockpit: a live summary of what needs attention.
Under the module name is the screen list. That is where the real work happens — the cockpit only points you at it.
The title bar shows the version, for example v19.91. When something is fixed for you, the fix only reaches your machine after a hard refresh.
steps: On Windows press Ctrl + Shift + R
On a Mac press Cmd + Shift + R
Check the title bar shows the new number

sections.h: Your work is shared, not local
p: Nexi syncs between the machines. What you save, the others see. That is why a record you did not create can change while you are looking at it — someone else edited it.
If two people edit the same thing, the newer save wins. So do not leave a screen open for hours with half-typed work: save it.

sections.h: Every module opens on its cockpit
p: Click a module in the left rail and you land on its cockpit: a live summary of that module — one box per screen with its open calls, criticals and warnings, the records behind them, and a click straight through to the screen that holds the detail.
It is built from the same data the screens use, so a figure that looks wrong on the cockpit is wrong on the screen too — open it and see.

note.k: IF IT SAYS A SHORT NAME
note.t: A cockpit headed with a short code rather than the module name — “prod” instead of “PRODUCTION” — means an old copy of the app. Hard refresh.

sections.h: “Coming Soon” on a screen this guide describes
p: It means you are on an old copy of the app. Hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac) and check the version in the title bar. If the page still says Coming Soon after that, say so — the screen exists and something is wrong.
A few screens genuinely are not built yet — Licenses and the Projects dashboards. Those are not described here, and Coming Soon is the truth on them.

sections.h: When a screen looks empty or wrong
steps: Hard refresh first (Ctrl+Shift+R). Most odd screens are an old copy of the app.
Check the top of the screen for a red or amber banner — it usually says what is missing.
If a button does nothing, you probably do not have the right for it. The screen normally says who to ask.
Still wrong? Ask in this Help centre — the “Ask” tab sends it to Eyal, Dr Amy and IT with the screen name attached.

p: That is not a rights problem — it is your account record on this machine. Every permission in Nexi is checked against the signed-in account; if that record is missing from this machine’s user list or marked inactive (a sync from another machine can do that), every check reads as none, while the name and role in the top corner stay as they were at sign-in.

A red banner at the top of the screen now says which it is and offers the one safe repair: restore the account from this machine’s saved copy, reactivate it (primary administrator only), recreate the default admin (only when it is the admin account and no copy exists), or sign out and back in.

note.t: If the banner is not there yet (older copy of the app), signing out and back in re-reads your record and fixes the stale case on its own. If the sign-in is then refused, the account really is missing or inactive on that machine — another administrator restores it in Administration → Users.

sections.h: Jumping between a guide and the screen it explains
p: Every guide opens with a Contents list: click a heading to jump to it. Each section ends with ↑ Contents to go back up.
Where a guide names a screen, you see a blue ↗ button, for example ↗ 👷 Labor Payroll (Weekly). Click it and Nexi takes you straight to that screen.
A 📖 Back to the guide button then waits at the bottom-left of the screen. Click it and you are back in the same guide, at the same section. ✕ hides it.
You only see ↗ for screens your account may open.
The 💬 Ask for guidance tab is there for exactly that. Say what you need — “Show me how”, “Something is wrong”, or “I need a right, a rate or an approval” — and start typing.
As you type, Nexi searches every guide and offers the sections that may already answer it. Tap one and read it; most questions end there.

If nothing fits, send it. The question is filed with the screen you were on, and Eyal, Dr Amy or IT answer it in place. The answer stays visible, so the next person who wonders the same thing finds it already answered.
Every module has view rights and edit rights. View lets you read, edit lets you change and approve. If a button is missing, that is why.
Eyal sets rights in Administration → Users.

sections.h: 📡 ערוצי תקשורת (v20.89) — לאיזה מייל/וואטסאפ/ויבר/לוח-שנה Nexi יתייחס
p: בכרטיס העריכה של כל משתמש (Administration → Users → ✏️ Edit) יש טאב שני נוסף על "🔑 הרשאות", בשם "📡 ערוצי תקשורת".
שם מגדירים, לכל משתמש בנפרד: כתובת מייל, Calendar ID, מספר WhatsApp ומספר Viber — וכל אחד בנפרד ניתן להדלקה/כיבוי. גם שעת קבלת סיכום יומי (ברירת מחדל 06:00, Asia/Manila).
זו שכבת ההגדרה בלבד — עדיין אין סוכן שקורא בפועל את הערוצים (זה יגיע בשלב הבא). מה שנקבע כאן הוא איפה הסוכן יידע לחפש כשהוא יופעל.

note.k: לא ניתן להדליק ערוץ בלי הסכמה
note.t: למעלה בטאב יש תיבת הסכמה — "אני מאשר/ת שסוכן ה-AI יקרא תכתובת עבודה בערוצים שיסומנו". בלי לסמן אותה, כל 4 הערוצים נשארים נעולים (disabled), וגם אם מישהו ינסה לעקוף מהקוד — הפונקציה עצמה בודקת את זה שוב ומסרבת. וגם: מחיקת הערך של ערוץ (למשל ניקוי שדה מספר הטלפון) מכבה אותו אוטומטית — לעולם אין ערוץ "דלוק" בלי יעד לשלוח אליו.

title: Item requests, transfers and asset deployments
who: Jomel · warehouse · anyone raising a request
summary: Raise a request, move an item from a place or a person to another, approve it, confirm the issue, have the employee sign for an asset, and post it to SOS.

p: Inventory → 📝 Requests. Two tabs: ➕ New Request to raise one, 📋 Requests for the queue. Three counters sit on top: Open, To issue, Completed.

note.t: Raising needs Inventory = view. Approving, confirming an issue and adding a location need Inventory = edit.

head: Type
Use it when
rows: Shipment
Goods leave the company — a delivery out.
Stock Issue
Something is consumed and will not come back — gloves, fertiliser, fuel.
Asset Deployment
A durable item is handed to a person — laptop, phone, drill. The person signs for it.
Stock Transfer
An item moves between two places or two people and stays company property.
Purchase Request
It has to be bought. Nothing moves until it is received.
Return / Replacement
Something is coming back.

p: Rule of thumb: will one named person hold it and be responsible for it? Then it is an Asset Deployment.
The item box reads the live SOS catalogue. Do not type the name by hand.
steps: Start typing a name, item number or SKU — two characters is enough.
The box lists items that START with what you typed, then under a divider the ones that CONTAIN it, including a match in the description.
Move with the arrow keys and press Enter, or tap the line. Esc closes it.
The item becomes a green chip. Wrong one? Press ↻ Change item.

note.k: THE SERIAL IS YOURS TO GET RIGHT
note.t: Item number, description and serial fill in from SOS. The serial belongs to the unit in your hands, not the catalogue line — if SOS has none, or the wrong one, type the serial off the equipment. It then follows the item onto the request, onto the page the employee signs, into the 201 file and into SOS.

sections.h: Where it comes FROM and where it GOES
p: A movement has two ends and either end can be a place, a person or a department.

Coming from an employee releases the item from that person’s 201 file when you confirm the issue. Going to an employee logs it into theirs. A handover like Edelyn → Mea is ONE request that writes both sides.

note.t: A transfer with no origin. From and To being the same place. From and To being the same person.

sections.h: Adding a location that is not in SOS
steps: Open the From or To location box.
Press ➕ add location (needs Inventory = edit).
Type it the way everyone should read it, e.g. “Office — Server Room”.
It is saved and available to everyone.

note.t: Follow the pattern already there. Two spellings of one room become two locations and the stock splits between them.

head: Situation
Approver
rows: Department Manager
Above ₱10,000
+ Division Head
Above ₱50,000
+ VP / COO
Purchase Request
+ Procurement, + Accounting
Anything going to an employee
+ HR (201 file)

p: Nexi shows the chain before you submit, then numbers the request IR<date>-<year>-<seq>.
Do this when the item physically leaves your hands. It is the step that moves the stock.
steps: Open the request → 📦 Confirm issued → post to SOS.
If you are issuing more than Nexi thinks is on the shelf it warns you. The shelf is the truth — if the box is really there, confirm; the override is written into the history.
If the auto-post fails the request sits at “Awaiting SOS ref”: post it in SOS, paste the reference, save.

p: After the issue an amber panel appears naming the person, the item, the asset tag and the serial.
steps: Hand the device to the employee.
They sign in the white box with a finger or the mouse.
Check the name, then press ✍ Sign & file to 201.
p2: That writes three things into their 201 file: a document holding the signature, an entry in the asset register as an outstanding item that HR ticks as returned later, and a memo line.

Signed on paper instead (v21.75)? Press 📤 Upload signed form in the same panel and pick a photo or PDF of the request with the employee’s signature (max 15 MB). It is filed straight to the employee’s 201 file as “HR review pending”, and everyone with HR Edit gets a review note in the Assistant inbox. HR opens 📄 Signed form and presses ✓ HR accept, or ↩ Return with what to correct — a corrected copy is uploaded with 📤 Replace signed form. A screen signature can also get its paper copy attached the same way.

note.t: The signature is the record. If they are not there, leave it unsigned — the panel is what tells everyone it is still waiting.

title: GPS Daily Report
summary: The per-vehicle daily trip log: stops, driving and stop time, distance, odometer and fuel.

p: Logistics → 📍 GPS Daily Report (also under Fleet). Pick the DATE and the VEHICLE at the top — everything below belongs to that one truck on that one day.

sections.h: Two or more trucks on the same day
p: A day holds a separate log for every truck, and the OUT ON <date> strip under the toolbar shows each one that already has a log — its stops, its driver, and a tick when the day has been finished. One tap switches to that truck.
To start the day for another truck, pick it from ➕ Another truck on this day beside the strip. Changing the date no longer forgets which truck you were on.

If you are on a copy older than v20.08, none of this worked: the VEHICLE box, the date box, the truck chips and ➕ Another truck all looked normal but never actually changed the truck or the day — the screen simply redrew the first vehicle. Hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) and check the title bar reads 20.08 or higher.

The Driver and Helper shown at the top are the ones set for THAT truck on THAT day. If they were never set for the day it says (from truck) or (usual) so you can see where the name came from; set them in 📋 Daily Summary below.

steps: Driver and Helper: pick from the lists. Pick the driver first — the helper who usually rides with that truck fills itself in.

ODO Out (start) and ODO In (end): type the reading off the truck’s DASHBOARD odometer — the actual dial or digital display in the cab, read by the driver at the start and end of the day. NOT the km the GPS tracker shows. Total KM works itself out.
Fill-up Liters and Cost per Liter: Total Gas Cost and KM / Liter work themselves out.
Dash Cam: WORKING, NOT WORKING or N/A.
General Note: anything the office should know.

note.k: THE TOTALS UPDATE AS YOU TYPE
note.t: From v19.90 the figures at the bottom recalculate while you type and the screen is never rebuilt under your fingers. If you are on an older copy the field kept losing the cursor — hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) and check the title bar reads 19.90 or higher.

p: Press ⚙ Auto-fill from tracker to pull the day’s stops from the GPS tracker, or ➕ Add Stop to log one by hand.
Driving time, stop time and distance are calculated from the times and the odometer — you do not type them.

sections.h: Typing the times and the KM
p: The time boxes are hours and minutes only — no seconds. The ⏱ button beside each one stamps the time right now, which is the fastest way to log a stop as it happens.
A time or a KM is saved when you leave the box, not on every character, and only the calculated cells redraw — the table no longer rebuilds under your fingers.

note.k: WHAT DOES THE KM COLUMN MEAN?
note.t: The small box under the KM heading says it. ODOMETER (the default) means you type the reading on the dash, and the distance of each leg is worked out from the row before it. KM THIS LEG means you type the kilometres of that leg itself and it is used as it stands. Getting this wrong is what produced a negative distance — a negative figure now shows in red.

p: Every field saves as you type — there is no Save button to press. The heading shows “✓ saved 09:41 · uploaded to the cloud” (amber while the upload is still on its way). Since v21.23 each day’s report carries the time of its last edit and the cloud keeps the newer copy per report, so another computer’s older copy can no longer replace what you entered. If a day ever looks emptier than you left it, tell IT the date and vehicle at once.

Since v21.23 it is figured on the GPS total distance (the odometer readings are typed by hand and were 20–26% short on 28 Sep); the odometer-basis figure is shown beside it. Under 3 km/L shows red, 3 to 5 amber, above 5 green. A red figure is worth a look before the report is filed — either the odometer is wrong or the truck has a problem.

sections.h: GPS vs Odometer is watched too
p: A new tile beside Total KM (ODO) and Total Distance (stops) shows the gap between them, in km and in %. A few percent is normal — GPS position drifts a little even while the truck is stopped or idling, and that adds up over a day.

Quiet (green) up to 15%. Amber 15-25% is worth a glance. Past 25% (red) is flagged with a note — that is too big to be ordinary GPS drift. The same figure prints on the sheet and exports to the Excel, so it travels with the report wherever it goes.

note.k: THE #1 CAUSE OF A BIG GAP: GPS KM TYPED AS ODOMETER
note.t: This exact thing happened — a driver was typing the number the GPS tracker showed into ODO Out/In, thinking that WAS the odometer, instead of reading the dashboard. That turns the "GPS vs Odometer" comparison into GPS-vs-GPS, and the two numbers can still disagree because the tracker’s own running total is worked out differently than these per-stop readings are. If a red flag shows up, the first thing to check is simply: did whoever filled this in actually read it off the dashboard? The field label now says so directly.

sections.h: The odometer is the truth, the GPS is a stand-in
p: GPS position drifts a little even parked (satellite noise, signal bouncing off buildings) — summed over a day that becomes several phantom km, which is why GPS almost always reads a bit HIGH against the real odometer. The odometer only counts actual wheel turns, so it never has this problem. Comparing the two, instead of trusting either one alone, is what catches a real error.

sections.h: 🌙 The same check runs every night, before anyone opens this screen (v20.90)
p: A separate worker (Night Auditor) now scans the last 3 days for every vehicle at 02:00 and flags anything past the same 15%/25% thresholds shown above — so a bad day is caught the next morning instead of waiting for someone to open GPS Daily Report and notice.

Findings show as a 🔔 banner at the top of the Production Dashboard. It only appears once someone (a primary admin) has set the worker's URL — before that, admins see a one-line "set worker URL" link there and everyone else sees nothing.
This first version only watches the GPS-vs-odometer gap — the same rule as this screen, nothing more. It is not yet checking attendance or payroll timing; that is a later phase.
Nothing to press — every field saves as you leave it, and the other machines see it. The office exports the Excel in the company’s own format from the same screen.

title: 201 files — documents, contracts and assets
summary: Every employee’s document library: scans, IDs, contracts, memos, and the assets they signed for.

p: HR → 📁 201 Files. The list shows every employee with a document status — CRITICAL when a key document is missing, WARNING when a lesser one is. Click a row to open the file.

head: What
Who
rows: 201 documents
Mea, Chen, Jinky
Contracts (upload and review)
Jinky only
Both, always
Eyal and Dr Amy

p: The bar at the top of the 201 screen says who may upload and what you personally may do. Eyal and Dr Amy change the two lists from the ⚙ button on that bar. If you are not on the list the upload is refused and you are told who to ask.

steps: Open the employee’s file.
Find the row for the document.
Press 📷 Upload and pick the scan or the photo (up to 15 MB).
It uploads to the cloud where it is available on every machine.

p: A signed asset deployment lands here by itself — a document holding the signature, and a row in the asset register marked Outstanding.
When the item comes back, press ✓ Returned on that row. That is what closes it.
The contract block holds the type, the dates, the probation end, the version and the notes, plus the signed scan. Only Jinky, Eyal and Dr Amy can put a contract in or read the signed scan.

title: Trip incentives and the tariff rate table
summary: What a driver and a helper are paid for the trips they make, and how the rate table behind it works.

p: Until v22.16 a day Syra had checked could come back as ⏳ pending logistics check on Jinky's screen, and an approved day could come back too. Each computer works the trips of a day out from the deliveries AND from things only that computer has - its own GPS trace of the truck, the roster it has loaded, the rate table it has received. When Jinky's computer worked out 1 trip where Syra's had worked out 2, it re-opened the day, and that re-opened copy reached every computer.

Now a checked or approved day changes only when its DELIVERIES change: a delivery row added (also one typed earlier on another computer that reaches this one late), deleted, marked failed, moved to another day or driver, or its driver, helper, area or trip # edited. What one computer sees differently never re-opens it: a drop that computer cannot place (a zone missing from its rate table, an area it could not match) stays on the day, also when its customer or status is edited - only deleting it, marking it failed or moving it to another date or driver takes it off; when another delivery of that day changes there, the drop keeps its trip, and a computer that can place it checks the day again. A drop with no trip # keeps the round the day was built with - correcting its area or helper does not move it - so every computer pays the same trips.

Rounds from the truck GPS win. If a computer without the GPS trace built a pending day (all its drops in the 1st trip), the computer that has the trace (Syra's) splits it into the GPS rounds once; the day stays pending and the audit log says 'rounds taken from the truck GPS'. The same when the GPS trace was still incomplete when the day was built (the truck on its 1st round): once the trace shows more rounds, the pending day is split again. Nothing splits or joins it back. A checked or approved day is never renumbered. A drop with no trip # added to a checked or approved day on a computer without the truck GPS (Jinky's) sends the day back for a check, because that computer cannot know which trip it was; Syra's computer then splits it by the GPS. Typing the trip # on the row avoids this.
A real change after the check still sends the day back. After a final approval it goes back for approval too, so an added trip is paid, and a locked run that already paid the day keeps it.

A day that is pending again says why in its Status column: '↺ pending again — was ✔ checked by logistics by Syra' (or 'was ✅ approved by Jinky'), then the reason, e.g. 'why: deliveries changed after the logistics check (1 delivery row added, trips 1→2 …) by Syra'. If the reason reads 'deliveries changed (trips 2→1 …) by Jinky' with no row added or edited, it was the old v22.16 problem: Syra did check it.

Days v22.16 re-opened that way get the check back by themselves (again if a computer still on the old version re-opens them), when the deliveries show nothing was changed and the trips Syra checked are known (the day already holds them again, or the computer has the truck GPS); the row then says '↺ check restored by Nexi'. Nothing is ever approved by itself. A day Nexi cannot prove stays pending: ask Syra how many TRIPS the truck made that day, not only the amounts (a 2nd trip counted as the 1st pays ₱0), then ✔ Check or approve anyway.
To pick a drop as the 1st trip, choose 1st trip on its row. It is stored now, so the GPS can no longer move it back to a later round.

note.t: Approve the days, then press 🔄 Recalculate on the weekly run (or open Labor Payroll for that week) and check the 🚚 Trips column before exporting the Excel. A run is a frozen snapshot until then. Every computer must be on v22.18 or later (title bar; Cmd+Shift+R / Ctrl+Shift+R) - an older one still re-opens days. A v22.16 screen left open shows a red 'OLD Nexi' bar, stops uploading and loads v22.18 by itself after 3 idle minutes.

sections.h: The amount you type is the amount paid — the ×2 box is gone (v20.99)
p: Until v20.98 a row could be ticked ×2, which silently doubled the additional rate typed in it. Clark City had 500 / 200 typed AND ×2 ticked, so every Clark trip after the 1st paid ₱1,000 / ₱400 instead of ₱500 / ₱200 — a whole week of corrections. The ×2 box no longer exists: Driver additional ₱ and Helper additional ₱ are exactly what each trip after the 1st pays, in every screen and in payroll. Clark City stays 500 / 200 and pays 500 / 200.
Every row shows in orange, under its name, what a trip after the 1st pays — it is always the number typed. Check it before you approve.
"Earlier run — not a delivery" legs pay ₱0 by design and are no longer counted in the red "trips paid ₱0" banner.

An APPROVED trip day keeps the amount it was approved at, so fixing the table alone does not change days already approved. Press APPROVE on the table and it lists every approved day priced with the old rates (old → new amount) and offers to RE-PRICE them. Say OK, then regenerate the payroll run. The driver and the helper are checked SEPARATELY. A day stays at its old amount only for the person an APPROVED weekly run has already paid it to: a run whose lines hold that person, matched on the day's pay date. A run saved without lines counts as holding everyone. The other person on the same day is still re-priced. An approved OFFICE cut-off never locks a trip day, because drivers and helpers are paid on the weekly run. Days that stay at the old amount are listed, so the difference can be recovered by memo. Until every approved day matches, an orange '⚠ N approved day(s) priced at an OLD rate — re-price' button stays on the Rate tab. It also says how many of those days are inside an approved run; those days are listed only.

APPROVE lists every changed area with what it ACTUALLY pays per extra trip, old → new. It also lists every change to a 1st-trip rate or a ⭐ Other-trip tick. It asks a second time (BIG JUMP) when a rate at least doubles, reaches ₱1,000 or more, or goes from ₱0 to any amount. Example: ALABANG driver 1st trip ₱0 → ₱1,700. A ⭐ Other-trip row is a flat rate.

Days approved while the old ×2 rule was in force still carry the doubled amount until they are re-priced: after this update the Rate table shows the orange "⚠ N approved day(s) priced at an OLD rate — re-price" button once — press it, say OK, then 🔄 Recalculate the weekly run. Days inside an approved (paid) run are listed, not changed.

note.t: Approve the table, then REGENERATE every payroll run holding those dates — a run is a frozen snapshot. If the run was already paid, the difference must be recovered separately.

p: The FIRST trip of the day is usually inside the salary. It is the SECOND trip onward that pays the additional amount, and some areas pay it twice.
A night trip to an area marked 🌙 counts as the third trip of the day, so it pays the additional rate even when it is the only trip that night.

A delivery day inside a week whose payroll run is already APPROVED is carried into the next open week when it is final-approved. It keeps its own date, and the list shows '→ paid <date>'. If the locked run already paid the day and trips were added later, the Deliveries link sends it back for approval. Approving it again keeps it with the run that paid it, so it is not paid twice, and the confirm names the part that run did NOT pay, e.g. driver ₱200. Add that as a one-time payment. A carried day that comes back after the week it was carried into has also been locked is checked the same way and carried on again if that week did not pay it.

On the Trip log, an approved day shows the amount it was approved at, which is what payroll pays. When today's approved table would give a different figure, 'table now ₱X' appears under it. That frozen amount only applies when the day is the person's ONLY approved record on that date in the same pay week (a day carried to a later week is counted in that week). Pending or rejected records do not count. It is paid even if the live rate table is empty. If the driver (or, separately, the helper) has two approved records on one date, payroll joins them and prices the joined day from the live table. The row then shows that live figure, with no 'table now'. The 🩺 Trip doctor says the same.
Each area has a driver and a helper amount for the first trip, and a driver and a helper amount for every additional trip. The additional one is the one that pays.
There are two copies: a DRAFT you edit and a LIVE one that pays. Nothing you type changes anyone’s pay until it is approved.

note.t: Jinky, Eyal and Dr Amy. Everyone else sees the table and who to ask.

sections.h: ⭐ Other trips — EVIA, Housing, RV, employee drop-offs
p: Not every run is a delivery. Evia, Housing, RV and the employee drop-offs are OTHER TRIPS — that is the category for every run that is not a delivery, and it is where an employee drop-off belongs. The rule that the first trip of the day is inside the salary does not apply to them: an Other trip pays its FLAT amount every time it happens, whether it is the first run of the day or the fifth, and it is never doubled.

If a rate you approved shows an older figure again (Clark back at ₱1,000 / ₱400 on 30 Sep 2026), a computer that had not opened Nexi for weeks pushed its stale table over yours — fixed in v21.25 so only a person's Save or APPROVE can outrank the cloud copy. Retype the rate in the draft, APPROVE, then press re-price on the approved days the banner names.

If a red banner appears at the top of the Rate Table saying trips paid ₱0, press 🔧 Tick ⭐ and APPROVE now — it ticks the rows and approves the table in one press. Then regenerate the payroll run that holds those dates: a run is a frozen snapshot and will not change on its own.

They are in the rate table at ₱100 for the driver, ticked ⭐ Other trip. The helper amount is ₱0, and that is settled — Eyal, 16 Sep 2026: no helper is needed on the Evia run. If a future Other trip does carry a helper, type that helper amount on its own row.

note.k: TICK ⭐ AND THE SYSTEM DOES THE REST
note.t: Any row can be marked ⭐ Other trip. Once it is, the amount you type is paid per trip with no first-trip rule, so a new drop-off point never needs its own arrangement. Like every rate change, it pays nothing until the table is approved.

sections.h: If the trip box still shows only 1st to 4th (v20.77)
p: The area and trip boxes on a delivery row were only redrawn when something about that row changed. They are built from the tariff rate table, but the table was not part of what they watched — so a zone you added, or a zone you ticked ⭐ Other trip, did not appear on a row already on the screen until you reloaded the page. If you asked for the ⭐ option and did not see it on a version that has it, this was why.
From v20.77 the boxes watch the rate table too. Change it and the rows redraw on the next tick, no reload.
One thing still needs a reload: moving to a new version of Nexi. Hard refresh with Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac) and check the version in the title bar.

note.t: The title bar shows the version. If it does not say v20.77 or later, hard refresh before judging whether something is missing.

sections.h: ➕ Adding a zone from the delivery row (v20.76)
p: The areas in the drop box on a delivery row are the zones of the tariff rate table. To add one, open that box and pick ➕ Add a new zone… at the bottom. Nexi takes you to the rate table, opens its add box and types the delivery’s destination in for you. Name it, set the driver and helper rate, choose 🚚 Delivery or ⭐ Other trip, and add it.

It lands in the DRAFT table. From v20.74 it is in the drop box straight away, marked ⏳ not approved yet, so tagging can carry on. It pays once Logistics presses ✅ APPROVE on the rate table and the week is regenerated.
Picking ➕ Add a new zone changes nothing on the delivery row — it is only the way in. Editing the rate table stays with Eyal, Dr Amy, Jinky and admins; anyone else is told so.

note.t: See a destination with no zone → ➕ add the zone → tag the drop → approve the table → the run pays. None of it needs leaving the work.

sections.h: 🚚 Picking the run by name in the trip box (v20.75)
p: The trip box on a delivery row no longer offers only 1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th. Every zone ticked ⭐ Other trip in the tariff rate table is an entry of its own in that same box — ⭐ EVIA, ⭐ HOUSING, ⭐ RV, and anything Jinky adds later. Syra picks the run by name and Nexi tags it as its own run and sets the area in one action, so the tag and the area can never disagree.
A zone Jinky has only added to the DRAFT shows there too, marked ⏳ not approved yet, and says so when picked. It pays once Logistics approves the rate table and the run for that week is regenerated.

The numbered part of the list now grows to whatever the row actually holds. Before, a day the truck GPS split into five rounds showed “1st trip” ticked on the fifth one, because the list stopped at four — and the next change on that row wrote 1st over the 5, moving what the run paid.

note.t: Jinky adds the zone and its rate → Syra sees it in the trip box and picks it on the delivery row → the day prices it flat from the approved table → it reaches the driver and helper on the weekly payroll. Regenerate the week after tagging.

sections.h: 🔗 A zone you add is in the drop box at once (v20.74)
p: Add a zone in the tariff rate table and it appears in the area drop box on the delivery row immediately, marked ⏳ not approved yet. You no longer have to approve the table before Syra can tag deliveries to it. Nexi will also auto-match it from the destination like any other zone.

It pays nothing until the table is approved. Tagging a ⏳ zone says so on the spot, the “why is a trip not in payroll” button names it, and the moment Logistics presses ✅ APPROVE on the rate table every day already tagged to that zone prices itself on the next regeneration.

A ⏳ zone can never take a run away from an approved one. If a round has drops in both, the approved zone prices the round — before this version an unapproved zone with a higher rate could take the round and pay ₱0.

note.t: DRAFT is what Jinky is editing; APPROVED is what pays. The drop box shows both so work is never blocked; payroll reads only the approved one, so money never moves by accident.

sections.h: ⭐ Tagging an EVIA / Housing / RV run on the delivery row (v20.73)
p: The trip box on a delivery row used to offer 1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th trip only. That number is the run’s POSITION in the day, and every drop carrying the same number belongs to the same run. So tagging an EVIA drop “2nd trip” on a day that also had a real 2nd delivery round put both in the same run — and a run pays one area, the dearer of the two. One of the two payments disappeared without a word.

The box now has ⭐ Other trip. Tag an EVIA, Housing or RV run with it. That drop steps out of the numbered sequence: it cannot take a delivery’s place and a delivery cannot take its place. The row then reads “⭐ other trip” instead of “trip 2 of 2”.

The money comes from the rate table exactly as before. An area ticked ⭐ Other trip there pays its flat rate every time it happens. If you tag a drop ⭐ whose area is NOT ticked ⭐ in the rate table, Nexi says so at once and it pays that area’s additional-trip rate instead.
Two drops of the same other run: give them both the ⭐ tag and they count as one run, the same way two drops of one delivery round share a number.

note.t: Nothing already logged changes on its own — no row carried this tag before. Re-tag the EVIA rows of an open week, then regenerate the payroll run for that week.

sections.h: Adding, changing and removing rows — and where it goes
p: Jinky, Eyal and Dr Amy can add a row (➕ Add area), rename it, change either amount, tick or untick ⭐ Other trip, and delete a row (🗑) — all of it in the DRAFT, at any time, with no one else needed.

Nothing has to be wired up afterwards. The moment the table is APPROVED, the new row appears in the area drop box on the trip log, the day rows price themselves from it, and the weekly payroll picks the amount up on the next run. A payroll run already generated is a frozen snapshot — regenerate it to pick up a rate you changed after it was made.

note.k: THE ONE STEP THAT IS NOT AUTOMATIC
note.t: ✅ APPROVE. Until the draft is approved, payroll keeps paying the old approved table — the screen says so in orange.

steps: Press ➕ Add area.
Choose 🚚 Delivery or ⭐ Special / non-delivery — the box relabels itself to match.
Type the area name.
For a delivery, type the driver and helper ADDITIONAL amount — that is the one that pays. For a special run, type the FLAT amount per trip.
For a delivery only: tick 🌙 if a night trip there counts as the third trip. The additional amount you type is exactly what each extra trip pays — there is no ×2 box any more.
Save, then approve the table.

note.t: An area with no amount is why a trip shows ⚠ ₱0 on the log. The row is not broken — it has no rate yet. Set the amount and approve.

p: A payroll run is a frozen snapshot. If the run for that week is already generated, reopen and regenerate it, or the new rate will not be in the pay.

title: CCTV — the daily check
summary: The daily camera check, the camera list, the NVRs and the live wall.

p: IT → 📹 CCTV. A row of buttons at the top switches between ✅ Daily check, 📷 Cameras, 📦 NVRs and 🎥 Live wall. Nexi remembers which one you used last.
One row per camera. Mark each one working or not working, and write what is wrong. That is the record that proves the cameras were looked at.

Edit the name, the location or the IP address in place, or add a camera.
It appears in the daily check from then on.

sections.h: If the live wall will not load
p: The wall needs the cameras to be reachable from that machine. When it cannot load it says so — the daily check and the camera list still work, so the check is never blocked by the wall.

p: Administration → 📦 SOS Inventory Sync shows whether it is connected and which account it is on. Nexi pulls the items, the locations, the lots and the shipments every five minutes, and the stock list you see IS the SOS catalogue.

Confirming an issue posts the movement to SOS — an issue, a transfer, a purchase order, a shipment or a receipt depending on the request type. The item number, the serial and the asset tag go with it.
