p: An issue that has left the store but is not yet acknowledged by SOS is already subtracted on screen, so the shelf and the screen agree while SOS catches up. It cannot be counted twice.

title: Attendance and the biometric
summary: How a scan becomes a day’s attendance, and what happens when there is no scan.

p: The clock sends its report by e-mail → the bridge reads the inbox every 15 minutes → Nexi pulls it every 3 minutes and fills the attendance. The first scan of the day is the time in, the last is the time out. One scan alone before noon is a time in with no out; one scan alone from noon on is the time out with no in, and that day is filed as late, measured from 07:00 to the scan, until Eyal or Dr Amy decide it or Reconcile sets the real arrival time. A manual entry always wins over a scan.

sections.h: No record is not the same for everybody

head: Who
No record means
rows: Labor (weekly payroll)
ABSENT — it is deducted
Office (semi-monthly)
PAID — only a manual absent deducts

p: From the Administration memo of 4 Oct 2026, effective 5 Oct: Admin 07:00–17:30 · Production & Packaging 07:00–17:30 · Maintenance 07:00–17:30 · Drivers & Helpers 05:00–16:00 · driver Antonio Garcia 06:00–17:00 · Contractors and Construction crews 08:00–17:00 (Edwin Suitado works admin hours). Nexi reads the person's department and name and applies the matching start and end everywhere a late or an undertime is decided — the attendance day, the biometric sync, timecard imports, the Late queue and payroll. A driver scanning at 05:10 is 10 minutes late; a contractor at 07:50 is on time. If one person has an agreed different schedule, type it on the HR card as schedStart / schedEnd and it beats the table.

A late after the person's official start (07:00 for most; see Official work schedules) is held for Eyal or Dr Amy to decide. Since v21.38 (Dr Amy's memo of 2 Oct 2026) the WHOLE DAY is withheld until they decide: DEDUCT pays the day minus the late minutes, EXCUSE pays it whole, NOT PAID keeps it withheld. A decision made after the run was locked is paid in the next cut-off by the locked-run carry. If the time-in is corrected after a DEDUCT was signed, the row returns to HR ▸ ⏰ Late approvals as ⚠ RE-DECIDE. Until they decide again, payroll takes the smaller of the signed and the current minutes. Only Late approvals changes a decision; Reconcile never does.

sections.h: Fixing a day by hand — what Nexi never overwrites
p: Uploading an NGTeco Timecard Report never overwrites a day a person already decided. That covers a day edited in Attendance, a Reconcile 'sent home', a ½ half day, a Missing IN/OUT fix and a leave. The message counts these as 'person-decided mark(s) preserved'. A report row with both Clock In and Clock Out blank is not saved as present; the normal rule decides that day: labour = absent if nobody marked it, office = paid.

On a day Reconcile marked '½ Half day', the Attendance day editor now shows a '½ Half day' tick box. Untick it, or set Time Out to 17:00 or later (which unticks it), then Save to pay the full day. A real OUT scan at 17:00 or later clears the half day automatically.

Correcting a day that has already been paid. The Attendance day editor and the Attendance Matrix now ask before you change a day inside an APPROVED run. Reconcile fixes and timecard imports show a warning. The paid run does not change. Open that run in Payroll: a ⚠ 'Attendance changed after this run was approved' banner lists each person with paid days → current days and the difference × that run's own daily rate. Press ➕ Carry to add the unpaid part to the next open cut-off as a one-time 'prior-period adjustment'. This happens once, and the line then shows as carried. The next draft run also names earlier runs that still have unpaid changes. An overpayment (for example an absent entered after the lock) is only listed and is never deducted automatically. Only runs approved from this update onward are checked.
Press a card — Present, Absent, Late, Authorized or Pending — and the list below shows only those people; press it again to clear. The card that is on has an amber frame.

A day counts as Late when it carries late minutes or a clock-in after 07:00, whatever word the record holds — the Late card, the Late filter, the badge on the person and the Lates & early-outs banner under the cards always agree. Absent, Authorized and Pending stay exactly as marked.

Pending explains itself in one line under the cards: how many are not on the biometric clock at all (management — counted attended by default), how many have no scan yet on a day still running, and how many have no record on a day that is over. If this machine’s storage is full it says so there too, because a scan that arrives while storage is full cannot be saved and will not appear.

note.t: On a day that is still running, a person with no scan yet is pending, not absent. From the next day, weekly labour with no record counts as absent; office staff with no record are still paid.

p: When one clock ID scans two or more times in the morning (before 11:00) or two or more times in the evening (from 15:00), at least 10 minutes apart, or five or more times in one day, Nexi treats it as a deviation. It can mean two people are using one ID, or somebody scanned for a colleague.
In the Attendance Matrix the day gets a red dashed frame and ⚠ CHECK, and a red banner above the grid counts what is waiting. Press ⚠ Review deviations to see the scans and what attendance recorded.

Accounting (Jinky) reviews first. ✅ Approve when it is fine. ⚠ Send to admin when there is an issue: the day turns orange ⚠ ADMIN and only an admin can then ✅ Approve or ⛔ Not accept it. Every step needs a short note and keeps the name and time. After the decision the cell shows ⚠✓ OK or ⚠ ✗.
To change the day itself (for example mark it absent), press ✏ Correct the day: the matrix opens on that month and person; click the day as usual. The change is logged and the review panel shows it.

Each new deviation is e-mailed once, in one message, to accounting@abapardes.com.ph and it@abapardes.com.ph, from the machine that pulls the biometric clock. If the send fails, the panel says so and Nexi tries again.

note.t: Approving or rejecting records that the day was checked. It does not edit the attendance record or the payroll. If the day itself is wrong, correct it in the matrix as usual.

p: HR & People ▸ 📅 Attendance Matrix in the sidebar, or type “matrix” into Search anything (Cmd/Ctrl+K). The same grid is also behind the 📅 button on ⏰ Attendance and on the IT attendance-store panel — one grid, three doors.

It shows every employee against every day of the range: the real clock hours, L and the late minutes, and on a late day a badge saying whether it is ⏳ waiting for Eyal or Dr Amy, ✓ excused, or ➖ deducted.

An office Saturday or Sunday that was scanned stays green and carries its own badge. ⏳ unsigned means it waits for the Accountant and then Eyal or Dr Amy to sign it in HR ▸ Weekend Approvals; ✓ signed 130% means they have; ✗ refused means they said no. Management and a fixed-fee Consultant, Contractor or Advisor show 'fixed pay': the scan is recorded but never paid. 'Contractual' is not a fixed fee, so those staff get the badge like everybody else. A labour Saturday with a clock scan (fingerprint or timecard) shows as a worked day, exactly as payroll pays it, never as 'Sat rest'. The ✓ totals count attendance, not paid days.

note.t: A late day keeps its green background. Red ✗ means there is no record for that day at all — hover it to see whether the scan is missing or somebody marked the day absent by hand.

title: Fixed Assets — QB Reconciliation
summary: The fixed-asset register (APTI’s MTC audit), registering a single new asset, and importing a whole lapsing / depreciation schedule at once.

p: Accounting → 🏗 Fixed Assets. It tracks every asset against the MTC audit and QuickBooks — not-in-QB, wrong account, write-offs, life corrections and open questions — until the books match.

Use ➕ New Asset for a single purchase: description, price, quantity, purchase date, useful life and department/category. Save and Nexi assigns the QB account number and writes the acquisition and monthly-depreciation journal entries for you to post.

sections.h: Importing a whole lapsing schedule at once
p: At the top of the ➕ New Asset tab, ⬆ Choose Excel file… reads a standard lapsing/depreciation schedule — Mother account · Category · Department · Equipment · Quantity · Estimated years · Acquisition date · Recorded in QuickBooks · Vendor · Cost — and registers every row in one action, through the exact same pipeline as a single hand-typed asset.

It finds the header row by its column names, so a title banner above the table (e.g. “LAPSING YEAR 2026”) does not break the import. A row with no description or no cost is skipped and counted, never silently dropped.

note.t: Every imported asset lands in the same “new asset(s), waiting to be created in QB” list as before — review the assigned account numbers, then create the accounts and post the journal entries in QuickBooks exactly as instructed on each row.

sections.h: What Nexi tells you to open and post for every NEW asset (v20.98)
p: Each new asset (typed in or imported) shows four blocks, on the ➕ New Asset tab, the 🔁 QB Recon tab and the 📒 Dep. JE tab alike:

① Accounts to open, in order: the mother account (the category) if QuickBooks does not have it yet, the sub-account if any, then the asset itself N (it shows the NET), N-1 “Original cost” and N-2 “Accumulated depreciation”. Each is checked against the live QuickBooks chart: ✓ exists, OPEN IT, or check (no live copy). The P&L depreciation account is taken from the live chart when QuickBooks has one.

② JE 1 — the purchase. If the lapsing file says where it was booked (e.g. 1013-001-001 ADVANCES or 1016-300-003 INVENTORY), the entry RECLASSIFIES it from there: DR N-1 original cost / CR that account. If it was never booked, it credits the payment source instead.

③ JE 2 — catch-up depreciation from the month after purchase to the last month-end. Months of earlier years go to Retained earnings (the accountant confirms); this year’s go to Depreciation expense. It assumes nothing was posted yet — if some months were, post only the difference.

④ The RECURRING monthly JE to create once in QuickBooks (Make recurring · monthly): DR Depreciation expense / CR N-2, the monthly amount, the first month, how many times it runs and the final month. The final month carries the small rounding difference so the total equals the cost to the centavo.

An imported asset is numbered under the MOTHER ACCOUNT its lapsing row names (e.g. 1025-003-002 Furniture & Fixtures - Office Machine and Equipment), not a default. Moving it to another department or category on purpose renumbers it.
The Excel export has the same package for every new asset on the sheet “08 New-asset JEs”.

title: CEA — Building & Structures (building permits)
who: Edelyn · CEA · Jinky · Eyal · Dr Amy
summary: One workspace for the Muntinlupa building permits: PRJ12 production / factory and the water-tank roof. It covers scope, site, design, filing, fees, the permit and whether work can start, inspections, completion and occupancy.

p: 🏛 CEA ▸ 🏗 Building & Structures. The top list picks a case, or shows the portfolio of all cases. Groundwater stays in 💧 Water / Deep Well with its 19 steps and gates G0–G13.
steps: First time: press 🏗 Create PRJ12 + water-tank roof cases (or use Case ▾ ▸ New …). Each case gets a BLD-year-number id, and Edelyn is the owner.
Open a case. The left list (or the screen menu on a phone) has 21 screens, BP01–BP21, grouped Definition, Design, Approvals, Applications, Delivery, Closeout, Operations and Administration.
Fill a screen and press 💾 Save, then Next ▸. Each field says when it is needed: to create, to file, before work or before use. Unknown values stay blank; they are never guessed.

p: The right-hand panel answers it. The banner shows five gates: Definition, Design, Filing, Construction and Occupancy / use. Press Why? to open the gate review, which lists every missing item by screen.

Construction and use NEVER open without a VERIFIED government check: Email, Document or Portal, with a reference and an evidence file (Case ▾ ▸ 🏛 Record a government check). An internal sign-off by Eyal or Dr Amy, an upload, a receipt or a stamp photo does not verify.

Every required document from the Muntinlupa OBO checklists (rev. 18 Feb 2025; reconfirm at filing) has its own row. There are 30 for PRJ12, 36 for the tank roof, plus 9 closeout documents that are needed before occupancy.
Upload with ⏫ on the row, then set its state. "Verified for submission", "Filed snapshot" and "Agency approved" need the file first. "N/A — justified" asks why.

Fee states run ESTIMATED → ASSESSED → FOR PAYMENT → PAID → VERIFIED. PAID needs the OR number and the amount. VERIFIED also needs the OR file and who reconciled it. The same OR number on two rows is refused as a duplicate. An official assessment always replaces the estimate.

A building permit is not renewed every year. Nexi watches the two PD1096 §305 events instead: one year after the permit is issued to START work, and 120 days of suspension or abandonment. A task is created 60 days before either date.

The roof set has 12 A1 sheets, RF-01 to RF-12. Import the ORIGINAL PDF with ⏫ Import. Nexi checks its SHA-256 against the supplied original and says whether it matches; a different file is kept as a revision. RF-01 requires review, signature and seal by a PRC civil/structural engineer. The blank approval boxes on the drawing are not a signature.

Case ▾ ▸ 🤖 Ask Nexi — what is blocking this case? answers in plain words from the gate rules: which gate holds the case, the first items to do (click one to jump to its screen), and what does NOT count as evidence. It does not check drawings or calculations.

Case ▾ ▸ 🧠 AI review of a document reads a plan set (PDF) or an agency letter or photo (up to 20 MB) together with the case. Case ▾ ▸ 🧠 AI: what is blocking this case? reads the case alone. Both return what the AI sees, what is missing, quotes with page numbers, what it is unsure about, and proposed tasks.

The AI only suggests. A task is created only when you press ✅ Create this task, and only once. The AI cannot verify an approval, change a status or fee, or check engineering, signatures or seals. Instructions written inside an uploaded letter are ignored. If the AI is down, all manual work carries on.

Each screen keeps its actions under Actions ▾. Case ▾ creates cases, records a government check, requests internal sign-off or archives. Export ▾ and ⚙ Settings ▾ sit beside it. Anything the agency asks for extra goes in as an Agency request, and a blocking one keeps work closed until it is closed.

Every file you upload in Compliance is saved in the company Dropbox under /Nexi/CEA/<Company>/<Case>/<Category>/. Nexi keeps the reference and a SHA-256 fingerprint, not the file itself. Until the admin sets up ⚙ Settings ▾ ▸ 📦 File service, Nexi can keep only small files (up to 300 KB) and says so; it never claims an upload that failed.

title: CRM — Customer Care (accounts, visits, complaints)
summary: Accounts, interactions, visits, complaints and opportunities — moved from Compliance to CRM.

p: CRM & Sales ▸ 🤝 Customer Care. It used to be Compliance ▸ Customer Relations; it is the same screen with the same data, and every old link opens it here.
Accounts with their health, interactions, visits, complaints with their response time, and opportunities. Dormant accounts are listed so someone follows up.

title: Storage — automatic clean-up
summary: Each computer’s browser store is limited to about 10 MB. Since v21.16 every store that keeps uploaded files, scans and photos moves by itself into the device database, which holds gigabytes. Nothing is deleted and everything still syncs.

p: Uploaded files kept inside the browser: compliance documents (the in-browser copy used until Dropbox is set up), 201-file scans, contracts, SOP files, CRM, inventory and fleet files. Photos in calls, memos and checklists go to the cloud (R2) by the existing photo mover when the computer is signed in. One computer’s store is not another’s — Edelyn’s fills with what Edelyn uploads.

Within a few seconds of opening Nexi, and every 5 minutes after, those stores are moved into the device database (IndexedDB) and a 12-character marker is left in their place. The screens read them exactly as before; the cloud sync pushes and merges them exactly as before. The 📦 counter and the ⚡ storage panel show only what really sits in the browser store, so the number drops.

Before the device database has answered at start-up, a write onto one of these stores cannot overwrite it with a stale copy: an empty default is dropped, a real change (an upload made in the first seconds) is kept and merged into the store a moment later — a toast says so. If the device database does not answer at all, a warning says so; that session the files and attendance run from memory and the cloud copy, nothing on the computer is overwritten, and a browser restart brings the device database back.

Press ⚡ (bottom right) → Clean now, then reload once. If a computer stays above 9 MB after that, send IT the TOP list from the console (F12 → Console → the storage line) so the store that is filling it can be added to the list.
The archiver used to treat today’s daily report as an old backup and move it to cloud archives every few minutes; it now only archives a day older than 21 days.

sections.h: Speed and memory — what Nexi does by itself (v21.19)
p: After the Logistics team reported a delay on every dropdown click and a “page not responding” warning, the timer engine was rebuilt so it cannot happen again. Nothing to switch on: (1) background jobs that serve only one module’s screens — for example the R&D tools panel, over 150 timers that used to scan every box and button of the page twice a second on every screen — now sleep unless one of that module’s screens is open; (2) while you are clicking, typing or scrolling, the background work is held to a few milliseconds and any heavy job waits for the next quiet moment, so a dropdown opens at once; (3) a job that keeps taking too long is slowed down automatically; (4) uploads to the cloud send only what changed on this computer (a full copy every 30 minutes) with a 4-minute deadline, so the red “Sync error / timed out” badge is gone; (5) memory is released as you work: closed 3D previews and drawing boards drop their listeners, a map is removed before it is redrawn, photo caches are capped, deleted-record markers older than 180 days and old reminder marks are pruned, and a store that has not changed is not decompressed again on every read; (6) the storage meter measures every 10 seconds instead of every 2.5, with the real (compressed) sizes; (7) the “new version” check reads only the first kilobytes of the page instead of downloading all of it every 2 minutes; (8) the goodbye upload when a tab is closed sends only the keys changed on this computer, in small batches the browser accepts, and the list of changed keys survives a reload so a reload no longer triggers a full upload; (9) page-wide watchers that react to screen changes are batched five times a second instead of firing on every single change; (10) the daily backup skips file stores already kept in the device database and old daily reports, and starts a minute after opening when the computer is idle; (11) the growing operational logs (GPS reports, trip log, deliveries, fuel, planting, checklists, audit trails, field captures) now live in the device database like the file stores.
For IT: F12 → Console → window.__hnxGovStats() lists every background job with its average and worst time, whether it is screen-scoped, and how often it was skipped or deferred.

title: Tasks — my work, my team, repeating work, approvals
summary: Since v21.17 Nexi has one task record for the whole company. ✅ Tasks in the left rail: My Day (yours), Team (your department’s assigned and shared work, for department heads), Repeating (rules that create tasks 90 days ahead), Approvals (tasks waiting for your review) and the Tasks calendar. Every module calendar also shows task deadlines (⏰) and work blocks (🟩) and has a ✅ New task button.

p: Two minutes after Nexi opens on any computer it measures that computer: CPU and memory, how long loading took, how much of the time the screen was frozen, the heaviest background jobs and how full browser storage is. Once a day per user it sends this as a 🩺 Speed report to Eyal, Dr Amy and the System Admin (Nexi inbox). If the screen was frozen more than 15% of the time, ⚡ Lite mode is switched on automatically on that computer. v21.96: every photo you attach anywhere in Nexi (production photos for analysis, calls, issues …) is resized to 1280 px before it is saved — about 150 KB instead of 3-5 MB — so photos never fill the browser again; photos already saved are shrunk once in the background. v22.13: photos no longer stay inside Nexi’s data at all — within minutes of being saved (maintenance tasks, daily reports, R&D, any screen) each photo is moved to the company cloud and only a short link stays, so the data every computer reads and syncs stays small. The photo still shows everywhere (it loads when you open it; you must be online and signed in to the cloud). 🩺 Nexi Health shows for each computer how many photos are still inside its data and, if one cannot be moved, why. v22.03: when the screen is blocked for more than 8 seconds, a red box appears naming the operation that was running, the ones before it and which stores fill this computer's browser — screenshot it for IT. v22.15: the automatic rescue snapshots now live in the computer’s device database instead of the small browser store, and every “is the browser full?” check knows that Safari on a Mac gives Nexi about half the room Chrome does — the “NOT SAVED” strip clears itself as soon as saving works again and never covers the buttons. Opening Labor Payroll no longer freezes the screen for seconds; Nexi’s automatic clean-ups no longer cut the audit log, seed studies or recurring history or delete your backups on a computer that is not full (they only run when the browser storage is really nearly full); the Nexi Brain’s moving graphics pause in ⚡ Lite mode and whenever they cannot be seen; storage numbers in the red box, 🩺 Nexi Health and the storage meter now show what is really stored in the browser. v22.14: the red box is small, sits at the bottom-left corner, never stops you clicking what is underneath it, has ✕ and closes by itself after 25 seconds; it no longer appears when Nexi was only waiting because its window was minimised or covered by another program, or the computer was asleep. v22.11: 🩺 Health Guardian — runs on every computer all the time. Every minute it measures freezes, memory, page size, browser storage and sync, and repairs by itself: cleans storage before it fills, switches ⚡ Lite on when a computer struggles, slows heavy background jobs during overload, and, when memory runs high, shows a notice with a Refresh now button (v22.12: it never refreshes by itself, so nothing typed is ever lost). v22.12: the after-login freezes are fixed at the source — call lists, sidebar counts, notifications, payroll for all staff, ✓ Bulk Present / Absent, ZKTime import, Reconcile Accept-All and the Recurring calendar no longer re-read whole stores for every item; the daily payroll draft waits until someone signs in. Admins see every computer in ⚙ TOOLS → 🩺 Nexi Health; a computer that stays red for 10 minutes sends an alert to the admin and Eyal inbox. v22.10: ⚡ Lite is now ON by default on every computer (animations off, background refreshers slower) — on an office PC the moving graphics alone blocked the screen about 11 seconds of every minute. Press ⚡ Lite in the top bar to switch the animations back on for a strong computer. Also v22.10: the login page is quiet — before anyone signs in, the hundreds of background screen decorators run only twice and then once every 30 seconds (cloud sync keeps its pace), so the login page no longer freezes. v22.09: the red stall box now also shows “🎯 BROWSER SAYS”, the exact function the browser saw running during the freeze. v22.08: the two background checks that re-read the maintenance and calls stores every 6-8 s (12 s and 6 s on office PCs) now only work when something actually changed. v22.07: the login page no longer freezes — the job that rebuilt the call buttons every half second waits until you are signed in. v22.06: the local Data Rescue snapshot is skipped when the browser store is already big (the cloud keeps 30 versions). v22.05: the red stall box also names the exact background job and the three slowest jobs. v22.04: the old blocking “Storage is full” pop-up is gone — a toast says the rescue is running instead. Also v22.03: 🚑 Storage rescue — when this computer's browser store passes 80% or a save fails for lack of space, Nexi frees space by itself (regenerable copies and old backups deleted, logs trimmed, big records compressed in the background) and sends a 🚑 line to the admin inbox; nothing that exists only on this computer is deleted. v22.02: compression of big records now runs in a separate background thread (Web Worker), never on the screen thread — the 3-6 second stalls on office PCs when the maintenance store (2 MB) was compacted or saved on a full browser store are gone. v22.01: the company-wide freeze is fixed — since v21.98 the device database kept a compressed copy of the calls store and decompressed 4 MB on every read, dozens of times a minute; it is now decoded once and kept ready. Nexi also no longer compresses big records before the login page appears, and background compression waits while you are typing or clicking. v22.00: if Nexi freezes (“Page Unresponsive”), the next start sends a 🧯 Freeze report to Eyal, Dr Amy and the admin inbox naming the exact operation that froze the computer; if the same operation froze it twice, that operation is skipped on the next start. Stores over 1 MB are merged from the cloud at most every 5 minutes. v21.99: the QuickBooks and SOS caches (11.7 MB on the admin computer) are no longer copied through the cloud — each computer reads them straight from QuickBooks/SOS when Accounting or Inventory is opened — so a cloud sync is now a small download. v21.98: saving no longer compresses big records every time (that cost seconds on slow PCs while Nexi opened) — records are compressed only when the browser is full or in the background when idle; calls (with their photos) now live in the device database. v21.97: when Nexi opens, the cloud data is merged in small slices so the login screen never freezes (“Page Unresponsive”), and records that did not change in the cloud are skipped. Also: syncing no longer downloads the whole company store (~15 MB) after every edit — only the records you changed are checked with the cloud before upload, and on a slow internet line the background full sync runs less often (up to every 5 minutes). Old in-browser backup copies are no longer written, so a full browser store stops filling up again. Also in v21.95: the menu-position guard no longer runs three full passes on every screen change (it was the single heaviest job on slow PCs, e.g. Mea's) — it now runs at most once every quarter second.

sections.h: 🚦 Release control, rollback and safe mode (v22.16)
p: A new Nexi version no longer reaches everybody at once. It goes first to one or two 🚦 trial computers (⚙ TOOLS → 🚦 Release control → “Make this a trial computer”), which open the trial copy of Nexi with the same data. Everyone else stays on the stable version until the trial computers have stayed green in 🩺 Nexi Health for a few hours; then IT makes the trial the new stable version.

If a version blocks work, the owner presses ⏪ “Roll everyone back to the previous version” in 🚦 Release control: within about a minute every computer shows a purple bar and moves to the previous version (by itself after one minute without typing). “Cancel rollback” brings everyone back. If Nexi will not open at all, use Netlify → Deploys → the last good deploy → Publish deploy.

Safe mode: when Nexi is slow or stuck on one computer, click “Nexi slow or stuck? Start in safe mode” under the sign-in box (or add ?safe=1 to the address). Nexi then runs only what it needs to work — sign-in, your data, cloud sync — with background helpers, decorations and clean-ups off and Lite mode on. A green 🛟 SAFE MODE badge shows it; click “leave” to return to normal.

A red CRITICAL card appears once when a new urgent call or maintenance task is created; 🧹 Clear all closes the whole stack. Before v21.88 Nexi remembered only the last 500 alerts it had shown, so once there were more than 500 calls and tasks the oldest came back as new critical cards. Now an alert is remembered for as long as its call or task exists, so a cleared card does not return.

Since v21.89: a call or task older than 48 hours never pops up as a new alert. A CRITICAL (urgent) call can be closed only by a supervisor (supervisor / manager roles, department heads, Jinky, Dr Amy, Eyal, admins), and only after writing what was done (at least 15 characters); everyone else reports with 💬 Update. Bulk close in My Calls needs a note and leaves critical calls open for non-supervisors.

🔎 Review old critical (N) appears above the alert cards when critical calls have been open more than 7 days: tick the ones no longer present or already fixed, write what was checked / done, and close them as Finalized — the note is saved on every call.

Since v21.90 no more than 3 alert cards are on screen at once; the rest are counted on one “+N more alerts” card that opens My Calls. A computer still running an old version shows the red “Load the new version” bar and, when nobody has touched it for 3 minutes and nothing is being typed, loads the new version by itself.

Since v22.20 alerts make NO sound (owner rule, 9 Oct 2026: “critical — no noise, just blink”): no beep for criticals or warnings, the computer’s pop-up notifications are silent, and Nexi no longer reads new criticals aloud. The red cards still appear and the alert bell still blinks. In 🔔 Notifications the “Play sound” switch is off and greyed.

Nexi Assistant → 👁 Team follow-up is for Eyal, Dr Amy and the System Admin only; everyone else sees a lock. With “All users” selected it lists every active user who has tasks: open, overdue, due today, done in the last 7 days, routines on track and behind, today’s duty score and when they last touched a task. Click a row or pick a name in the ▾ dropdown to open that person.

One person shows: Overdue · Today · Next 7 days (each task with due time, module, status and proof count) · 🔁 Routines — every repeating task with next due date, last done date, misses in the last 30 days and on track / behind · 🧭 Role duties today with their D / L / X codes (Rea, Mea, Edelyn, Joshane, Syra) · Waiting review / blocked · Done in the last 7 days. Click any row to open the task.

Tasks → 👥 People & Work is the live picture of Rea, Mea, Edelyn, Joshane and Syra. At the top each person has a score ring for today; click a person to open her work queue. “The day” shows one lane per person: every duty is a block at its deadline — grey while still in time, green D, yellow L, red X, purple NA? waiting approval — and a green line shows the time now in Manila. Click any block to open the duty and upload the proof.

Needs your decision lists every missed duty and every NA request of the last 7 days; managers approve or return an NA right there. The work queue has four tabs: Do now, Missed, Waiting NA and Done. The week calendar (v21.92) shows the selected person’s Monday to Sunday: every duty of each day at its time, with a coloured edge for its status (grey still in time, green D, yellow L, red X, purple NA?); click a duty to open it; ‹ › moves a week, future days show the planned duties; today is outlined and Saturday is marked off. Every duty is also a task, so it appears in the 📅 calendars too. The month strip colours each day green (≥95%), amber (85–94%) or red, with Saturdays hatched as off.

Jinky, Dr Amy, Eyal and the admin see all five people; each employee sees only her own lane, queue and month. It refreshes every minute and uses the same duties and scores as the 🧭 Duty board and the 17:45 fail report.

sections.h: 🧭 Duty board — Rea and Mea role files (v21.80)
p: Every duty in Rea’s (Accounting · AP · Inventory & SOS recon) and Mea’s (Admin & HR) role files appears on its day as a task that needs a proof to close: daily duties every workday, weekly on their weekday, monthly on their date. Since v21.83 the board also runs Edelyn Nicolas (Compliance, Importations, Immigration, Customer relations — from her JD Rev 0), Joshane (Purchasing, assets, bank and credit-card reconciliation) and Syra Mae Montesa (Logistics — from her own task list since v21.84: harvest report, harvest PO and product builds in SOS, supply requests, GPS and driver time in/out, megabox and crate IN/OUT and Friday counts, fuel, Lalamove, GCash, daily filing, truck permits); Joshane’s file is a draft until Eyal confirms it. Every duty is a task, so it also shows in the 📅 calendars. Nexi Assistant sends each person a 🌅 morning brief at 07:00 (today’s duties with times and proof, plus yesterday’s misses carried over) and Jinky, Dr Amy and Eyal a 🧭 team brief at 07:30. Workdays are Monday to Friday plus Sunday; Saturday is off, so Saturday duties from the files are on Friday, and a monthly date that falls on a Saturday moves to the Friday before — except the 1st, which moves to Sunday the 2nd so it stays in its month (v21.85).

Scoring: D = done with proof by the deadline (1 point) · L = done later the same day (½) · X = not done after the deadline, or done a later day (0) · NA = cancelled as not applicable (not counted). Green ≥95%, amber 85–94%, red below 85%.

30 minutes before a deadline the owner gets a reminder with the proof required; 15 minutes after a missed deadline a red “Missed” alert. Each duty opens with the exact steps from the role file and names its reviewer (Jinky, Dr Amy or Eyal, as in the file’s “Report to” column). A daily duty still missing 2 hours after its deadline is escalated to that reviewer; a weekly or monthly duty one working day late is escalated at 09:00. NA is only a request: the owner cancels the task with a reason, the board shows “NA?”, and it counts as not applicable only when a manager presses ✓ approve NA (↩ return reopens it). A day with no duties shows “No tasks due”, never 0% (v21.82). At 17:45 every workday Jinky, Dr Amy and Eyal get the NEXI FAIL REPORT in their Nexi inbox and by e-mail (company addresses, through nexi-notify), with a ready WhatsApp message; the board also has 📨 Send now and 💬 Share on WhatsApp.

Tasks → 🧭 Duty board: Rea and Mea each see their own day; Jinky, Dr Amy, Eyal and the admin see both, with today’s and the month-to-date score. Rea’s user card carries her mobile +63 917 820 9154 and reag@abapardes.com.ph (v21.81, only where blank). Mea’s Nexi user (meajean, Admin + HR, payroll amounts hidden) is created the first time an admin opens Nexi; the first password shows once on the admin’s Duty board and must be changed at first login.

sections.h: Creating a task — the three-step wizard (v21.47)
p: Every desk with a head is a tile — Accounting, Purchasing, Compliance, R&D, Administration, Safety and Meetings included (v21.48). Press ➕ New task — on the Tasks cockpit header, the floating ➕ button on any Tasks screen, or any Create task button. Every user has it. Step 1 What: a short title, what “done” looks like, the module tile it belongs to and the kind of work. Step 2 Who & when: the owner (you, unless you hand it to someone — a task given to a person in your team is mandatory for them), priority (Critical asks for the impact), Today / Tomorrow / Friday / Next week or a date, and who can see it. Step 3 How: tick done, evidence required or a reviewer, optional steps inside the task, and a preview. ✨ Create task shows the ✓ celebration; Open it goes straight to the task. Enter moves to the next step.
steps: ✅ Tasks
➕ New task
Title → Continue
Owner, priority, due, visibility → Continue
Rule, steps → ✨ Create task

p: Title, outcome (what “done” looks like), one owner, module, priority (Critical asks for the impact), type, start and due date. When a due date is moved the original stays on the card (“was due 12 Oct”). Subtasks go three levels deep; a REQUIRED subtask blocks the parent from being Done until it is done or waived by the reviewer or the department head.

Completion rule: Simple (the owner marks Done) · Evidence required (a note, a Nexi record or a file must be added first) · Reviewer approval (the owner submits, the reviewer approves or returns it with a note; nobody approves their own task).

Visibility on every task: 🔒 Personal (only you — never shown to anyone, only counted as “private” for your head) · Shared with my department head · Team (your department) · Selected users. A task your department head or an admin assigns to you, or one created by a repeating rule, is team-visible and cannot be made personal.

The department head is chosen by an admin in Administration ▸ Users ▸ Department heads (one per department). Heads see the Team screen: open work per person, blocked, overdue, due this week — and are reminded when someone’s task is 2 days late.

sections.h: Evidence files and the customer follow-up 3× a day (v21.74)
p: Evidence of done can now be a FILE: open the task ▸ Evidence ▸ 📤 File — a photo, PDF or scan (up to 25 MB each, several at once). Whatever you typed in Note becomes its caption. The file is kept in the Nexi cloud Files store and opens again with one click on 📄 in the task. Only the owner, whoever assigned the task, the department head or an admin can add evidence.

Customer tasks (CRM tasks, or tasks linked to a customer) are followed up three times a day: at 09:00, 13:00 and 17:00 Manila Nexi shows every user the customer tasks they own or that are shared with them which are late, due today or due in the next 2 days — one message per time, also kept in the Assistant inbox. Admins see all customer tasks that are not personal. If Nexi was closed, the last missed time is shown once when it opens. With the CRM brief script installed, the same list is e-mailed at 08:00, 12:00 and 16:00.

Tablo Group order start (6 Oct 2026): every row of the action plan is a required step of the task “Tablo Group — order start”, owned by Edelyn (she follows up also the steps Tablo must deliver), shared with Eyal and Dr Amy, each closed only with its evidence. The deadlines are in every calendar; the plan is on the Tablo lead in CRM ▸ Tasks.
steps: ✅ Tasks ▸ My Day
Open the task
Evidence ▸ type a note ▸ 📤 File
Pick the photo / PDF
✓ Done

sections.h: Calendar: deadline is not work time
p: ⏰ A deadline is the task’s due date, drawn by the calendar from the task. 🟩 A work block is time you reserve to do it (Schedule in the task, as many blocks as you like); moving or removing a block never changes the due date. Both appear in the module’s calendar and in the Tasks calendar; clicking one opens the task.

Reminders (in-app, when Nexi is open): the day before the due date, on the day, one day late → the owner; two days late → the department head; a task waiting for your review; a blocked task whose check-again date has come.

Tasks ▸ 🔁 Repeating ▸ New: daily / weekly (days) / monthly (day or last) / quarterly / yearly, start, optional end, due time. Working days only by default: a Sunday or a holiday from Payroll’s holiday list moves the task to the next working day — once, never a duplicate, also across computers. Nexi keeps the next 90 days generated. Change one occurrence on the task itself; change the rule “this and future from a date” or for all on the rule (past and edited occurrences are never touched).

steps: To do → ▶ Start → In progress.
🚧 Blocked needs a reason, who/what you wait for and a check-again date; it shows in orange on the Team screen.
📤 Submit for review (approval tasks) → Pending review → ✅ Approve = Done, or ↩ Return with a note.
✓ Done stamps who and when; ↺ Reopen keeps the previous completion in the history. ✖ Cancel needs a reason and is not Done.
🗑 Delete: only whoever created the task, or an admin; subtasks go with it; it does not come back from another computer.

p: Maintenance Task Board, IT Task Board, Compliance Tasks & Approvals, CEO follow-through and the Overview Task Tracker keep working as before; the Task Tracker also lists team-visible tasks from here. E-mail reminders and the daily agent e-mail for tasks come in the next phase.

title: Every module’s calendar — tasks and reminders
summary: Each module has its own 📅 Calendar at the end of its menu: tasks, reminders, meetings and deadlines, with who it is for and when Nexi reminds.

sections.h: Day · Week · Month · Year, in colour (v21.93)
p: Every module calendar and the main 📅 Calendar use one look. Choose 1 Day, Week, Month or Year at the top; ‹ › moves one period, Today jumps back. Each module has its own colour — the legend shows how many items each has; click a module in the legend to hide or show it. The filter shows All, Open, Late or Done, and 🔎 searches titles, notes and people. Above the calendar a strip counts the items, done, open and late in the period shown.

Drill down: in Year, click a month name to open that month or a day square to open that day (squares are coloured by how busy the day is); in Month, click the day number or “+N more” to open the day; in Week, click a day header. The breadcrumb (2026 › Oct › week of 10-12 › Tue 13) walks back up. Day shows every item as a large card with time, notes, person, module and late / done. Click any item to open it; in a module calendar, clicking an empty space on a day still adds a task or reminder on that date. Late items have a red outline, done items are faded.

At the end of each module’s menu (Production, HR, Maintenance, Irrigation, CRM, Compliance and the rest): 📅 Calendar. It shows only that module’s items. The main 📅 Calendar still shows everything together.

steps: Press ➕ Add task / reminder, or click a day on the grid.
Give it a title, the date and, if you want, a time.
Pick the type: Task, Reminder, Meeting or Deadline.
Assign it to a person, or leave it on nobody (then it reminds you).
Choose when Nexi reminds: on the day, 1 day, 3 days or a week before, or no reminder.
Save.

p: From the reminder day, the person it is for gets a 🔔 reminder in Nexi when they open it, once a day, until it is marked done. Late items show in red in the Upcoming list.
The assigned person, whoever added it, or an admin can press ✓ Mark done. Only whoever added it, or an admin, can change or delete it. Every change is logged.

title: Customers — three screens and what each is for
summary: 🤝 Customers, 🆕 Customer Master and 📁 Customer 360° Files / 📊 Customer Matrix each hold a different piece of the customer — which to open when.

p: The top of the screen is 🔗 QuickBooks Customers: the live customer list from ABA Pardes QuickBooks, with ↻ Refresh, search and a mode on each customer — 🆕 New (added in the last 30 days), ⚪ Not Active (inactive in QuickBooks) or 🔘 Uncategorized (active; the order cadence is not wired yet). A CRM supervisor can set a customer’s type and its price list from here; everyone else sees them read-only.

Below the line are the won leads — every lead whose stage reached Won, with its samples, meetings and days since the last activity. Click a row to open that lead’s record (overview, activities, 📎 Files).

note.k: THIS IS WHERE DAILY SELLING HAPPENS
note.t: Follow-ups, samples, meetings and quotes all hang off the lead record. If you need to know who we sell to and how to reach them, this is the screen.

p: The B2B onboarding record: company info, TIN, contacts by role, currency, credit terms (COD, 7 to 60 days, PDC, consignment) and a status that moves Pending → Under Review → Approved (or Rejected / Expired). Each customer gets a CUST-0001 style code; search by company, TIN or code.

Its document list is the accreditation file: Business / Mayor’s Permit, BIR 2303, SEC / DTI registration and a valid ID of the signatory (the critical four), plus audited FS, bank certificate, supplier agreement and NDA. Scans are uploaded on the record, versioned and dated, and stay with it.
Open it when a new customer is being taken on, when accounts asks about credit terms, or when a permit or ID has to be found.

sections.h: 📁 Customer 360° Files and 📊 Customer Matrix — is the file complete?
p: 📁 Customer 360° Files lists every won customer with a Doc Status (✓ Complete, or what is still missing), the document count and their quotes and orders. Click a customer for the checklist — signed contract, business permit, BIR 2303, TIN (the critical ones), then SEC / DTI, credit application, bank reference, 2307, price-list acknowledgement, delivery address, authorized persons, facility photo. Upload a scan, add a new version (old versions are kept), leave a note, or view what is on file.

📊 Customer Matrix is the same completeness read across the whole base: one row per issue, one column per industry, each cell the % of customers in that industry with the item resolved. Use it to see where the gaps are before a review, not to fix a single customer.

Open

title: Catalog & Pricing — products, segment prices and price lists
summary: The master product catalogue with a price per customer segment, and the custom price lists a supervisor attaches to a customer type or a single customer.

p: One row per product: photo, SKU, name, variety (Lettuce, Leaves, Kale, Plant, Solution), unit, the base price and a price for each segment. The base prices were seeded from the March 2026 price list; ✓ / ✕ marks whether the product is available.

The segment prices are the base price times a fixed multiplier: Online ×1.10, Hotels ×1.00, Restaurants ×1.00, Supermarkets ×0.90, Distributors ×0.85, Retail ×1.15. They recalculate when the base changes; ✏️ on a row lets you edit any single one.

Search by SKU or name, filter by variety or availability. + Add Product creates one, 📷 puts a photo on a product that has none, ⬆ Import updates products in bulk from a CSV and ⬇ CSV exports the table. 🖨 Print Master prints the whole catalogue.

A custom price list is a named set of products and prices built for one customer (or generated from a segment with 📑 Generate from Segment), with an optional Valid Until date. Each row shows the customer, segment, item count and total value; 📋 Open edits it, 🖨 prints or saves it as a PDF, 📧 emails it to the customer.

Above the table, 🏷️ Default price list per customer type sets which list each type (hotels, restaurants, supermarkets, online, distributors, retail) gets automatically. A customer inherits its type’s default unless a supervisor sets a per-customer override on the 🤝 Customers screen; with nothing set, the base segment prices apply.

note.k: ONLY A CRM SUPERVISOR CHANGES PRICING
note.t: Type defaults, a customer’s type and a customer’s price list can be changed only by an admin or supervisor login. Everyone else sees them read-only — that is deliberate, so a discount is a decision, not a slip. The rule on the opening price (₱395, never ₱329 first) is in the CRM & Sales guide.

title: Potential Customers — the prospect list before it is a lead
summary: A researched list of hotels, restaurants and chains to go after, kept apart from CRM Leads until someone decides to pursue one.

p: Prospects grouped by type — hotels by star rating, restaurants by cuisine, chains by branch count — across Metro Manila, Clark and nearby, each with area, city, business type, branches and a stage (new, contacted, sampling, negotiating, won, lost). The counters at the top show totals, hotels, restaurants, chains and won.

On an empty list, ⬇ Load researched leads (Manila + Clark) fills the starter batch; ↺ Reset to seed reloads it. ➕ More leads (Indian/JP/Vegan · Cebu/Davao) appends a second researched batch and skips names already in the list. These are starter leads — verify contact details before using them.

➕ Add Lead adds your own. Every cell in the table is editable in place; ✎ on a row opens the details drawer for contact person, phone, address, estimated monthly kg of greens, priority (High / Med / Low) and notes.

Search, the 🏨 Hotels / 🍽 Restaurants chips, the area and stage drop-downs narrow the table. 🗺 Map view plots the prospects on a map: there is no GPS on a prospect, so each is placed near its area or city, coloured by stage — click a marker for its details.
📤 Export CSV downloads the whole list (name, type, category, area, city, chain, branches, stage, contact, website, products, notes) for work outside Nexi.

sections.h: ➕ Lead — sending a prospect to the CRM
p: When a prospect is worth pursuing, press ➕ Lead on its row. It is added to 🎯 Leads as a new lead with source “CRM-AI potential” and a note saying where it came from, and the follow-up work (samples, meetings, quotes) happens there. The prospect row stays here; update its stage by hand as things move.

note.t: Nothing here is a customer or a lead until ➕ Lead is pressed. Keep the research in this screen and the selling in 🎯 Leads, so the pipeline only shows what someone is actually working.

title: CRM — Sales & Order Intelligence
who: Eyal · sales managers · everyone with CRM access
summary: Every QuickBooks customer: net sales by month and year, category, mother account and distinct items — one company at a time.

p: Every figure opens what is behind it. Click a month bar, the Net sales tile, a category amount, a customer’s month cell or total, a top item, or a row in the new View → By item table, and a panel lists the QuickBooks documents that make that figure: date, type (invoice, sales receipt, credit memo, refund), document number, customer, lines, quantity and net amount. Click a document to see its lines (item, description, quantity, unit price, discount, net); click a customer or an item inside the panel to narrow further; the search box filters by document number, customer or item; ⬇ CSV exports the lines shown. The panel closes with ✕ or a click outside it.
CRM & Sales ▸ 📈 Sales & Order Intelligence, next to Sales Analytics. Sales Analytics still shows quotes, orders and the pipeline; this screen shows what was actually billed in QuickBooks.

steps: View: Overview, Customers, Mother accounts, Classify customers or Data health.
Company: APAC or APTI. The two companies are never added together.
Year, Category and Measure (₱ net sales, quantity or distinct items).
Customer: type part of a name to narrow the list.
Tick “include customers with no sales” to see every customer in QuickBooks, with zeros.

p: Net sales = invoices and sales receipts, less credit memos and refund receipts, after discounts, excluding tax, in pesos, by transaction date. Payments and deposits are not sales. The line under the filters always says which company, which basis and how fresh the data is.
If a month could not be read, an amber box names it and the totals leave it out. A missing month is never shown as zero.

Open Classify customers and pick each customer’s category: Hotels, Supermarkets, Restaurants, Restaurant chains or Privates. Until then the customer counts as Unclassified. When the customer card in CRM has a matching name and Company Type, a suggestion appears; it is applied only when you click it.

A mother account adds up its own direct sales and all its branches, once. Branches come from QuickBooks sub-customers automatically; you can also set a mother account by hand, or mark a customer as standalone. Only a CRM manager or admin can change categories, and every change is logged.

Closed months are read once and kept. The current and previous month refresh every night at 02:00 Manila. Actions ▾ ⟳ Refresh pulls the selected year straight away, and ⬇ Export gives the table as a CSV file with the basis written on the last line.

Data health lists each month: documents, lines, sales, credits and net. To check, run Sales by Customer Summary in QuickBooks for the same month on an accrual basis and compare. A difference usually comes from journal entries posted straight to income accounts, which are not customer sales.
Advance orders from SOS (what is booked ahead, by delivery day, week and month), product families and varieties, saved reports and Nexi insights.

title: CEA — Follow-up Desk and My Reminders
summary: What is due today, in the next 7 days and at renewal, and what is waiting for an update or for an agency — per person, supervised by Edelyn.

p: 🏛 CEA ▸ 📅 Follow-up Desk. Edelyn and admins see everyone, and can filter by owner or switch to Only mine. Everybody else sees My Reminders: only what is assigned to them.

Today · Next 7 days · Renewals (register items within 180 days, with their ladder step) · Waiting for update (a case untouched for 14 days, or with no next action) · Agency waiting · Escalated (2+ days late, critical or blocking) · No owner. The last list is Next 12 months: how many items fall due each month.

steps: 📂 Open goes to the case, request or register item.
👍 Acknowledge means "I have seen it". It STAYS open until the work is done.
📅 Set internal follow-up date brings an item forward, with a reason. It NEVER moves the official deadline.
👤 Reassign (tasks) and ✅ Mark done (a note is required).

p: Every morning at 08:00 Manila the gov-watch worker checks every case, task, permit and agency request, and prepares each person's digest: Due today, Next 7 days, Renewals, Waiting for your update and Blocked. It also prepares Edelyn's supervisor line: no owner, 2+ days overdue, stalled 14+ days, no next action, renewals within 14 days and blocking requests.

Once the admin sets up the nexi@ mailer (workers/cea-digest-mailer.gs), everyone also gets that digest by e-mail after the 08:00 run, but only when it has something in it. Edelyn gets the portfolio line and a list of people with no e-mail on file. If the run is missing, the mailer sends Edelyn a warning, never an "all clear".

WhatsApp, when the admin switches it on, is for URGENT items only: something due today or late, something blocked, or a renewal within 14 days. It comes from Nexi's number +63 977 857 2214, at most one message a day. Your phone must be on your employee card, and Edelyn's e-mail lists anyone with no phone on file.

The top of the Follow-up Desk shows the last run. If today's run is missing after 08:30 it says so in amber, never "all clear". Nothing is e-mailed or messaged yet; it is in Nexi only. An admin connects it once: ⚙ set up (the same gov-watch link and token as the Deep Well Sources tab).

Every dated compliance item also appears in 📅 Calendar as a 🏛 Compliance entry. Edelyn and admins see all of them; everyone else sees only their own. Restricted immigration items never show. Moving a date in the case moves it on the calendar; the calendar never changes a deadline.

title: CEA — Regulatory Register
summary: The register of every license, permit and certificate — including the ones that never expire.

p: Compliance & External Affairs (CEA) → 📜 Regulatory. One row per license/permit/certificate, with its agency, license number, issue and expiry date, and how many days of runway are left.
Press ➕ New Item and fill in the agency’s own wording for the item name, its company, agency, license number and issue date.

Expiry date is optional — leave it blank for a document that never expires, such as a SEC or BIR Certificate of Registration. It saves the same as any other item and shows "no expiry on file" instead of a countdown.

note.k: WHY THE EXPIRY MATTERS WHEN THERE IS ONE
note.t: A dated item drives the 180/120/90/60/30/14/7/0-day renewal reminders (§6.2) — that ladder has nothing to count down to on an item with no expiry, so it is deliberately left out of it. Press 🏛 Verify afterwards to record how the expiry was confirmed with the agency; until then it is labelled an unverified (operational) expiry.

p: A case’s Status box will not accept APPROVED or RELEASED on its own — typing it in does nothing. It needs a VERIFIED government check FIRST: press 🏛 Log Government Check, pick Method Email/Document/Portal (not Manual or Forecast — those never confer VERIFIED), fill in the agency’s reference number and its exact wording, attach the evidence document, set Normalized Nexi status to APPROVED, and Save. Once that check is recorded the Status box accepts APPROVED and the case is stamped with exactly when.

That stamp, plus the case’s own "Approved on" / "Released on" line, is how you can always tell a case is final and approved — not implied by silence, but a recorded date backed by the evidence you attached.

note.t: Any case linked to a register item (regulatory, renewal or immigration) shows the register’s expiry AND the "file the renewal by" date right in the case header — the expiry minus that item’s lead days (90 days = 3 months by default, editable per item, minimum recommended 1-3 months). That is also the exact date the renewal case is raised automatically, so it is never missed.

sections.h: 🖊 Request Internal Sign-off is a DIFFERENT button
p: 🖊 Request Internal Sign-off does not touch the government status and will never move a case to APPROVED — it only asks an admin (President/VP) to sign off internally, in ✅ Tasks & Approvals. Pressing it again and again will not get a registration approved; only 🏛 Log Government Check does that, per the section above.
When a case has no VERIFIED government check yet, a small amber note appears right under the Status box saying so — that is the reminder to use 🏛 Log Government Check, not the sign-off button.

sections.h: A CLOSED case never shows a red countdown again (v20.94)
p: Once a renewal case reaches CLOSED, its card shows a quiet “✓ <date>” instead of the red “Xd → date” urgency badge — closing the case is enough on its own, nothing else to do to make the countdown go away.

The countdown itself still belongs to the register item, not the case: if this was a true renewal (a new expiry date), update that on the Regulatory Register item so the NEXT renewal cycle counts down correctly — closing the case just stops IT from nagging you.

title: Overview — the whole company on one screen
summary: Where you look first: what is wrong right now across every module, what is overdue, and what the day produced.

p: 🚨 Critical Summary is the shortest useful screen in Nexi: warnings and criticals only, from every module, with nothing else in the way.

📋 Task Tracker is the daily check-in on those items. Anything left unresolved escalates by itself, and 🚨 Escalation groups what escalated by owner and by module — that is the list to work through with a supervisor.

Every site at a glance.

The 🚐 Fleet line counts what 🚛 Trip Log holds for the day: how many driver-days were logged, how many drops those cover, and how many different trucks ran. It is the same store payroll pays trip incentives from, so if the line looks light, the trips were not logged yet — and the incentive will be light too.

note.k: THE FLEET LINE IS A LOGGING CHECK
note.t: Deliveries ran and the Fleet line is missing? Nobody has logged them. Chase the log before the payroll cut-off, not after.

sections.h: What to do with what you find
p: Nothing here is fixed from here. A red item names its module — open that module and deal with it there, or raise a call from the header so it lands with the right team and stays visible until it is closed.

title: Production
summary: The daily checklist across the greenhouses, the recurring cleaning tasks, seed studies and the seedling plan.

steps: Open ✅ Checklist (or 📋 Supervisor Daily Report for the full 50-item × 10-greenhouse grid).
Work down it and set each item OK, warning or critical. A warning or a critical wants a note saying what you saw.
Anything you mark critical becomes visible on the Critical Summary and the Brain immediately.

p: 📋 Supervisor Daily Report puts the whole checklist against every greenhouse in one grid, auto-filled from the recurring tasks. Tap any cell to set its status and add a note. It is the fastest way to see which greenhouse is behind.

sections.h: 📍 The Location Heatmap — and why a dot may be missing
p: The map at the top of the checklist is tables A–F × numbers 1–32 for the greenhouse you are on. A flagged item appears on it ONLY once you have told it WHERE — and a coloured dot is one affected category in that cell.
steps: Flag the item ⚠ or ✕.
Press 📍 on that item and choose the location.
Table + No. puts a dot in that one cell. Table + No. + a second No. lights the whole run, for example D12 to D18.
Affects MOST tables or Affects ALL tables hatches the WHOLE grid instead, because nobody recorded which tables — the pill above the map names the category.

note.k: THE HEADER TELLS YOU WHAT IS MISSING
note.t: It reads, for example, “5 flagged · 1 with location · 4 unplaced”, and the amber strip under it NAMES the unplaced items. Those four are not lost and the map is not broken — nobody has said where they are yet. Add the location and the dot appears.

sections.h: If the map itself looks wrong
p: The checklist redraws itself every few seconds so that what another machine saves reaches your screen. If the map ever cannot be drawn, it now says so in its own box and the checklist below it keeps working — it does not take the page with it.
A map that says “this facility has no checklist record loaded yet” has not lost anything: refresh the page. If it stays that way, report it with the message shown.

What it is for

Every recurring task — today, the week, the month calendar, history. The long-cadence ones (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual) each carry a next-due date, a last-done stamp and a ✓ Done that rolls the date; the follow-up strip shows what is overdue, due within 7 days, or not yet scheduled. On the 📍 Per-Greenhouse Schedule grid a per-week task only opens 2 of 10 greenhouses a day (e.g. waterlines: Mon → GH3&4, Tue → GH5&6…) — a dashed cell outside today’s pair is still tappable: work finished ahead of or outside the rotation marks and logs the same way, it just does not count toward that row’s "N due today" total.

5-level proficiency certification with supervisor sign-off; the level drives the pay rate.

Germination, growth, yield and commercial viability per variety and batch.

The weekly soak and plant schedule per greenhouse. One NFT line = 336 rockwool plugs.

PRJ11 / PRJ12 lettuce, per table (A1-A6, B1-B6), with photo progression.

sections.h: Saying what is being done about it
steps: Open 🩺 Problems & Actions. It lists every ⚠ and ✕ open on the day, grouped by greenhouse and then by issue group.

For each one pick from the drop box what is being done about it. The list offered is written for THAT kind of problem — water flow offers balancing the tables, cleaning the NFT line, checking the pump pressure; disease offers spraying, isolating the table, removing the infected plants; leaf offers the EC, the pH, the calcium, the shading.
Add the detail beside it — which table, how much, who.
Press Mark done when it is done.

note.k: AN ACTION TRAVELS WITH ITS PROBLEM
note.t: A problem still open tomorrow arrives with its action already on it, still marked to-do. An action already marked done does not repeat — if the problem is back, it needs a new decision.

p: Pick 7, 14, 30 or 90 days or any from–to range. 📈 Status History then breaks the period down the way the crop is: one bar per greenhouse, split by issue group, so you can see at a glance that GH4’s problem is water flow and GH7’s is disease.

The groups are exactly the rows of the 🌿 Crops Matrix — same order, same names, same colours — including its two extra rows, NFT Pipes Clean and Seedlings / Nursery. A group with nothing in the period is still shown, dimmed, so the picture never changes shape.

The table below it is the Crops Matrix itself over the period: the same rows, the greenhouses in the same column order, and each cell says how many times that was flagged. Click any block or any figure to dig in: every single occurrence with its date, its note, what was done about it and whether that was finished — plus how many days of the period it was present, the item that comes up most, and the action normally taken.

note.k: “NOTHING RECORDED” IS THE NUMBER TO WATCH
note.t: The dig-in marks in red every occurrence where nobody said what was done. A recurring problem with no action recorded is the one to raise in the meeting.

sections.h: A problem stays until somebody clears it
p: Until now the checklist started blank every morning, so an unresolved ⚠ or ✕ disappeared at midnight and had to be typed again. It no longer does: on the first load of a new day every warning and critical still open the day before is carried into today and marked as carried, and it stays there until somebody changes it.
An OK is NOT carried. Yesterday’s pass is not evidence that today was checked — an item nobody has looked at today still reads as unchecked.

📈 Status History is where the record lives. Pick 7, 14, 30 or 90 days or any from–to range and it draws problems per day, a greenhouse × day strip (tap a square to open that day), and a ranking of what comes back most often — that ranking is the one to bring to a supervisor meeting.

sections.h: Long-cadence tasks — scheduled, followed up, on the calendar
p: The monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual tasks used to be a list with a cadence word and nothing else. Each now carries a NEXT DUE date. Press ✓ Done today when it is done: the completion is logged with your name and the next due date rolls forward by the cadence. Type a date in the box to schedule or move it by hand; the small box beside it takes a follow-up note.

The Today tab shows only what is on today, grouped under its owner — GH workers, Maintenance, IT, Logistics — with a count per group; everything not scheduled today folds into one line at the bottom (tap it to show). A long-cadence task appears there only on the day it is due, as one DUE / OVERDUE row with ✓ Done.

The follow-up strip above the cards counts what is OVERDUE (red), DUE TODAY, DUE WITHIN 7 DAYS, and NOT SCHEDULED — a task with no date yet is listed there in red until somebody sets one. Overdue and due-today tasks also appear in the Today tab.

Scheduled tasks land on the calendars: the Recurring Tasks Month tab shows each one on its due day (OVERDUE in red), and the Overview 📅 Task Calendar shows a 🔁 chip on the day — press the day to see the tasks and mark them done from there.

sections.h: The Digital Twin — one greenhouse, everything about it
p: The 🧠 Nexi Cockpit shows every greenhouse as a card; press a card and its Digital Twin opens. Every figure on it is a link — checklist, warnings, open items, fan issues, attendance, requests, the critical in the Emergency box, each line in the Nexi AI box — press it and the screen holding the detail opens, already on that greenhouse.

Below the summary the twin lists what is linked to that greenhouse: 🩺 today’s open problems with what is being done about each (red “no action yet” where nothing is), 📈 the last 14 days as squares (press one for the history), 📞 its open calls and issues one by one (press one to open the call), 🔧 its fan issues, 👷 who is present today, 📋 its memos (press one to read it), and 📦 its item requests. Each heading opens the full screen.

note.k: NO SENSOR IS NOT A FAULT
note.t: Climate, radio, NFC and photo rows say “no sensor” or “no device feed yet” because those devices are not wired to Nexi. They will fill in when they are; nothing is invented meanwhile.

Marking something critical raises it to the people who can act. Marking everything critical means nobody can tell what is urgent. Use warning for what needs attention this week and critical for what stops production or risks the crop.

title: Maintenance
summary: The task board, the preventive-maintenance calendar, equipment, spare parts and the calls that come in from every other module.

p: Most maintenance work is not typed in by the maintenance team. It arrives: Production logs a broken fan, Irrigation logs a pump, the equipment check fails, the PM scheduler fires, a spare part crosses its reorder point. All of those raise a call.

📊 Calls Matrix organises the open calls by subject × department — that is the board to run the day from. 📞 Open Calls is the flat list — and for Maintenance it is EVERY open call on the site, whichever module raised it (a badge says which), because Maintenance handles all calls; the cockpit box counts the same list.
Under ⚙️ Equipment & Machines → 📻 Radio, ➕ Add Radio Unit and the row ✕ add and remove radio units (managers only); a removed unit keeps its check history.

steps: Open ✅ Task Board — the day’s tasks with status and photos.
Check 📅 PM Calendar for what preventive maintenance is due.

Anything needing an item from the warehouse goes on the task as a material: start typing and the SOS item list opens (items that start with your letters first, then the ones containing them); pick one and the item number, description and unit come with it. 📦 Material Requests lists them for tomorrow — press 📦 Raise item request on a line, or 📦 Raise item requests for all pending, and each becomes a real item request routed for approval and issue, with its number shown on the line. A material typed by hand is marked “free text” and still works, but the warehouse cannot match it to stock.
Close what you finished, with a photo where it helps.

sections.h: 🤖 AI photo analysis on a call (v20.93)
p: When raising a call, any photo you attach gets a "🤖 Analyze" button. Press it and the AI reads the photo and shows what looks wrong and the specific next action, right there in the call form — before the call is even submitted.

It is one press, not automatic — nobody's data or photo goes anywhere unless someone presses the button. If it says nothing looks wrong, that is also useful: it means the photo doesn't show the fault, attach a clearer one.

note.k: IT IS A SUGGESTION, NOT A DIAGNOSIS
note.t: The AI reads the photo, not the machine. Use its read as a head start, not the final word — the technician who opens the call still decides.

note.t: A repair that is done but whose call is still open keeps showing as a problem on the Brain, the Critical Summary and the other team’s matrix. Closing the call is part of the repair.

title: Irrigation
summary: The pools four times a day, the drum levels, dosing, calibration and the equipment behind them.

p: 🏊 Pool Monitor is the core of this module: 4 rounds a day (08:00, 11:00, 14:00, 16:00). The date always opens on today, Manila time, and moves to the new day after midnight. Readings are colour-coded against the thresholds set in ⚙️ Pool & Drum Setup.

Saving (v22.22): a value is saved when you press Tab or Enter, or click outside the box. Nexi never saves a half-typed number, and the cursor moves on to the next box. When a reading looks like a typo, Nexi asks first, for example “EC 1 for Pool 1 is far from the last reading (1.68)”. Press Cancel to re-type it, or OK if that is really what the meter shows.

Two meters (Eyal): each pool is read with the controller AND the handheld meter. If the two EC readings differ by more than 0.05, or the two pH readings by more than 0.10, the row says CALIBRATE and no A/B/C is given until they agree. Otherwise Nexi doses on the average. One meter alone is used as read.

Under each pool, “💡 Nexi says” gives the result in one line, for example “Add 121 L pure water · A 2100 cc · B 2100 cc · C 30 cc”. The same numbers fill the Water Added and A/B/C boxes, 🎯 Smart Dosing and 📋 Export for Reven. A number you type yourself in those boxes is never overwritten.

Instruments (v22.22): above each pool’s boxes you see its tank with the fill valve (water drips in while the pool is being filled to its daily target, and the litres to add are written under it, with the A/B/C drums of its fertilizer room), a pH column 0–8 with a yellow level, and an EC column 0–5 with a lightning level. They change only when a reading is saved (Tab, Enter or click away), never while you type, and they never take the cursor. The colours are the same ranges as the boxes. Tap a gauge for the big view. With ⚡ Lite ON (or a computer set to reduced motion) the gauges stand still; the 🎞 Motion button above the table changes that for this computer only.

Alarms (v22.22): every pool alarm, colour, chip and call is judged ONLY from the LATEST saved reading of that pool — the latest round of today. Older rounds and older days never raise anything. A CRITICAL EC, pH or water level opens ONE call (with its task) per pool and problem; the moment the next reading is back in range Nexi closes that call and task by itself, with a note of the reading that cleared it. When a new day starts, yesterday’s pool alarms close by themselves and nothing is raised until the first reading of the day arrives. A warning only turns the box orange. The red alert card of a pool alarm leaves the screen (and the “+N more” count) the moment that alarm is closed, a card is never shown for a call that is already closed, and the 🔔 Alerts panel lists the alarm under Resolved once the reading is back in range. Nexi closes a pool alarm only after this computer’s first cloud download of the day has arrived (a computer that opens with yesterday’s copy never closes an alarm that is still live elsewhere); while the computer is offline, an alarm closes only on a reading typed here that is newer than the alarm’s reading, never because “there is no reading here”. Readings typed on two computers are combined: each value keeps its newest entry, and nothing typed is lost when the cloud download finishes.
steps: Open 🏊 Pool Monitor and pick the round.
For each pool type the level, both EC readings and both pH readings, pressing Tab after each one.
Read “Nexi says” under the pool and add exactly that.
If it says CALIBRATE, calibrate both meters and measure again.

p: Every reading box turns green (OK), orange (warning) or red and blinking (critical). The same ONE table of ranges is used by the gauges, the CRIT / WARN chip of each pool, the alarms and calls, the Issues Board, the 💧 EC / pH Watch, the FR matrix, 🎯 Smart Dosing and the line “Target ranges” above the table — there is no second list of limits anywhere in Nexi.
EC (mS/cm): OK 1.70 – 1.90 · warning 1.50 – 1.69 or 1.91 – 2.00 · critical below 1.50 or above 2.00.
pH: OK 5.80 – 6.50 · warning 5.50 – 5.79 or 6.51 – 6.80 · critical 5.49 and below or 6.81 and above.
Water level (cm, the level you measure): see the table. Each pool’s bands can be changed by an admin in ⚙️ Pool & Drum Setup → 📏 Level bands; EC and pH ranges per pool are in the same card.

The CLEANING target is only for refilling the pool after cleaning (the old 130 / 120 / 100 cm values). Both are set by an admin in ⚙️ Pool & Drum Setup.

sections.h: What to add: the dosing matrix (Eyal’s workbook)
p: Water: gap = daily target − level, in whole cm. Water (L) = L × W × gap ÷ 1000.

A and B (each): EC matrix value (row = EC rounded to 0.05, lowest row 1.50; column = cm to add, at most 48) × pool template (Pool 9 ×1.5, Pools 7 and 8 ×0.67) × water-source factor (Pure 1; Over-tank or Mix reduced by the over-tank EC set in the toolbar).
If the EC is above 2.35: water only, no A/B, then re-check.
C (acid): gap × 5 cc per cm × pH factor. pH factor = 1 + (pH − 6.2), kept between 0.5 and 2.
Example: Pool 1 at 54 cm with EC 1 is 6 cm under its daily 60 cm (the level is GOOD; the EC 1 is critical, so the EC box is red): add 121 L pure water · A 2100 cc · B 2100 cc · C 30 cc.
The old fill rule (v21.71: morning fill, whole litres of A and B per cm) is no longer the default. An admin can switch a pool back to it in Pool & Drum Setup → 🌱 Fill rule (v21.71).

🎯 Smart Dosing shows every pool of the round on one screen with the same numbers as “Nexi says” (water in litres, A, B and C); ✓ APPLY ALL writes them into the Pool Monitor. A pool that needs CALIBRATE gets no dose there either.
🧠 AI Insights looks back over 14 days and learns how much each dose actually moved EC and pH in that pool, and shows the confidence behind it.

Below the Pool Monitor table: pick a pool and press "Analyze last 5 days". It reads that pool's last 5 days of EC/pH (all 4 daily rounds, manual meter preferred over the controller reading, same as the rest of this screen) against its target range and says whether it is drifting toward or past the range — not just whether today's single reading happens to be in bounds.
This catches a slow drift across several days that a same-day colour check on its own would not flag until it was already out of range.

What it is for

title: Packaging
summary: The wash-and-trim process, the daily checklist QC reviews, the materials, and who is responsible for what.

p: 🥬 Wash & Trim SOP runs the day: Pick Ticket → wash, trim, spin, mix → weight log → output. Follow it in order; the weight log is what the dashboard’s variance against target weights is built from.
✅ Daily Checklist is the packaging process and policy check — and QC reviews it. Do it honestly: QC’s 🔬 Process Inspection reads these same subjects.

What it is for
rows: Dashboard
Daily output, per-product variance against target weight, a materials snapshot, traceability and the QC link.
📦 Materials
Boxes, labels, films, trays, ice packs — stock levels, reorder points, suppliers.
⚙️ Operations
The operating screens for the line.
📋 Duties Matrix
Per position (Supervisor Packaging, Packaging Staff): assign to a worker, tick off, with live cold-storage, harvest-PO and shipment checks from SOS.
📞 Packaging Calls
Pending approvals and open packaging issues.

The 💰 Salary Category decides which payroll pays the person: weekly labour (no attendance record = absent) or office (no record = paid). Without that permission Nexi puts the old value back and says so. With it, Nexi asks first. Changing the department of someone who has their own category never moves their payroll: the category stays, and the mismatch banner offers Align to someone with payroll permission.
