sections.h: What a GH memo moves in payroll
p: A GH memo is priced by exactly the rule payroll uses. It counts everyone assigned to the GH, plus every supervisor connected to it, who was present or late that day, at the ⚙ Memo rates for their tier. The FINAL approval and the signing both show each person's amount and the total, for example 'Payroll will move: −₱1,800.00 (10 lines)'. When a memo is signed, the rates of that moment are frozen on it, so a later edit to ⚙ Memo rates does not change a signed memo. In ⚙ Memo rates, a ₱0 you save means ₱0. A ₱0 stored before this version still counts as the default until you press Save there once. An individual (HR) memo bigger than one pay period's basic pay is flagged on the memo and at approval. Older memo records that hold the GH under 'ghAffected' now show on the approval the same figure payroll deducts.

A memo dated inside a payroll period that is already approved is carried into the next open cut-off when it is fully signed or applied, after you confirm. A production memo still charges only the workers present on its own date. A memo the locked run already paid or deducted is never carried. If the cut-off it was carried into is locked before the memo is applied, Apply to payroll carries it on again. The Memo trace says where a carried memo counts.

Open the memo. In 🏛 Executive Approval, Eyal, Dr Amy or an Admin pick one Decision from the dropdown: ✔ Approve → payroll (the FINAL approval) or ✖ Reject / cancel. Rejecting asks for the reason, which is required; the memo then shows REJECTED with who, when and why, and payroll does not count it. A memo that was already signed or applied can be rejected too — regenerate the payroll run that paid it. The Memos list has a Rejected filter. If it was rejected by mistake, an admin presses ↩ Re-open: the memo returns to Pending and the rejection stays in its trail.

Attended days ÷ 26
Attended days ÷ 22

note.k: THIS IS THE MOST COMMON MISUNDERSTANDING
note.t: A missing scan costs a labor employee a day and costs an office employee nothing. That is deliberate — but it means a clock that failed for a labor crew has to be fixed in attendance BEFORE the run, not argued about after.

steps: Make sure attendance for the whole period is correct — including any late that is still waiting on Eyal or Dr Amy.
Open 👷 Labor Payroll or 🏢 Office Payroll for the period.
Generate the run and read it before approving it.

Approve & Lock. From that moment the run is a frozen snapshot. If attendance changed after the screen was built (for example the clock report for the last day arrived while you were reading), Approve & Lock refuses, names who changed ('JO SANTOS: 5 → 6 day(s)') and rebuilds the screen with the current figures. Read it again and approve.
p: The 👥 Show employees filter works as before on both runs. By default it lists only people with attendance in the period, a trip, or final pay still owed. An unmarked office day is PAID, so the office Approve & Lock check names every Active office employee missing from the run, with the half-month at stake (for example ₱8,000 on ₱16,000/month). A card with no pay basis at all is named as such, with the instruction to fill the rate or set the card Inactive. If one of them should be paid, switch the filter to show everyone and press ↻ Recalculate before locking. The same check also names every inferred start (Date Hired blank) and every signed late that needs a re-decision.

Draft runs are no longer trimmed in the background. An office-department employee (for example APAC_PACKAGING) and a leaver who is still owed their final cut-off now stay in the stored draft, so All Payroll, the journal and the BIR reports see the same lines as the payroll screen.

note.t: Changing an employee card, a rate or a trip table afterwards does NOT change an approved run. Attendance or money that arrives later for a locked period is carried into the next open cut-off (see 🔒 After a run is approved). Reopen and regenerate only when the whole run really has to be re-priced.

sections.h: Holidays, half days and people who join or leave mid cut-off

head: Situation
What payroll does now
rows: A special non-working holiday nobody worked

It is a normal paid office day. It used to quietly cost every office employee one full day of pay and part of their allowance, because the day stayed in the divisor the rate is built from but was never counted as paid.
Somebody leaves mid cut-off
Set Contract End on their HR card. Payroll stops at that date. Before, an office leaver kept being paid every remaining weekday because an unmarked office day counts as paid.
Somebody joins mid cut-off
Set Date Hired. Payroll starts there, the allowance prorates to the days that remain, and their first ever scan is never counted as late.
A half day

Mark it in Attendance, Reconcile (½ Half day). It pays half a day. On a holiday, the premium is paid on the half worked, and the half not worked is paid like an unworked holiday. Office ₱16,000/month (₱727.27/day): a half day on a regular holiday is ₱8,000.00 + ₱363.64 = ₱8,363.64. A half day on a special holiday is ₱8,000.00 + ₱109.09 = ₱8,109.09 (it used to pay ₱7,854.55, less than staying home). Weekly labour at ₱500/day: special half day ₱250 + ₱75 = ₱325.00, regular half day ₱750.00. The button used to change only the time out, and payroll still paid the whole day. To undo it, open the day in Attendance and untick the ½ Half day box, or set Time Out to 17:00 or later, then Save. Choosing a Lunch Shift no longer re-ticks the box, and a real OUT scan at 17:00 or later clears the half day by itself.
A holiday on an office rest day (Sunday, or Saturday on a five-day card), worked

Paid only once it is signed in HR ▸ Weekend Approvals, like any weekend day. Once signed it pays the rest-day 130% (Sun OT column) plus the holiday premium (Holiday column): a regular holiday is 260% of the daily rate in all, a special holiday 150%. At ₱727.27/day: regular ₱945.45 + ₱945.45 = ₱1,890.90, special ₱945.45 + ₱145.45 = ₱1,090.90. A special working day stays 130%. A half day pays half of each part. Until it is signed it pays nothing and waits (⏳) at the full amount. Management and fixed-fee consultants never get weekend pay. On a six-day card, Saturday is a scheduled day (a regular holiday on it is 200%). Weekly labour is unchanged: a labour Sunday is an ordinary day, so a regular holiday on it is 200%.
“Paid when NOT worked” on the 📅 Holidays screen

This % applies to the daily rate for weekly labour only. Office staff on a monthly basic get their full half-month whatever the % says. Above 0 only takes the holiday out of the rate divisor, and 0 leaves it in as an ordinary paid day. The Holidays screen says this, and it flags in amber any value other than 0 or 100.
The Basic Pay line on a payslip

The line multiplies out. For 26 Aug–10 Sep with 31 Aug a regular holiday nobody worked, the office line reads “Basic Pay (11 regular days × ₱727.2727) ₱8,000.00”. The regular holiday prints on its own row as included, because it is already inside the half-month. Sunday work is in Sun OT. The rate shows 4 decimals when it is not a whole number of centavos. The line used to say 12 days beside ₱8,000.00. On weekly slips every paid day is counted, Sunday included: 7 days × ₱658.00 = ₱4,606.00 (it used to print 6).

note.k: THE RATE PER DAY DOES NOT MOVE FOR ANY OF THESE
note.t: A mid cut-off hire or leaver changes only the days counted, never the rate per day. Narrowing the divisor would quietly raise their rate.

sections.h: When pay cannot cover the deductions
p: Net pay can no longer go below zero. If signed deductions come to more than the period pays, the shortfall is shown on the line instead of printing a negative net. Decide deliberately whether to recover it in a later cut-off. Before this, the negative flowed into every total while the bank file simply dropped the person with no message.

An allowance added to the same cut-off with + Allowance pays that shortfall first. Someone absent for the whole cut-off still owes ₱700 of SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG. With a typed ₱1,000 transport they net ₱300, and nothing is left “still owed” on the payslip, the CSV or the QuickBooks journal.

sections.h: Typing in a location or a search box
p: On the GPS Daily Report, type the location freely. The box suggests customers, saved places and locations used before, and picking one sets the Kind for you. Nothing is rebuilt while you type, so the cursor stays where it is.

The same used to happen in the search boxes on HR, Training, IT Devices, Maintenance, Tools, Radios, Inventory, the four CRM screens and Accounting Purchasing: the list rebuilt after every letter and took the cursor with it. All of them keep the cursor now.

note.k: IF A FIELD EVER LOSES YOUR CURSOR AGAIN
note.t: First check the version in the title bar against the red bar described below — twice now the fix was already live and the person was on a cached Nexi. If the version is current, it is a bug: say which screen and which box.

sections.h: 🔎 If something you saved goes missing
p: Press the 🔎 button beside the sync chip at the bottom left. It lists every time the cloud replaced something saved on this computer — when, what, the old value and the new one, newest first. Screenshot it and send it with your report.
An empty list is an answer too: it means the sync on that machine did not take it, which rules out a whole class of cause in one look.
The warning that says “Sync replaced N entries” now opens this list by itself, instead of scrolling away before you can read it.

note.t: Opening this changes nothing. It keeps the last 80 changes, on that computer only.

sections.h: The red bar: “You are running an OLD Nexi”
p: Nexi checks the copy on the server every so often and compares it with the one on your screen. If the server is ahead, a red bar appears at the top with one button, ↻ Load the new version. Press it. It reloads past the cache, which an ordinary refresh does not always do.

This matters more than it sounds. A browser can keep an old Nexi for days, and every fix made for you in that time is simply not on your screen — which has already cost two people several days of reporting bugs that were fixed. The bar exists so that can no longer happen quietly.

head: What you see
What to do
rows: Red bar naming a newer version
Press ↻ Load the new version. Nothing you have typed into a form is saved, so finish the line you are on first.
No bar
You are on the current Nexi. If something still behaves wrongly, it is a real bug — report it.
You pressed Later
It comes back. Nothing is broken, but the fixes are still not on your screen.
The sync chip at the bottom left stays AMBER

That chip is the cloud sync. GREEN means this device is publishing what you save to everybody else; AMBER means it has not completed a sync recently; RED means it hit an error and will retry. Say so if it stays amber — until this was fixed a single dropped connection could switch sync off for the rest of the session with nothing turning red, and everything saved after that stayed on that one machine.
A yellow 🔑 box says the QuickBooks link key is not set

QuickBooks reports and the customer feed need a key that used to be written inside Nexi’s page, where anyone could read it. Since v21.13 an admin enters it once: click Enter key and paste the key set on the qb-api worker in Cloudflare. It is kept in Nexi’s synced settings, so the other signed-in machines receive it within a minute; reload them once. Only admins see the box.
The sync chip is RED with “sync timed out” or “upload held”

The first download from the cloud is large (about 15 MB) and can take a minute or two on a slow line. Nothing you save is sent until that download finishes, so a new user or a changed password does not reach the other machines yet. Leave Nexi open for two minutes; the chip turns green and your changes go up. If it stays red, click it and press ↕ Full re-sync.

note.k: THE VERSION IS IN THE TITLE BAR
note.t: Every screenshot you send should show it. It is the fastest way to tell a real bug from an old copy.

sections.h: 🪪 Where is the HR card? — setting a contractor to group 19 (v21.04)
p: The HR card is the employee card. Open it from HR & People: click the employee's NAME in the list, and the card opens.
Scroll UP on the card to the pay block, below Employment Type, Job Title / Position, Pro Level and Daily Rate Override. There you find 💰 Salary Category.
In 💰 Salary Category choose '19. GH15 & GH16 Project Contractor Labor'. Then, lower on the card in the 👷 CONTRACTOR box, pick the project: PRJ15 – GH15 or PRJ16 – GH16.
Press 💾 Save. If you close the card without saving, Nexi asks: OK saves, Cancel does not.
Do this for each contractor, then regenerate the draft labour week. The payroll screen and reports then show GH15 and GH16 as separate groups, each with its own subtotal.

sections.h: 👷 GH15 & GH16 Project Contractor Labor — the no-benefits group (v21.03)
p: Salary Category '19. GH15 & GH16 Project Contractor Labor' on the HR card separates the project contractor workers from everyone else. They are paid in the weekly labour payroll and appear as their own group in the rosters and exports.

They get NO benefits: pay is only the days actually worked × the daily rate. No paid leave, no holiday pay or holiday premium, no recurring allowances, no SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG (employee or employer share), no 13th month, and no leave cash at final pay.
Anything extra must come through a signed memo (trip incentives included), a one-time payment, or a contractor bonus / penalty. Those still pay as usual.
Set the project (PRJ15 / PRJ16) in the card's Contractor section as before. The HR ↔ payroll mismatch banner never offers to 'Align' this group back into a benefits category.
Moving someone into this group changes the NEXT run you generate. An approved run is a frozen snapshot, so regenerate a draft week if it should follow the new group.

Their day is 08:00–17:00 on the daily rate: 8 paid hours, 08:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 (lunch unpaid). Arriving AFTER 08:00 (first scan) or leaving BEFORE 17:00 (last scan) is deducted automatically, in proportion: paid minutes missed ÷ 480 × the daily rate. Example: ₱600/day, in 08:30 → ₱37.50; out 16:00 → ₱75.00; in 08:30 and out 16:00 → ₱112.50. Never more than the day.
Arriving before 08:00 or leaving after 17:00 pays the same daily rate. There is NO overtime for this group, ever.
There is no approval step: these deductions do not appear in Late approvals, and the WARNING ONLY switch does not apply to them. A day with only a time-in (no out scan) is charged for lateness only.

GH15 and GH16 are shown as TWO separate groups, each with its own subtotal: '19. GH15 Project Contractor Labor' and '19. GH16 Project Contractor Labor'. Which one depends on the project picked in the card's Contractor section. A contractor with no project set appears under the combined heading, so set the project.

Every payroll report is grouped by payroll category, with a subtotal for each group and a grand total: the full Labor / Office Excel, 🧾 Payroll Totals and 📑 All Payroll. The group comes from the employee card, so change the category on the card first, then export.

sections.h: 💾 Employee card — saving, and leaving without saving (v21.03)
p: A card with no Job Title / Position now saves. Before, 💾 Save refused it and the background auto-save stopped without a word, so a changed payroll group was lost. A title is still required when you ADD a new employee.
If you close a card you changed (✕, clicking outside it, or Esc), Nexi asks. OK = save the changes. Cancel = don't save: the card goes back exactly to how it was when you opened it.
A card you only looked at closes with no question.

A bonus adds to gross; a penalty comes out of gross, exactly like any other deduction. Both then flow through to net in the normal way, so the run reconciles and the QuickBooks journal and the CSV both carry them.

A penalty can never take more than the person receives that week, and the rest is not written off. The week takes what it can. The check before Approve & Lock and the payslip show 'Penalty taken this week' and 'Carried forward to next week'. Once that week's run is APPROVED, Nexi writes the balance as a penalty entry ('Penalty balance carried from the week …') in the next week that is still open for that person. If that week cannot cover it either, the rest carries again. Weeks approved before this version that left a balance are not collected.
Adding a bonus or penalty asks you to confirm the peso amount and the labour week it lands in. A penalty larger than a full week's pay (6 × the daily rate) needs an administrator.

To WAIVE a carried balance, an administrator presses ✕ on its 'Penalty balance carried from…' row. The row stays in the list, struck through and marked WAIVED with the name of whoever waived it. It is never collected, and Nexi never writes it again. If you remove the ORIGINAL penalty after its week was approved, Nexi asks whether to waive the carried balance too. What an approved week already took stays taken, because that run is frozen.

A bonus or penalty dated inside a week that is already approved is carried into the next open week after you confirm. It keeps its date, and the list shows '→ paid <date>'. A contractor with no scans that week is still paid a carried bonus.

note.k: IF YOU EVER SAW “THIS RUN DOES NOT RECONCILE” ON A CONTRACTOR WEEK
note.t: That was this. The penalty was missing from gross, so the check could never balance and pressing Recalculate changed nothing. It balances now.

p: Set Date Hired on the HR card. For office staff a day with no attendance record is PAID on purpose, so without it a new joiner draws the WHOLE cut-off — every Mon–Fri, including the days before they worked here.

If the card has no Date Hired, payroll protects itself, but only on proof. Nexi finds the person's earliest record in the whole attendance store. If that record falls inside this cut-off AND is proof of work, they cannot have been employed before it, so that day is used as the start and the Days cell says so. Proof of work means present or late with a clock time, on a Monday to Friday (Saturday too on the weekly run). An absence, a leave or a weekend scan is never a start date. A 'no scan' absent that the machine wrote inside the cut-off (the NGTeco absent-fill or an import, with nobody's name on it) is ignored when looking for the start. But ANY record dated before the cut-off, a machine absent included, shows the person was already on the roster, so the whole cut-off counts as usual. A real Date Hired always wins.

note.t: The inferred start is a safety net, not a substitute. On the office run, 🔒 Approve & Lock names every inferred start with the working days it leaves unpaid and the pesos (for example 2 working days ≈ ₱1,454.54 on ₱16,000/month). On the weekly run it is a note with no pesos: a labour day with no record is unpaid anyway, and the start only keeps those days out of the absence count. Fill in Date Hired and press ↻ Recalculate.

head: Step
What to do
rows: Set Contract End on the HR card
Payroll stops paying at that date. Do this BEFORE the next run.
Run Final Pay

Payroll ▸ 🧮 Final Pay prices the leaver's unpaid days with the payroll engine itself, cut-off by cut-off (week by week for labour), from UNPAID SALARY FROM to the LAST WORKING DAY. It uses the payslip's daily rate and the same holiday, weekend-signature and proof rules, and an unmarked office weekday is paid. UNPAID SALARY FROM starts the day after the last APPROVED run that paid the person. A DRAFT run does not count, because a draft has paid nothing. It also pays the allowances of those days, including the + Allowance entries of the cut-off: an entry carried from the previous cut-off is prorated by the days, and an entry entered for the cut-off is paid whole. It also pays 🚚 trip incentives, signed memos, one-time payments (including one dated after the last day but inside the same cut-off) and an unpaid referral bonus. Decided tardiness, memo deductions and contractor penalties come off.
A weekend day in the last cut-off

Final Pay prices it with the payroll engine, so only a SIGNED weekend day is paid, including its holiday premium if it is a holiday. At ₱727.27/day a signed Sunday regular holiday is ₱1,890.90. An unsigned one is not paid. It is listed under “Waiting for a signature and NOT in this final pay” with the amount it will cost, so have it signed or refused before you record the final pay.
Offboarding ▸ 💰 Final Pay (T-46)

'Unpaid from' is the day after the last APPROVED run, never before the cut-off (or week) holding the Last Working Day. 'Days paid here' and 'Working days in that cut-off' come from payroll. A card with no monthly salary on the contract or the HR card shows 'Daily rate (₱/day)' instead of 'Base salary' and is paid days × that rate. For example, ₱700/day for 10 days is ₱7,000.00. Changing either date re-reads the days, 'Other pay for these days' and 'Other deductions' from payroll. Anything you typed in those boxes is replaced, so re-enter it after changing a date. 'Other pay' carries the holiday and Sunday premium, allowances (including the cut-off's + Allowance entries), trips, memos, one-time payments and an unpaid referral bonus. A blank '13th-month base' means ₱0 of earlier basic. 💰 Release is REFUSED, with the reason shown in red before you press it, when: an APPROVED run already paid any of the days; the last working day is after today; 'Unpaid from' → last day covers more than one cut-off or week (use Payroll ▸ 🧮 Final Pay for that); days of the same cut-off before 'Unpaid from' were paid by nobody (it names them); the days paid are not the days payroll counts; or what payroll pays for those days changed since it was prepared (a new absence, memo, trip…). In all these cases press 🔄 Recompute & re-prepare. Otherwise Release closes the days, and the items above, to payroll, so the regular run pays them only once.
Check the unused leave days
The box starts at 0. Enter only leave that is genuinely unused. It used to pre-fill 5 days for everyone, including people who had already taken and been paid for them.
Record the final pay as PAID

✅ Record as PAID closes those days. No payroll run pays them again, nor anything this final pay carried for them. It is REFUSED while any day of the window is after today: payroll does not count a day that has not happened, so recording early would close that day unpaid. Record it on or after the last working day. If UNPAID SALARY FROM starts inside a week or cut-off whose earlier days nothing paid, the UNPAID DAYS CHECK names them: press Cancel and set FROM to the period start. If a DRAFT run still holds the days, press 🔄 Recalculate on it before approving.
Then mark them Inactive or Resigned

Safe at any time now. A leaver still appears in the ONE cut-off that holds their last work, paid only up to their Last Working Day. It used to remove them from every run the moment the flag was set, so their final days were simply never paid.

note.k: THE RATE IS THE SAME RATE
note.t: Both final-pay screens use the rate on the leaver's payslips. For a monthly salary it is half the salary ÷ the working days of that cut-off (12/52 of it per labour week), with a regular holiday taken out of the divisor. For a card with no monthly salary it is the daily rate itself: ₱700 a day for 10 days is ₱7,000.00 whatever the length of the cut-off. It used to come out as ₱7,700.00 in a 10-day cut-off and ₱7,700.00 for 12 days.

sections.h: Payroll runs after a final pay
p: When a final pay has been recorded or released, a run skips its days and the trips, one-time payments, signed memos and contractor adjustments dated on them. It also skips a + Allowance entry entered for that cut-off that the final pay paid whole, a one-time payment dated after the last day that the final pay took, and a referral bonus the final pay paid (it is marked paid 'finalpay_…'). A carried allowance entry is prorated on both sides, so each side pays only its own days. The line's other days are paid as usual.

An Offboarding (T-46) final pay released before v20.97 wrote nothing payroll could see, so the regular run could pay the same last days again. The first time this version opens, each such release that paid last-period wages closes its days: from the start of the cut-off or week holding the last day (or the day after the last approved run, if later) to the last day. The audit log shows 'Final pay (T-46) released before v20.97 … now closed to payroll'. A release whose days an approved run already paid gets nothing. If a DRAFT run for that cut-off exists, press 🔄 Recalculate before approving it.

One rule everywhere: the 🎁 13th-month accrual, Payroll ▸ 🧮 Final Pay, the HR card's 📋 Final Pay and Offboarding T-46. It is the basic pay (Sunday and rest-day premium excluded) of APPROVED runs whose period ends in the year, ÷ 12. A final pay adds the basic it is paying. Draft runs never count. The management fixed engagement and consultant or advisor engagements get ₱0, and the screen says why. Contractual, Production-Contractual and 'Contractor' staff are INCLUDED, and every final-pay screen shows an orange 'owner decision pending' line until the owner confirms.

The 13th-month report accrues basic pay ÷ 12 for every rank-and-file employee, whatever the employment status. Regular, Probationary, Contractual and Production-Contractual workers are all included; Contractual ones are marked, and a note on the report counts them. Management (by salary category) and fee engagements (Employment Type Consultant, Contractor or Advisor) are left out. If someone listed as Contractual is really a fee-paid contractor, change their Employment Type to Contractor or Consultant.

sections.h: Editing an employee card is safe again
p: Saving a card used to replace the whole record, quietly deleting any field the form does not show. For anyone whose monthly salary was stored under an older field name that meant the salary itself was erased and payroll fell back to a stale daily rate or to zero. Saving now merges, so nothing you cannot see is lost.
Emptying the Daily Rate Override now really does hand the person back to the level rate, as the box has always said it would.

sections.h: Things that used to lose money quietly

head: What you do
What happens now
rows: Approve & Lock before the cut-off has ended
You are told how many working days after today are NOT in the figures. Locking freezes them out permanently, so normally you wait.
Change the payroll cut-off

Labour close day: the week already running on the effective date still ends on the OLD close day. Then ONE short bridging week (1 to 6 days) runs up to the first new close day, and normal weeks follow. If weekly payroll is already approved past the effective date, the new weeks start the day after the last approved week. No day falls in two weeks or in none. The preview and the confirm on Save name the last old week, the bridging week and the first new week. ▶ Next and ◀ Previous on Labor Payroll step into the bridging week, never over it. A bridging week pays, and deducts SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG, for its own days only. Office cut-off days: the warning about approved runs appears only when the office days change, and it names office runs only. The one switch-over cut-off that is neither an old nor a new half-month is paid its calendar share, monthly × 12 ÷ 365 × its days, with the monthly allowance scaled the same way. Example: 11–25/26–10 → 1–15/16–end from October gives 26 Sep–15 Oct = ₱10,520.55 on ₱16,000. The preview shows that cut-off.
Change the cut-off a second time

Every earlier cut-off era is now kept, so old periods keep the days they were actually paid on. Only one previous setting used to be remembered, so a second change silently re-cut everything from the first era.
Open the cut-off preview

It only draws a preview now. It used to write the preview settings into the real setting and put the original back afterwards, so anything that interrupted it — a reload, a closed tab — erased the effective date and the history for good.
Merge duplicate people

Their attendance is moved onto the record you keep, and you are told how many days move and how many clash. Pay fields are never copied silently: if the keeper has no rate and the duplicate does, you are asked, and an audit line is written. The old id still resolves in payroll history.

note.k: NONE OF THIS CHANGES A FIGURE BY ITSELF
note.t: Every one of these is a guard. They tell you what a step is about to cost before you take it.

sections.h: A period that is already approved is closed
p: Once a run is approved the attendance behind it is closed too. Fill from Timecards, Attendance Repair and the biometric import now refuse to write into a period covered by an approved run, and say which run is blocking them. Reopen that run first if the attendance genuinely has to change.

head: Action
What happens now
rows: Recalculate a locked run

Eyal or Dr Amy only. The confirm says the period goes back to DRAFT and must be signed again. What was paid is kept in the run history, and everybody the run paid stays on it, even if their card has since moved to the other payroll.
Reopen a period

The original approver and date are kept, together with what each person was PAID. Every line is re-priced from TODAY's cards, attendance and rules. Approve & Lock then lists each person's was-paid → now, with rate, days and allowance changes and people dropped or new, and asks for an explicit OK. The approved run shows a 🔁 banner with the difference to transfer or recover. Attendance days that were carried out of this run and already PAID in a later run count as paid. For example ₱3,290 → ₱3,948 with ₱658 already paid through the carry means nothing more to transfer. Carried adjustments still sitting in an open cut-off are taken back out when you reopen. If the save fails you are told, and the period stays approved.
Fill missing attendance on a Saturday or Sunday
You are warned first. A filled labor Sunday is paid at the full daily rate and does not go through Weekend Approvals, so nobody signs it off.
Move someone between the weekly and the office payroll

Only Admin, Accounting or someone with payroll permission can do it, however it is done: by picking a payroll category on the HR card, by Align on the mismatch banner, or by changing the department of a card whose payroll category is “— By department (legacy) —” (the department decides that person's payroll). Anyone else sees a message and the change is undone: the old category, or the old department, is put back. With permission, Nexi asks first and names the move. For Align it also names a Trainee → Regular switch and the SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG it starts (about ₱1,180 a month at ₱600 a day). Cancel keeps the old category, or the old department on a By-department card. A change that stays inside the same payroll follows the department silently, as before.
Recalculate, Add Worker, an allowance or a government deduction on a machine that has not yet received the approval
The approved run stays approved on every machine, with its approver. These buttons re-price only a draft, where it stands, and never delete a run. Only 🔓 Reopen takes a run out of APPROVED.
Approve & Lock a run that still pays days already in another APPROVED run

Refused. The alert names the approved run, the dates and the people, and nothing is locked. It happens to a draft made before the other run was approved, for example after a close-day change, or when someone moved between labour and office in the middle of a cut-off. Press 🔄 Recalculate or reopen the screen. Nexi leaves those days out, together with their government share, their memos, their trip days and any one-time item that run already paid. Then approve again.

sections.h: A day is never paid twice by two runs
p: A date inside another APPROVED weekly or office run that paid this person is left out of this run. It counts as neither worked nor absent. Its SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG share, the memos and trip days that run already carried, and any one-time item it already paid are left out with it. The Days tooltip says NOT PAID HERE and names the run. A line that paid nothing (somebody absent all week on the wrong payroll) settles nothing, so those days stay payable where the person really belongs.

The check above Approve & Lock shows two lines for this. 🔁 <name>: N day(s) of this period are already paid in approved <run>, left out of this run and not paid twice. 🔀 <name>: MOVED from the weekly labour (or office) payroll, last paid in <run>; this replaces 🆕 FIRST payout and names any dates between the two payrolls that no run pays. Those dates are NOT paid automatically. If the person is owed them, add them by hand.

The weekly government refresher that brings stored drafts up to the every-week rule uses the same days as the payroll. A bridging week, or a week with days already paid in another run, keeps its smaller share and is no longer rewritten every minute.

On the accounting dashboard, a finished labour week that overlaps an APPROVED run shows “overlaps APPROVED run <id>” instead of “has NO run yet”, and Nexi does not draft it by itself. Open Labor Payroll and check which days still need paying.

sections.h: 🔒 After a run is approved — money and attendance that arrive late

head: What happens
What Nexi does
rows: A one-time payment, contractor bonus or penalty, memo or delivery day dated inside an approved run

You are asked first. OK carries it into the next OPEN cut-off. It keeps its own date, and the list shows '→ paid <date>'. Cancel saves nothing. Something the locked run already paid (a memo in its memo list, a delivery day in its trip list) is never carried again.
The next cut-off is locked too before the item is signed, applied or re-approved
It is carried on again to the next open cut-off.
A delivery day the locked run already paid, with trips added afterwards (Deliveries sends it back for approval)
It stays with the run that paid it and is not paid twice. The confirm names the part that run did NOT pay (e.g. driver ₱200). Add that as a one-time payment in the next open cut-off.
A labour worker owed carried money who has no attendance in that week
They stay on the weekly run. The days are absent as usual, and only the carried money is paid.
An office employee or a leaver owed carried money who is not on the run
They are not added automatically, because an office line would also pay the whole half-month. Approve & Lock names them with 📦 and the amount. Use ➕ Add Worker, or settle a leaver in Final Pay.
Attendance changes after the lock (a late clock report, a correction)

The approved run shows '⚠ Attendance changed after this run was approved', and the next draft shows a summary: paid days → days now. Unpaid days are priced at the run's OWN daily rate and booked as prior-period BASIC pay, so they count for the 13th month. Their allowance share is paid at the run's own allowance: weekly monthly ÷ 26 per Mon–Sat day, office half the month × that cut-off's share, per-day allowances × days. Paid days means worked plus authorised: authorised leave later turned Present changes nothing and carries ₱0. A correction that moves money but not days (a late scan fixed, so less tardiness; a Sunday premium or holiday pay added) is listed too, and its difference is carried as a prior-period pay adjustment. ➕ Carry books that once into the next open cut-off. An overpaid day is only listed and never deducted automatically.
An allowance on today's HR card that an approved run did not pay

An approved run no longer tells you to press Recalculate because today's HR card has an allowance, which used to pay a new allowance back into an old, paid period. If the card already had the allowance when the run was locked and the run did not pay it, the banner names the person and points to a one-time payment in the next cut-off.

sections.h: If two Nexi screens ever disagree about the same figure
p: They should not. Gross, Days, the allowance total and the government shares are now read from one place by the screen, the payslips, the Excel reports, the CSVs, the BIR filings, the bank file and the QuickBooks journal. Where they used to disagree it was the report that was wrong, never the pay.

head: What to know
Why
rows: Days on the screen means Mon to Fri
Weekend days are in the Sun and Sat columns. The Total Days tile counts everything including weekends, which is why the tile is larger than the Days total. The tile now says so.
Gross includes every allowance
Taxable and de-minimis alike. The tax is still worked out on the smaller taxable base, so gross minus deductions equals net on every surface.
Management EWT is not a deduction
The company pays that withholding on top. It is shown for remittance and marked, never taken off the payee.
Every filing and remittance counts APPROVED runs only, in the month the cut-off ENDS

The QuickBooks journal, the Remittance pack, Government Remittances, Gov monthly, Contributions per employee, the BIR Alphalist, Form 2316 and the 1601-C all count approved (paid) runs only. They put a run in the month, and the year, its cut-off ends. The office 26 Sep – 10 Oct cut-off is October everywhere, and 26 Dec – 10 Jan is filed in January. Each screen says how many drafts it left out, and Contributions per employee names them.
Employer shares are per cut-off
The figure on the line is already the share for that cut-off. The month is the sum of its runs.

note.k: IF YOU DO SEE A MISMATCH
note.t: Say which two screens and which figure. That is a bug worth reporting, not something to reconcile by hand.

sections.h: Which month a payroll run is posted and remitted in
p: A run belongs to the month its cut-off ENDS: it is paid, and SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and tax are deducted, after that date. The Remittance pack, the QuickBooks journal, Government Remittances, Gov monthly, the 1601-C, the BIR Alphalist and Form 2316 all use this one rule, so the same month shows the same SSS on every screen.

Earlier builds put an office cut-off that starts on the 26th in the month it STARTS, in the Remittance pack and the journal only. For the change-over, the pack and the journal show an amber “Month rule changed” box. It names every run that started in the previous month and was FIRST approved before this computer switched to the new rule, and it prints that date. If the previous month was already posted or remitted including that run, leave it out this time. If it was not, include it here.

The box never names a run first approved after the switch, and never one first approved after 1 October 2026, even on a computer used for the first time later. A run approved before the switch, reopened and approved again is still named, because its first approval came first.

note.t: The 26 Aug – 10 Sep office run now sits in September. If August was posted or remitted with it, posting September as it stands counts it twice.

sections.h: BIR Alphalist, Form 2316 and the 1601-C always agree
p: Only APPROVED runs are filed, in the year the cut-off ends. A draft is pay that has not been made yet. The BIR Register still lists drafts, marked “DRAFT — not paid, not filed”.

Taxable compensation is gross pay less the employee SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG, which is exactly the base the tax was withheld on. A taxable + Allowance is inside it: a ₱5,000 House Rental on ₱16,000 a month is taxed ₱282.45 on ₱12,300 and filed as ₱12,300. Non-taxable is the de minimis on the HR card PLUS the de minimis entered with + Allowance. When both are paid, both count.

All three alphalist screens show the same figures: the BIR Center, 📄 Full Alphalist, and Accounting → 📂 Reports → 🧾 BIR Alphalist, which now has a Taxable column too. The BIR Center checks that the alphalist taxable total equals the twelve 1601-C returns. The EWT the company pays on management fees is never counted as tax withheld on compensation.

note.t: Look for drafts. They are no longer counted anywhere a filing is made. Approve the run and it appears.

p: 📑 Contributions per employee lists each person’s SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG, employee and employer shares (EC included), and tax, for any date range. Only APPROVED runs ending in the range count. Any draft ending in the range is named in an amber ⏳ line on the screen and on the Excel sheet, so a total that is lower than an older printout has its reason in writing.
SOURCE “By law from attendance” works the shares out from attendance; tax still comes from approved runs. “Approved payroll runs only” adds up what the approved runs actually deducted.

sections.h: Signing weekend work — which box is yours
p: A Sunday is paid at 130% only after TWO signatures: column 1 is the Accountant, column 2 is Dr Amy or Eyal. Only column 2 makes the day payable.

The ORDER is enforced (v21.46, Eyal): Dr Amy signs column 2 only after the Accountant's ✓ is in column 1 — until then her column is drawn locked and a click says it is still waiting for the Accountant; she never signs column 1. Eyal signs either column at any time, and his final ✓ also fills column 1. The one-click ✓ approve-all, which signs both columns at once, is Eyal's only.

You can only tick the column that is yours. The other one is drawn locked with a padlock and cannot be clicked at all. It used to look exactly like a box you could tick — same tick, same colour — and clicking it quietly refused and left no mark, so it looked as if the screen was losing your ticks. It never lost one: it was never allowed to take them.
A banner at the top of the screen names your column before you start.

Weekend Approvals lists only the days that need a signature. Three kinds of day are not listed, and they are not counted in the banner or by approve-all: a Saturday on a six-day card (an ordinary basic day), a management weekend (never paid), and a fixed-fee engagement (Consultant, Contractor or Advisor). An office employee typed 'Contractual' (fixed-term) IS an employee. Their weekend day is listed and, once both signatures are in, paid at 130%. The amount shown is the rate payroll uses, whichever field holds the monthly basic. Example: ₱16,000/month on the 26 Aug–10 Sep cut-off gives 727.27 × 1.30 = ₱945.45.

head: What you see
What it means
rows: A padlock in a column
Not your signature. Tick the other column.
Save says “nothing to save”
No tick was accepted. You clicked a locked column, or you have not ticked anything yet.
Save says some days still need Dr Amy / Eyal
Your signature is stored, but those days will NOT be paid until column 2 is signed as well.
WAITING FINAL (Dr Amy / Eyal)
The accountant has signed. The money is still not payable.
APPROVED — WILL BE PAID
Both signatures are in and the day's payroll run is still open. Recalculate the period and it pays.
🔒 IN LOCKED RUN <run>

The day is inside a payroll run that is already APPROVED, and ticks on it are refused. 'PAID in that run' means it was signed before the lock and is paid. 'signed after the lock — NOT paid' or 'not payable unless reopened' means the frozen run cannot pay it. An admin reopens that run, or the day is paid as a one-time payment in the next open cut-off.

note.t: Ticks are held until you press 💾 Save. The Save button shows how many changes are waiting, so if it says plain Save, nothing has been ticked.

sections.h: Allowances — read the unit before you save
p: Every allowance row has a unit: per MONTH, PER DAY worked, or — since v21.23 — per MONTH if no missing day (an attendance incentive: paid whole in the cut-off that closes the calendar month, only when the month had no unauthorised absence; lates and approved leave do not break it; the payslip line says why it was or was not paid). The editors also warn when the same allowance row is on a card twice — Jomel’s Meal ₱2,000 sat there three times and paid ₱3,000 a cut-off. Since v21.24 an identical row (same purpose, unit, amount and taxable flag) is counted once by payroll whatever the card holds, and opening the card or the 💰 Allowances editor shows it as one row with a toast; press Save to keep the card clean, then regenerate the run. Per MONTH is prorated; PER DAY is multiplied by every day the person worked, with no ceiling. A ₱2,000 figure meant as a month, typed into a row left on PER DAY, paid ₱22,000 in one office cut-off.
A new row now opens on per MONTH, and the amount box says which unit it is in. Check the drop box on any row you did not create yourself.

Deleting every row now really does stop the allowance. It used to leave the same money being paid from an older hidden field, under a green Saved message — so an allowance that was supposed to end just carried on.

Switching a row between per MONTH and PER DAY now EMPTIES the amount, so type it again in the new unit. Nexi never carries the number across, because ₱2,000 a month read as ₱2,000 a day is ₱22,000 in one office cut-off.

Under the rows, the HR card shows what they pay in one cut-off with full attendance. For office staff that is per month ÷ 2 and per day × 11; for labour it is per month × 6 ÷ 26 and per day × 6. The HR card save, the 💰 Allowances manager and the 📜 Contracts vault ask a second time when a new or changed figure looks like a unit slip: per day above half the daily rate, per day × 22 above a quarter of the monthly basic, or the cut-off total more than doubling. They also ask when an allowance is removed or reduced, and say how much stops being paid per cut-off.

The 💰 Allowances manager will not save a row with no amount: type the amount or remove the row with ✕. The 📜 Contracts vault keeps per-day rows (it used to drop them) and shows them as ₱x/day. Before approval, the anomaly check names any allowance more than 1.5 times its 3-cut-off average, or more than half the basic pay.

A one-time payment dated inside a payroll run that is already approved asks first. OK carries it into the next open cut-off, and the list shows '→ paid <date>'. Cancel saves nothing. If the locked run already paid the same amount, you are warned before a second payment is saved. A labour worker with no attendance in the cut-off it is carried into is still paid it. An office employee or a leaver who is not on that run is named at Approve & Lock (📦): add them with ➕ Add Worker or settle it in Final Pay.

A category cannot be deleted while an entry in a cut-off that is not yet approved still uses it. The message names each of those entries (person, cut-off, amount). An entry whose category was deleted earlier is still PAID and is counted as TAXABLE; the Allowances dialog marks it 'Taxable ⚠'.

note.k: IF AN ALLOWANCE LOOKS FAR TOO BIG
note.t: Check the unit first. PER DAY on an office card is almost always a mistake.

sections.h: + Allowance entries, and the ones Nexi carries forward
p: An entry you type for a cut-off with + Allowance is paid as typed.

When an office cut-off opens with no + Allowance entries at all, Nexi copies in the Transportation and Telecommunication entries from the most recent earlier cut-off. Nothing else is copied. A copied (carried) entry is paid like the HR-card allowance: the amount × the days the person was paid ÷ the scheduled days of the cut-off. ₱1,000 carried to someone paid 6 of 11 days pays ₱545.45. Absent all cut-off pays ₱0. Full attendance pays it in full.
A deletion sticks. Once a cut-off has any + Allowance entry, nothing is carried into it again, and the next cut-off copies from this one without the deleted entry.

The + Allowance window shows each carried entry as entered and, under it, what it pays: “carried · pays ₱545.45 (6 of 11 days paid)”. The Total, Taxable and Non-taxable tiles add up what the run pays. The 💊 Allowance Doctor shows the same under its + Allowance column.

If the Doctor says “entered in an earlier cut-off but NOT in this one”, nothing will bring it back by itself. Add it with + Allowance if it is still due. The Doctor also warns when one person is paid through BOTH the HR card and + Allowance. If it is the same allowance, keep it in one place, or it is paid twice.

sections.h: ⭐ Special payroll — fixed annual tax, no government shares
p: A person on ⭐ Special payroll with an annual basic has a fixed withholding tax: the annual tax ÷ 24 per office cut-off, ÷ 52 per weekly run. The tax stays fixed when an incentive or allowance is added, when a referral bonus is taken off at approval, and when the weekly government refresher updates a draft. ₱300,000 a year withholds ₱312.50 a cut-off; ₱600,000 a year withholds ₱1,201.92 a week.

A person marked gov-exempt pays no SSS, PhilHealth or Pag-IBIG. On the office table those three cells cannot be edited. An override typed anyway is refused, with a message saying why; it used to be saved with “✓ SSS updated” and then ignored. To deduct, untick gov exempt in ⭐ Special payroll first.

Every minute, Nexi checks the DRAFT weekly runs against the current government rules and updates SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG. It uses the same daily rate payroll uses, so the HR card’s Daily Rate Override wins over an old daily rate. When a share changes, the tax, the taxable base, net pay and any uncollected shortfall are worked out again exactly as payroll would, and the run totals follow. Approved runs are never touched. Gov-exempt special payroll and the legacy flat-table mode are skipped.

sections.h: Reading the payslip — de minimis sits above GROSS
p: Everything paid is listed above GROSS PAY, and the rows add up to it: basic, holiday, allowances, and the de minimis (non-taxable) allowance from the HR card and from + Allowance, marked “included in gross”. The tax is still worked out on the smaller taxable base. There is no separate “added after tax” row any more.
Opening a line on the payroll screen shows “💵 Allowances this cut-off (+ Allowance)” with each category. For a carried entry, it also shows how the entry was prorated.

sections.h: SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG cells on the office payroll
p: Clicking into an SSS, PHIC or HDMF cell and out again changes nothing. Typing a different figure makes it an OVERRIDE for that person. It is kept every cut-off, underlined in amber, until their monthly basic changes. It is then retired automatically: the calculated figures for the new salary apply, and the audit log says so. A figure above the employee maximum per cut-off (SSS ₱875, PhilHealth ₱1,250, Pag-IBIG ₱100) asks a second time.

Overrides saved before Nexi recorded which salary they belong to are checked once against the calculated figure. One that EQUALS it is removed, which changes nothing. One that DIFFERS is kept as it is, but it is underlined in RED, the name shows '⚠ old gov override', and the check before Approve & Lock lists it, for example 'SSS override ₱450.00 vs ₱625.00 calculated for the current salary'. Click the badge. OK switches to the calculated figures and tells you how much more or less is deducted per cut-off. Otherwise you can KEEP the old figures for the current salary. The override stays flagged until someone decides.

sections.h: Level rates, promotions and the Pay Basis rate
p: 🎚 Level Rates ▸ Apply to All is for Admin, Admin-Secondary and Accounting. It does not change anyone with a Daily Rate Override or anyone paid a 🩺 Pay Basis Check daily rate. Before applying, it lists every change old → new, per day and per 6-day week, and it logs each one under 💰 Salary / rate changed. The HR chip shows the rate payroll actually pays: the override, then the stored rate, then the Pay Basis rate, then the level.

For someone paid FROM THE LEVEL TABLE (no override, no stored rate, no Pay Basis rate), the level IS the pay. Three things change the daily rate for the open period: a manual promotion, the automatic promotion on the last task sign-off, and a Pro Level change on the HR card. For a manual promotion or an HR-card change, Nexi says so before you confirm. For the automatic promotion it says so in the sign-off message. All three are logged under 💰 Salary / rate changed.

In 🩺 Pay Basis Check, the daily rate you type goes to the field payroll uses, and it also corrects an override or a stored rate. Emptying it asks first, then returns the person to the level table. A change of more than 2× or to less than half asks first and shows the weekly pesos. Every change is logged old → new.

sections.h: A weekend decision now really sticks
p: Rejecting a weekend day with ✗, or clicking a tick again to clear it, used to be write-only. The cloud merge settled a clash between “ok” and “no” by alphabetical order, so an approval always beat a rejection no matter which came later, and a cleared tick was simply put back by the next sync — and payroll then paid the day at 130%.
Every row is now settled by when each signature was actually made, newest wins, and a cleared row leaves a marker so the sync cannot resurrect it. If you reject a day, it stays rejected.

note.k: IF YOU REJECTED A WEEKEND DAY BEFORE AND IT CAME BACK
note.t: That was this. Reject it once more and it will hold.

sections.h: If a tick will not stick at all
p: Under the banner the screen prints who Nexi thinks you are and what it will let you sign, like this: signed in as Jinky Pagtama · role accounting · salary access yes · may sign: 1⃣ Accountant. If a tick never turns green, read that line first and send it to Eyal — it is the whole answer.

Who may sign is decided by the Payroll permission, not by anybody’s name. Anyone who may manage payroll signs column 1. Eyal and Dr Amy sign column 2, exactly as they alone can Approve & Lock a run. Until this was fixed the rule matched a NAME, so Dr Amy’s own level could not sign either column, and an accountant whose record spelled their name differently was locked out of their own job.

note.k: A REFUSED CLICK LEAVES NO MARK
note.t: A tick you are not allowed to make does nothing and turns nothing green. If a box goes green it is accepted and only needs 💾 Save; if it never goes green, it is permission, not the save.

sections.h: The weekend banner on the payroll screens
p: Saturday and Sunday work is only paid once the Accountant and then Eyal or Dr Amy have signed it in HR, Weekend Approvals. Until then the day is neither worked nor absent and no money is attached to it.

head: The banner
What it means
rows: Amber, naming two numbers
Some weekend days in this cut-off are signed and ARE being paid in the Sun and Sat columns. The others are still waiting and are not paid. Both numbers are on the banner.
Solid red
Nothing weekend-related is paid in this run at all. Every weekend day found is still waiting for a signature.
No banner
Nothing is waiting. Whatever shows in the Sun and Sat columns is fully signed.
🔒 grey banner, or a 🔒 line under the red/amber one

Weekend days that were never signed and sit inside an APPROVED run (the run is named). They cannot be signed into it now. Reopen that run, or pay a day that was really worked as a one-time payment. This is decided per person and day: an office Sunday whose office cut-off is still open can still be signed, and ✓ Approve all stays, even when the weekly labour run of the same week is already approved.

note.k: THE BANNER AND THE TABLE ALWAYS AGREE
note.t: The banner counts weekend days by exactly the rule the payroll engine pays them by, so it can never tell you zero while the table below it is paying Sunday or Saturday money.

sections.h: Where the office RATE PER DAY comes from
p: The office rate per day is not a stored number. Payroll works it out for each cut-off: monthly basic, halved, divided by the Mon-Fri working days of that cut-off. A cut-off with 12 working days gives a smaller rate per day than one with 10, and the half-month pay is the same either way. So the rate column genuinely moves from cut-off to cut-off without anybody having changed anything. The divisor is printed in small grey text under every derived rate - ÷ 12 working days - so you can see at a glance which number moved. Rest the mouse on the rate to read the whole sum for that line.

head: What you see
What it means
rows: A rate that changed since last cut-off
Normal. The cut-off has a different number of working days - compare the ÷ N working days line under each rate. The half-month pay is monthly / 2 either way.
A cut-off holding a regular holiday

Fixed in v20.30. A regular holiday is NOT a working day in the divisor: nobody is scheduled to work it and it is paid whether or not they come in, with its pay already inside the half-month. Counting it made the rate too small - 16,000 over the 26 Aug - 10 Sep cut-off read 666.67 instead of 727.27 - and dragged the rest-day 130%, the worked-holiday premium and the tardiness deduction down with it. The divisor line now shows the holiday-free count, with a marker beside it when the cut-off contains one.
A different rate on HR ▸ Weekend Approvals

Fixed in v20.28. That screen used to price every weekend day at half the monthly basic ÷ 11, with the 11 fixed, so on a 12-day cut-off it showed ₱727.27 where payroll paid ₱666.67. It now derives the divisor from the real cut-off and prints ÷ N working days under the amount, the same as payroll.
A weekend day that is also a holiday on HR ▸ Weekend Approvals

The amount includes the holiday premium that signing adds, and the row names the holiday, e.g. “+ National Heroes Day (regular holiday) = 260%”. At ₱727.27/day a Sunday regular holiday shows ₱1,890.90 and a special holiday ₱1,090.90. It used to show only the 130% (₱945.45), half of what signing then paid. A half day is quoted at half. The amount is worked out from the unrounded rate, as payroll does it, so a ÷13 cut-off shows ₱800.00, not ₱799.99.
A rate you never set

If nothing on the card sets a rate, payroll falls back to the TRAINING LEVEL table — level 1 is ₱350 a day — and it used to do that silently. The payroll line now says the rate came from the level table, and 🩺 Pay Basis Check works the rate out the same way payroll does instead of announcing that the person “pays ZERO”.
⚠ beside the rate (and NO ÷ working days line)

That employee has NO Monthly Basic on their HR card, so payroll fell back to the stored daily rate. Their half-month is days x rate instead of monthly / 2, which can overpay. Set Monthly Basic on the card and regenerate the run.
A rate you did not expect at all
Administration ▸ 📜 Audit Log, action 💰 Salary / rate changed. It lists every rate change with the old value, the new value, who made it and when.

note.k: EVERY RATE CHANGE IS NOW RECORDED
note.t: Changing a salary field on an employee card writes an audit line with the old and the new value. Only Admin and Accounting may change one at all, and now even an allowed change leaves a permanent trail.

sections.h: Somebody who started in the middle of a cut-off
p: Payroll pays a person from their Date Hired on the HR card, never before it. Days before the hire date are neither worked nor absent, on both the weekly and the semi-monthly run, and the allowance is prorated to the days that remain. The Days column shows a small blue "new" mark when a line is short for this reason; rest the mouse on it to see the hire date and the day count.

The first day is also never counted as late. A new hire is enrolled on the fingerprint clock some time during their first morning, and that enrolment scan is what the machine reports as the time-in, so it used to read as hours of tardiness that nobody owed.

note.t: All of this depends on Date Hired being filled in on the HR card. If it is blank, payroll pays the whole cut-off. The exception is a person with no history before the cut-off whose first record inside it is a real scan: that scan becomes the start (see 'A new hire mid cut-off'), and Approve & Lock tells you before you sign.

sections.h: The identity checks above Approve & Lock
p: Every run is now checked against sums that must hold whatever the calendar, the salary or the attendance does. Green means all of them tie. Red means a figure on the screen is arithmetically impossible - not merely unusual - and the run should not be locked until it is understood. Amber means the arithmetic is sound but something still needs a decision, most often a weekend day waiting for a second signature.

Each line prints its own sum, so you can read it rather than trust it. RATE - the daily rate times the divisor is half the monthly basic. HALF - somebody present the whole cut-off is paid exactly half the monthly basic. ALLOW - a full cut-off pays exactly half the monthly allowance, so the two halves of a month add up to it. NET - net is gross minus government minus tax, per person. WKEND - every weekend day worked is paid, refused, or counted as waiting. BASIS - nobody is paid with no rate at all. HOLS - a regular holiday is out of the rate divisor.

note.k: WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE ANOMALY CHECK
note.t: The anomaly check compares this run against the last three - it finds the unusual. It cannot see a rate that is wrong for everybody in every cut-off, because nothing stands out. These checks ask the opposite question: is the number possible?

p: A regular holiday is paid whether or not you come in, and that pay is already inside the half-month basic. So somebody who does NOT work it sees nothing extra - the day is simply not an absence. Somebody who DOES work it is paid the premium on top, one further day at the daily rate, shown in the Holiday column.
The holiday is also not a working day for the purposes of the rate. A cut-off with 12 Mon-Fri days one of which is a regular holiday divides the half-month by 11, not 12.

On an office rest day (Sunday, or Saturday on a five-day card), a worked regular holiday is 260% of the daily rate: 130% shows in Sun OT and a further 130% in the Holiday column. It is paid only once the Accountant and then Eyal or Dr Amy have signed it in HR ▸ Weekend Approvals. At ₱727.27 a day that is ₱1,890.90 (it used to be ₱945.45). A special holiday on a rest day is 150% (₱1,090.90). A special working day on a rest day is an ordinary rest day at 130%.

A half day on a regular holiday: the premium is paid on the half worked, and the other half is paid like the unworked holiday (for office staff it is already inside the half-month). ₱16,000/month, 31 Aug half day: ₱8,000.00 + ₱363.64.

Each holiday percentage in ⚖ Holidays accepts 0 to 300 only; anything else is refused. A figure above 100 asks a second time and shows the result. For example, 'extra when worked' 200 means the day + 200% = 300% of the day, which is ₱1,500.00 at ₱500/day. Each holiday line shows what its two boxes add up to. Changing the % for a holiday that falls inside an APPROVED run only takes effect if that run is reopened and regenerated, and Nexi says so.

note.k: THIS IS WHAT MOVED THE RATE
note.t: Before v20.30 the holiday was counted in the divisor, which made the daily rate too small and every figure built on it - rest day, holiday premium, tardiness - too small with it.

sections.h: 📅 Holidays: one shared list, changed only by admin / accounting
p: The 📅 Holidays button on 👷 Labor Payroll and 🏢 Office Payroll opens the government holiday list and the pay rule for each type: the % paid when a holiday is NOT worked, and the extra % paid on top when it IS worked. Payroll reads this list every time it builds a draft run, on every machine. A change here therefore changes the next draft everywhere.

Only admin, admin-secondary and accounting can change it. That covers a % (for a whole type, or in the boxes beside one holiday), ↺ Government defaults, ✕ removing a holiday and ➕ adding one. Everyone else with payroll access sees the list read-only: the boxes are greyed out, the ↺, ✕ and ➕ buttons are not shown, and a 🔒 line says who can change it. Before, anyone with payroll access could press ↺ or remove or add a date, even though the screen said only admin / accounting could change the percentages.

A change now stays, on every machine; the machine that saved last wins. Before, the sync quietly undid corrections: a % lowered from 200 to 100 went back to 200, a removed holiday came back, a cleared per-holiday box filled itself in again, and a holiday changed from special to regular went back to special. The next draft was then priced with the old value. ↺ Government defaults is a dated save too, so another machine’s older % no longer comes back after it.
A new machine builds its list from the government rules. Any date somebody edited, added or removed on another machine wins over that built-in copy on the new machine’s first sync.

'Paid when NOT worked' (Payroll > Holidays). This % is a share of the daily rate for weekly labour only. Office staff on a monthly basic get their full half-month whatever the % is, because the monthly salary already includes holidays. For office, any value above 0 only takes the holiday out of the days used to work out the daily rate; 0 leaves it in as an ordinary paid day. The screen warns in amber if any value is not 0 or 100, because it will move weekly pay but not office pay.

One-time check after this update: open 📅 Holidays once and look at each type's % and the boxes next to each holiday. A value you corrected earlier may have been undone by the old sync. If one looks wrong, type the correct value again and it will stay.

note.t: An approved run keeps what it paid. Press ↻ Recalculate on the open draft. Every machine must be on this version (hard refresh, then check the title bar). A machine on an older version can still put back a date or a % you changed.

sections.h: How a monthly allowance is split across the two cut-offs
p: An office cut-off is half a month, so it pays half the monthly allowance. If somebody was paid for every working day of that cut-off they get exactly half; if they were paid for some of them, they get that share of the half. The two cut-offs of a month therefore add up to exactly the monthly figure, whether the calendar gave that month 10, 11 or 12 working days per half.

Before v20.29 the sum used a fixed 22 instead of the cut-off's own working days. A long cut-off overpaid and a short one underpaid: a ₱4,000 allowance paid ₱2,181.82 in a 12-day half and ₱1,818.18 in a 10-day half, so a month of perfect attendance came to ₱3,818.18. Only an 11-day cut-off was ever right.

note.k: WEEKLY LABOUR IS DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE
note.t: The weekly payroll prorates over a Monday-to-Saturday month (÷26), because that is the labour week. Fifty-two weeks of it make exactly twelve months.

sections.h: Finding an account: the search box and the APAC / APTI buttons
p: The search box looks at everything recorded against an account, not only its name: the notes of its interactions, the wording of its complaints, what an opportunity is for, the purpose of a visit, the contact person and the stage. So a word you remember from a call finds the customer on every tab, not just the Interaction log.

The APAC / APTI buttons narrow to accounts KNOWN to belong to that company. An account is known to belong to one when a case has been raised against it for that company, or when it has SOS orders. A name that is only on the lead list belongs to nobody yet, so it stays on screen under both buttons - it is unknown, not excluded. The count line tells you how many are still unassigned.

note.k: BEFORE v20.34 THE BUTTONS EMPTIED THE SCREEN
note.t: Every untagged account was hidden, and on the real lead book that was all of them: 144 accounts, APAC 0, APTI 0. Raising a case against a customer is what assigns it to a company.

sections.h: A weekend that is signed but not yet paid
p: Weekend work is paid only after BOTH signatures: 1⃣ the Accountant, then 2⃣ Dr Amy or Eyal. Ticking column 1 and pressing 💾 Save stores your signature - it does not yet pay the day. Until the second signature is given, the day is worked, recorded and unpaid.

The payroll Sun column now says so instead of showing a blank: an amber ⏳ with the number of weekend days that are worked and waiting. A plain 0 with no ⏳ means nobody worked that weekend. Rest the mouse on the column to read which it is. The red or amber banner above the table links straight to HR ▸ Weekend Approvals. The amount shown as waiting (the pending column in the Excel and the “up to” figure in Final Pay) is exactly what signing will pay. A half day counts half, and a holiday on the rest day includes its premium. At ₱727.27/day, a whole Sunday regular holiday waits as ₱1,890.90 and a half day of it as ₱945.46.

note.k: IF THE SUNDAY DOES NOT SHOW, LOOK FOR THE ⏳
note.t: ⏳ means your signature saved and the day is waiting for Dr Amy or Eyal. Nothing has been lost, and re-ticking will not change it - the second signature is what pays it.

sections.h: Working a Saturday or a Sunday
p: A weekend is not a scheduled working day, so there is no start time to be late for. Somebody who comes in on a Saturday or a Sunday is doing the company a favour, and payroll now treats the whole day that way: the rest-day premium is paid and no tardiness is raised, however late in the morning the first scan is.

Before this, a Sunday scan at 09:00 was measured against the 07:00 weekday start and arrived in the late queue as 120 minutes. Approving that deduction took money off the same day the premium had just added it.
