sections.h: Why a labourer shows an absence — and how to see which day
p: Hover the red number in Abs (U). It names the days: “No record on: Sat 12 Sep, Wed 16 Sep”. The workbook has the same in its last column, No-record days.

A past day with no record is an absence by rule for weekly labour. But if the person really worked, the scan never reached THIS machine — the coverage strip on the payroll screen (“5/47” on a day means 5 of 47 people have a record) shows it at a glance. A machine with 🚑 STORAGE FULL cannot receive scans at all. Clear it, pull the scans (IT ▸ Biometric Sync), then press ↻ Recalculate.

Today is different. If the run is generated on the cut-off day before the clock’s report for that day has arrived, nobody has a record yet — that is not a day of absences. Payroll now files it as ⏳ today (not counted absent) and the cell says so. Recalculate once the report lands.

note.t: Nothing about a generated run changes on its own. Fix the attendance first, then Recalculate.

sections.h: 📐 The Rulebook — press it before you approve
p: The 📐 Rulebook button on the payroll screen runs the owner’s pay rules on the build you are using, right now, on your machine: the contractor Sunday, the Sunday rest day, the Saturday proof, the late gate (0 → ₱82.25 → 0), the three ⏳ columns, today-not-in-yet, the named absences, the half day, the new hire’s first day. Each rule shows ✓ or ✗ with the expected and the actual number.

It runs on fixtures — your attendance, memos and approvals are neither read nor changed. A ✗ means the build you have breaks a rule: send the line to Eyal before approving. Payroll Doctor section 5 shows the same result.

note.k: THE SAME RULES LIVE IN THE REPOSITORY
note.t: tests/payroll holds these cases as a test suite that must pass before any version ships. The button lets you check that the version that reached your machine is the one that passed.

sections.h: If the Rulebook showed a ✗ on 17 September (v20.72)
p: On the morning of Thursday 17 September the Rulebook reported that the build breaks a pay rule: “A past day with no record is an absence and is named by date”. Nothing was broken and no pay figure was affected. The fault was in the check itself: it blanked whichever day fell second in the week just gone, and on a Thursday that day is a Saturday — a rest day that needs proof, not an absence. The case now names a Monday-to-Friday day, so it reads the same whatever day you press it.
If you saw that ✗ and did not approve a run because of it, you can approve it now. Hard refresh first and check the title bar reads v20.72 or later.

note.t: A checking tool that cries wolf is worse than no tool. This one was caught by the repository suite the moment the calendar turned, before anybody acted on it.

sections.h: A labour day is paid on evidence, every day (v20.71)
p: Jinky reported two construction workers paid 6 and 7 days for 4 worked. The days came from the weekly HR 1/0 sheet: it is filled in advance, and a “1” on a day the person never scanned paid a full day — Sunday included. Until now only Saturday asked for proof.

From v20.71 every labour day follows the Saturday rule. A day pays when there is evidence: clock hours from the biometric machine, a timecard, the attendance sheet from before the clock (history), or a mark made by hand in Nexi, which carries the name of the person who made it. A bare sheet mark or an app-made placeholder with no hours and nobody’s name is not paid.

A Timecard (NGTeco) row with both Clock In and Clock Out blank is not imported. A stored present or late row with no clock time and nobody's name is refused the same way; it is counted under 'no proof', Sunday included. Re-uploading a Timecard file never overwrites a mark a person made: a day saved by hand, or edited or given a reason in Reconcile, stays as it is ('sent home' stays absent). The toast counts the 'person-decided mark(s) preserved'. Fill from Timecards reads a leave word (VL, SL, Leave…) only on a row with no clock times, and never reads 'Early Leave' as leave. So 'Late, Early Leave' on a worked day stays a worked late day, and a row with no times and no absence or leave word is skipped. A nameless HR-sheet VL/SL on a labour Sunday is the rest day, not paid leave; a leave saved by hand with a name still pays. Weekday leave is unchanged.

Where to see it: hover the Days cell on the weekly payroll — it lists every paid day with its hours and where it came from (clock, timecard, HR sheet, by hand) and, in amber, the days refused for want of proof. The Doctor’s DAY AUDIT names them; the workbook has two new columns at the end (Days paid (source), Not paid: no proof); the Attendance Matrix paints such a day “no scan” in amber.
If a refused day was really worked: open the day in Attendance and save it, or set it in the Matrix — a hand mark carries your name and pays. Then ↻ Recalculate.
Office pay is unchanged: office staff do not scan and an unmarked office day is paid, as before.

note.t: A run generated before v20.71 keeps its sheet-mark days. Press ↻ Recalculate on the open week, then check the Days tooltips before approving.

sections.h: What the sync audit fixed (v20.99) — approved runs and holiday changes survive the sync
p: An APPROVED run can no longer disappear. Before, pressing ↻ Recalculate or ➕ Add Worker, adding or deleting an allowance, or changing or resetting a government deduction on a machine that had not yet received the approval deleted the run. It also left a delete marker. The sync then removed the approved run on every machine, and the period came back as a fresh DRAFT with no approver and no history. That draft could be approved, and paid, a second time.

Now those buttons re-price the draft where it stands and never delete it. The run keeps its created date, its reopen stamp and its history, and the sync never removes an approved run. Only 🔓 Reopen takes a run out of APPROVED.
An allowance you add to or delete from an office line reaches the saved draft straight away, so Approve & Lock always locks the figures you see.
Holiday % and holiday dates now stay changed on every machine, and only admin / accounting can change them. See 📅 Holidays: one shared list.

note.t: A machine still on an older version keeps writing the old delete marker when someone presses Recalculate there, and on that machine an approved run can still vanish. Check the title bar on every machine that opens payroll.

sections.h: What the chain audit fixed (v20.70) — locks, sync and who may change what
p: 🔓 Reopen and ↻ Recalculate now survive the next sync. Before, the first draft render after a reopen dropped the reopen stamp, and any other machine that still held the approved copy re-locked the run with the OLD figures within a minute — the “I reopened it and it locked itself again” report. If you saw that, reopen once more on v20.70 and it stays open. From v20.99 a Recalculate made on a machine that had not yet received an approval can no longer delete the approved run either. See What the sync audit fixed (v20.99).

Approve & Lock warns about everything still waiting, not only lates: memos not yet signed (⏳ Memo), office weekends not yet signed (⏳ Sun OT) and delivery days not yet final-approved (🚚 Trip Incentives). Press Cancel, get the signatures, Recalculate, then lock. The check before signing also names money carried into this cut-off for anyone who is not on the run (📦), and it refuses to lock figures that no longer match the attendance on file.
The tardiness policy switch (DEDUCTED / WARNING ONLY) now sticks across machines. Before, once one machine had DEDUCTED the others could never turn it off.

Deleting a memo, undoing a late memo, or clearing an attendance day (✕ Clear in Attendance, the Matrix cycle, the payroll-line editor) now stays deleted on every machine. Before, the other machine’s copy brought it back within a minute — including any deduction on it.

A correction you make in the Matrix or the payroll-line editor now carries a time stamp, so the other machine’s older “present” cannot overwrite it. If a day you corrected kept flipping back, this was why.

Who may change what: pay rates on Pay Basis Check need payroll edit rights (accounting / admin); the late-approval policy (on/off, ignore-under, scope) is for Eyal and Dr Amy; a memo needs two DIFFERENT people’s signatures — the same account cannot sign as Supervisor and as HR Manager.

Outputs: the payroll-line modal prints the same Gross as the table and the payslip; the printed payslip no longer lists the company-paid EWT of management as a deduction; the Combined workbook’s GRAND TOTAL now includes NET PAY (it printed 0.00).

note.t: Two policy questions are yours, Eyal: (a) “🌐 All departments” and a Payroll department assignment currently grant payroll EDIT to any role — is that intended? (b) The per-user “Specific actions” toggles for payroll are stored but not enforced anywhere. Also pending: clock-skew-proof stamps (a machine whose clock runs ahead still wins ties) and the storage-full machine pushing its stale copy — both need a sync-layer change and are scheduled next.

sections.h: What the chain audit fixed (v20.69) — the screens now say what payroll does
p: Nothing in v20.69 changes a pay figure. It changes every place that described a figure differently from the engine.

Office table and office CSV: the ⏰ tardy note sits under Basic when a signed late was deducted, and the CSV carries Late Mins, Tardy Ded, the three ⏳ pending columns and the uncollected shortfall — the same columns as the Excel workbook. “Late min” on the workbooks and the weekly CSV is now the DECIDED minutes, the same number the screen prints beside the deduction (before, it printed every late minute of the cut-off, waiting and excused included).

Uncollected shortfall: when net hits zero (a whole week absent while SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG are still charged) the part that could not be taken shows in red under Net on the row, on the payslip and printed slip, in the CSVs and as “Uncollected” in the workbooks. The remittance pack still claims that share — collect it deliberately on a later cut-off.

Payslip: the allowance line prints the basis payroll really used — ÷ 26 × Mon–Sat days worked for labour, monthly ÷ 2 × scheduled days for office. A signed peso penalty prints as “signed peso penalty”, not “0 mins”.

Attendance Matrix: a day stored as present but carrying late minutes is painted as the late it is (payroll charges it, the queue lists it). A labour Sunday with no scan is a “Sun rest” cell, not a red ✗ — payroll never counts it absent.

Attendance screen: the Pending line says what payroll does with the day — rest day on a Sunday, “paid only with proof” on a Saturday, absent Mon–Fri for weekly labour. A Sunday is never Late. A late the clock-in implies but the record does not carry shows “+30min · not queued”: open the day and Save to put it in the Eyal / Dr Amy queue.

Reconcile ✓ Approve and Accept All: when Eyal or Dr Amy press it, a late that is still WAITING is EXCUSED in the queue (no deduction). A late they have already decided is never changed from Reconcile. That includes a signed deduct whose time-in was corrected afterwards (⚠ RE-DECIDE). In those cases ✓ Approve says 'Already decided' or 'Re-decide it in HR ▸ Late approvals' instead of 'Excused', and the Accept All confirm counts how many stay as signed. When anyone else presses it, the screen says the late still waits for the approvers in HR ▸ Late approvals.
Biometric Sync: a scan day you tagged in Reconcile at noon still receives its evening OUT punch. A status you decided (absent, authorized) is never touched by the clock.

note.t: A run generated before v20.69 shows the old columns in its CSV until you regenerate it. The pay is the same.

sections.h: What the chain audit fixed (v20.68) — regenerate any run that touches these
p: A SPECIAL holiday (21 Aug, 1–2 Nov, 8 Dec, 24 and 31 Dec, Black Saturday, Chinese New Year, EDSA) is no-work-no-pay: it is an ordinary scheduled day. It used to be taken out of the rate divisor while the day was still paid, so every office and management line on such a cut-off was one day over — 16,000 a month paid 8,800 instead of 8,000. A special day that IS worked now pays the day plus its +30% (8,218.18), never less than an unworked one. Regular holidays are unchanged: paid unworked, inside monthly/2.

An office absence YOU mark — in Attendance (✕ Absent) or Reconcile (“sent home”) — deducts, even on a day that had a scan. Only an absent the machine or an import wrote on its own is still paid as an office day. The Matrix and the Payroll Doctor show the same.

A leaver you flagged inactive with the 🚫 override is paid up to the Last Working Day on the card, exactly like a status of Inactive. If the card has no date, the day the override was set is the last day.
A card marked six-day week: Saturday is an ordinary basic day (÷13 and paid), not a weekend needing a signature.
A management run generated before a regular holiday in the cut-off pays the holiday once, not twice — you no longer need to wait for the holiday to pass before generating.
🔓 Reopen and ↻ Recalculate give back a referral bonus the locked run had paid, so the draft still carries it; approving again marks it paid.

Biometric Sync: five or more people scanning in the SAME minute at the gate keep their in-scan. Before, that minute was mistaken for a timetable column and dropped, and each of them was filed as late from 07:00 to their out-scan (⏳ in the late queue). A timetable time is only ignored when it repeats on three pulled days.
Timecard bridge: a row with an out-time but no in-time is no longer a silent 07:00 present day — it is measured from the out-time and waits in the late queue like any missing morning scan.
➕ Add Worker / Add Employee only offers people who belong on that run: labour on the weekly run, office on the semi-monthly run.

note.t: A run generated before v20.68 keeps its old figures. Any cut-off with a special holiday, a hand-marked office absence, an override leaver or a six-day card: press ↻ Recalculate, check the Doctor, then approve.

sections.h: Where the Excel and CSV exports are
p: 📑 Full Report (Excel) and 📄 CSV (plain data) sit on the payroll screen itself, next to the period bar — they never fold away. Every other tool is inside 🗂 All payroll tools… at the top of the screen.
The Excel workbook carries the same columns as the screen, including the three ⏳ awaiting-approval columns after NET PAY.

note.t: The export prints the run as it was generated. If you changed a rate, approved a late or marked a day since, press ↻ Recalculate first, then export.

p: Both payroll tables and both workbooks now carry three amber columns after Memo−: ⏳ Late, ⏳ Memo and ⏳ Sun OT. Each is money that is DONE but NOT YET APPROVED — a late still waiting for Eyal or Dr Amy, a memo still in draft or pending, an office weekend scanned but not signed. The figure is what it will be worth once approved. None of it is in Gross or Net.

Accounting reads the column, chases the signature, and regenerates the run after it arrives. ⏳ Late held shows the whole day(s) withheld while Eyal or Dr Amy decide; a pending Sunday shows the 130%; a pending memo shows its amount whichever way it will move.

note.t: A labour Sunday needs no signature — it pays flat from the scan — so ⏳ Sun OT is always — on the weekly table. Only office weekends wait for approval.

p: A construction worker whose employment type is Contractor is weekly labour: every day he scans is a paid day, Sunday included, flat. The consultant rule (a fixed-fee office consultant is never paid for a weekend scan) applies to office payroll only. Until v20.61 the word “contract” in his type matched that rule and his Sunday was filed as a rest day — paid 6 for a 7-day week while the matrix showed 7.

note.t: A run generated before v20.61 keeps the old count. Regenerate it and the Sunday comes back.

sections.h: Why a week can pay one day short — and how to check
p: Add the row up: Days + Sun + Sat + Hol + Abs (U) + Abs (A) should equal the days in the period. If it comes to one less, a day landed in no column at all, and that is always worth reporting. A ½ Half day is the one honest exception: it counts as half a day under Days and the other half was simply not worked, so the row comes to half a day short and that is not a missing day - since v20.65 the Doctor knows this and no longer reports it as one.

The commonest cause was a SATURDAY. For weekly labour Saturday is an ordinary working day, but it is only paid when there is proof somebody was there: real clock hours, or a person marking the day by hand with their name on it. A Saturday that exists only as a generated placeholder is not paid — and until v20.59 it was not even shown, so the row simply came up short.

Press 🩺 Payroll Doctor on the payroll screen. Section 4, the DAY AUDIT, checks every line of the run and names anybody whose days do not add up, and anybody whose Saturday was refused for want of proof. A run generated before v20.59 has to be regenerated before it can be audited.

note.k: IF A SATURDAY WAS REALLY WORKED
note.t: Mark it in Attendance ▸ Reconcile — a day you mark carries your name and counts as proof — then regenerate the run. A payroll run is a frozen snapshot and will not pick it up on its own.

sections.h: The Attendance Matrix shows who is waiting for your approval
p: A late day prints the real clock hour and, underneath it, where the approval stands. The background stays GREEN whatever the state: a late is never an absence.

⏳ waiting — a dashed amber frame. Nobody has decided yet, and the whole day is HELD (not paid) until Eyal or Dr Amy do. ✓ excused — green frame, the day pays whole. ➖ deduct or ₱ penalty — red frame, money comes off. ✗ not paid — the day is withheld for good. ⚠ warning — recorded in the 201 file, no money.
The badge appears only for lates that are genuinely in Eyal and Dr Amy’s queue — it is drawn from the same scan the approval screen uses, so the grid and the queue can never disagree.

Uploading the HR attendance workbook (the 1/0 sheet) never overrules the clock: a day that already carries clock hours, a late or somebody’s name is left exactly as it is, and the sheet only fills days that have nothing else. A day the sheet flattened before this is put right by the next biometric pull, which re-applies the real scan.

note.t: ✗ means there is NO attendance record for that day, so payroll counts it absent (weekly labour). Hover it: the tooltip says whether it is a missing record or somebody marked the person absent by hand. A very late scan that has not synced yet also reads as ✗ until it lands — the record, not the hour, is what is missing.

sections.h: Reading the Days column — why 7 days can print as 6
p: The Days column deliberately leaves out the days the Sun and Sat columns already show, so the row can be read across without counting the weekend twice. A labour worker with seven days including a Sunday prints as Days 6 · Sun 1. He is paid for seven — Basic Pay covers all of them.
Check it on the sheet: Basic Pay ÷ Daily Rate is the number of days actually paid. 4,606.00 ÷ 658.00 = 7, on the row that shows Days 6.

For office staff, the day trace now says what payroll does. A day with no mark, a pending day or a nameless imported absent is 'office day: PAID'. An unworked special holiday is 'paid as an ordinary office day'. The Days figure in the trace matches the engine, for example 11 days = ₱8,000 on ₱16,000/month for 26 Aug–10 Sep.

note.k: WHEN A DAY IS GENUINELY MISSING
note.t: Add Days + Sun + Sat + Hol + Abs (U) + Abs (A). It should equal the days in the period. If it comes to one less, that day has NO attendance record at all — and for weekly labour no record counts as absent. Fix it in Attendance ▸ Reconcile and regenerate the run.

sections.h: A new hire’s first day is never a late
p: The clock enrols a new person some time during their first morning and reports that as their time in, so the first scan on or after the hire date — within the first two weeks — is never treated as a late. After two weeks the rule stops: a late on the first day the store still holds for somebody hired long ago is a real late.

note.t: The store does not keep attendance for ever. Without the limit, a person hired years ago whose old records had been cleared could have a late forgiven on the first day still kept.

sections.h: Late and undertime — what they cost
p: A late day is a FULL day. It is never an absence: the person came to work. Only a day with no attendance record at all is an absence, and that rule is for weekly labour — on office payroll an unmarked day is paid.

The late minutes are recorded on the day and shown in the Late min column, but nothing is deducted by the machine. Every late after 07:00 waits for Eyal or Dr Amy to decide: excuse it, deduct the minutes, set a peso penalty, or record a warning with no money. While it waits, the whole day is HELD: the Tardy column carries the withheld day and says “n held”, and it is paid in the next cut-off once decided (whole if excused, minus the minutes if deducted, never if NOT PAID). A half day is held at half a day. NOT PAID also withholds that day’s allowance share.

Until Eyal or Dr Amy decide, the day is HELD: the whole day comes off the run (the payslip shows “1 held” beside the tardiness line) and the Approve & Lock check says how many days are held. Nobody else — not HR, not the guard, not the employee’s own explanation — can release it; that is Dr Amy’s memo to the security agency of 2 Oct 2026 in Nexi. Once Eyal or Dr Amy approve DEDUCT, the day still counts as a full day, and the approved minutes come off the pay: 60 minutes on a ₱658 day is 60 ÷ 480 × 658 = ₱82.25. The signed decision keeps the minutes it was signed for. HR may later correct the record so it shows FEWER minutes, for example a forgotten morning scan fixed to 07:30. Payroll then takes the smaller figure: 30 ÷ 480 × 658 = ₱41.13, not the ₱411.25 for the signed 300 minutes. The row goes back to HR ▸ ⏰ Late approvals under Waiting with a ⚠ RE-DECIDE note. If the record grew instead, only the signed minutes are taken. Either way the row waits for a fresh decision. It is counted in the payroll banner and in the Approve & Lock check, and it is decided one row at a time on Late approvals. The bulk buttons and Reconcile never change a signed decision. The deduct buttons quote the same daily rate payroll uses. A run already generated is a frozen snapshot, so regenerate it after deciding.

Leaving early is not deducted automatically at all. The fingerprint scanner captures the undertime minutes, but payroll does not read them. If only half a day should be paid, mark it with the ½ Half day button in Attendance ▸ Reconcile. That writes a real half day and is the only thing that reduces the day. To undo it, untick ½ Half day in the Attendance day window or set Time Out to 17:00 or later.

title: Harvest — from SOS to the packaging logbook
summary: Every harvest is a purchase order received into APAC CENTER COLD STORAGE in SOS. The packaging logbook is the hall’s own count and must match SOS exactly.

p: SOS Inventory (APAC account) → the item receipt of the harvest purchase order. Each line: Class “Aba Pardes Harvesting per GH:APAC GH4” → GH4; item “Curly Red Frisee B W & T” → variety Curly Red Frisee B, grade W&T (washed & trimmed); quantity → kg; lot “CRFB10012026-33” → harvest day 1 Oct 2026, lot 33. A line without a readable lot date takes the receipt date.

⟳ Pull from SOS asks the hnx-sync worker for the receipts of the period on screen (it keeps what was pulled before, so the screen also opens offline). If the worker answers “route not found”, the admin has not pasted workers/hnx-sync-itemreceipts-snippet.js yet — Step 4 of the pending list. Nothing here writes to SOS.

Period: Day · Week · Month · Quarter · Year, with ‹ › and a date box. 📊 Overview: total kg, greenhouses, varieties, receipt lines, open logbook differences; the greenhouse × variety matrix in kg; the trend by harvest day. 🏠 Per greenhouse and 🥬 Per variety rank them with their share. 🧾 Receipts lists every line with its lot, class and location.
Production sees the same screen under 🌱 Production → 🌾 Harvest (kg per greenhouse for the agronomy side); Packaging owns the logbook.

Packaging / Production managers add one line per day, greenhouse and variety: crates and kg (type the variety as SOS names it — the box suggests the names seen in SOS). Nexi lays the logbook next to the SOS receipt for the same day + GH + variety.

Eyal’s rule (1 Oct 2026): the two must match EXACTLY. A line that differs — or exists only in SOS, or only in the logbook — shows red until a reason is written in the Reason box (the box is red while empty). An explained difference turns amber; a match is green. Every reason goes to the audit log.

The Report tab writes the period’s report: total, per greenhouse, per variety, the matrix, and the logbook differences still unexplained. 📊 Excel (four sheets: matrix, by day, receipt lines, logbook vs SOS), 🖨 Print, 📧 Send now through nexi-notify to @abapardes.com.ph addresses.
Type the recipients once in the Report tab: on the 1st of each month (first three days, first device of a manager that opens Harvest) the previous month’s report is e-mailed to them by itself.

title: Meetings & decisions
who: Everyone who runs a meeting · Eyal · Edelyn · Cherie · Jinky
summary: One meeting record for the whole company: minutes on one template, decisions with approval, action items that become tasks on the owner’s My Day and report back to the minutes. Sub-tab 🎙 Meetings in CRM, Production, Projects and Accounting.

steps: Production ▸ 🎙 Meetings → ＋ New meeting. Pick the template (Customer, Internal/management, Supplier, Site visit, Bank/agency, Production), the title, date and place.
Link the record it is about: type a lead, customer or compliance case name and pick it from the list. The link is kept on every task that comes out of the meeting.
Tick the Nexi users attending; type external attendees one per line as “Name (role)”. Chair = the person who approves decisions.
Write the purpose (what must be decided) and the agenda, one item per line.

p: Type in “Notes taken during the meeting”, or press 🎤 Dictate (uses the browser’s speech recognition, or Cloud speech when IT has set it up). Mark lines with D: for a decision, A: for an action (“A: send the agreement — Edelyn — 2026-10-02”), Q: for a question. ✂ Sort notes moves them into the right section of the minutes; what is left becomes discussion points.

Only CRM managers and admins see 🔴 Record. Add the attendees first: before anything is recorded, Nexi lists them and asks you to confirm that EACH one agreed — recording a private conversation without everyone’s consent is a crime in the Philippines (RA 4200). Your confirmation, the time and the list of people are written on the meeting record.

While recording, the microphone is cut into 20-second pieces. Each piece is transcribed by the speech worker and appears in the Transcript box with its time, and the audio piece goes to the cloud archive — never into the browser. Press the D / A / Q / ★ markers when something important is said; they are kept with their time for the minutes.

If the line drops, pieces wait on this computer and are retried every 15 seconds until they go through — the status line shows “waiting”. ⏹ Stop ends the recording; the last pieces finish in the background. ▶ next to a transcript line plays that piece back; 🔍 finds a word in the transcript, and the meetings list search also looks inside transcripts.

The audio is deleted by itself 90 days after the recording (an admin can press 🗑 Delete the audio now); the transcript stays with the minutes. Needs: Cloud speech set up under IT → Voice Status, and cloud sync signed in on the recording computer.

✨ Draft minutes with AI sends the transcript — or the typed notes when there is no recording — with the meeting header to the Nexi AI brain and fills the skeleton: summary, discussion points with their [mm:ss], decisions as PROPOSED, action items, open questions, risks, the template’s section and the next meeting. Existing text is kept; the draft is added under it.

Action owners are matched to Nexi users from the attendee list. An owner the model could not match shows in orange with the name as said — pick the user. A due date is filled only when it was said in the meeting; the model never guesses one.

The draft is a proposal: a person reviews it, fixes it and presses 💾 Save. The model cannot approve a decision, publish a task or send minutes. Needs the Nexi AI brain set up on this device (⚙ TOOLS → Nexi AI brain).
One skeleton for every meeting: summary, discussion, decisions, action items, the template’s own section (commercial terms, documents requested…), risks, open questions, next meeting.

Decisions start as PROPOSED. Only the chair, the organiser or an admin can mark one approved, rejected or superseded, and that is written to the audit log. Approving a decision in the minutes never approves a price, a payment, stock or a permit — those keep their own approvals in their own modules.

Every action item needs one owner (a Nexi user), a due date and, ideally, the outcome that closes it (“the signed agreement is in Files”). An owner the notes could not match shows in orange with the name as typed — pick the user.

✅ Publish actions as tasks creates ONE task per action through the company Tasks engine: on the owner’s My Day, module of the meeting, visibility team, linked back to the meeting and to the customer or case. Publishing twice never creates a second task.

The minutes show each task live (to do / doing / blocked / done / overdue) and the header counts “3 of 5 actions done”. Changing the owner, due date or text on the minutes updates the task. A published action is closed through its task, not deleted here.
The owner presses ✓ Accept on the action (or works it from My Day). A task opened from My Day that came from a meeting opens these minutes.

🖨 Print internal prints the full minutes with task status. ✉ Send internal mails the full text through nexi-notify to the attending users’ @abapardes.com.ph addresses (set up under HR ▸ memo SMS); without the worker it opens a mail draft instead.

📨 External copy → mail draft leaves out the internal sections (the template’s extra section, risks, task status) and opens a draft in your mail program: you check the recipients and send it yourself. Each send is a numbered revision; a later edit becomes the next revision, the way a corrected PDF would.

↪ New follow-up meeting opens a new record for the same customer and attendees with every PROPOSED decision and every action whose task is not done. They keep their ids and their task — nothing is copied, so the history stays in one place.

The list shows, per meeting, decisions still proposed, actions done / overdue / not published, and whether the minutes were sent. “Open follow-up” hides meetings whose minutes were sent and whose actions are all done.

sections.h: Where the earlier CRM meetings went
p: The meetings typed on a lead’s card before v21.29 are imported once into the new list (template Customer, linked to the lead, decisions marked approved as they were). Nothing on the lead card was removed.

title: Accounting — Loyalty Savings
summary: The APTI loyalty savings plan (BDO Short Term Fund UITF) kept in Nexi: each employee’s portion of the fund month by month, the interest earned, and the months still to fund. Replaces the audit workbook.

p: Every payroll screen anywhere in Nexi — the Payroll module, payroll views inside Accounting, 🩺 Pay Basis Check, 🚚 Trip Incentives, 💰 Final Pay, 13th month, payslips, salary and Loyalty Savings — opens only for Jinky, Eyal, Dr Amy and the System Admin login. Other users, including other admin-role users and HR, do not see them in the menu and get a 🔒 message if they try another way. Access overrides cannot open them.

Loyalty Savings and every payroll screen (also the ones opened from Accounting) are visible ONLY to the System Admin, Jinky, Eyal and Dr Amy. Every other user — also Accounting users such as Joshane, and secondary admins — gets a 🔒 message and no employee amounts. Access overrides in Administration cannot open it for anyone else.

Since v21.26 the monthly amount is typed by Accounting on the employee's HR card (💰 Loyalty savings ₱/month) and the card is the source: the member here takes the card's amount, an employee given an amount becomes a member from the current month, a cleared card closes the membership at the end of last month. Payroll books the amount once a month as an EMPLOYER payable on the cut-off that ends on the 25th, exactly like the SSS employer share (never deducted from the employee); the Overview shows whether that run is approved, and 🏛 Government Remittances carries a “Loyalty savings — BDO” card with the month's total to deposit.

Every month the company sets aside a fixed amount per member (the monthly entitlement — ₱10,000 / ₱10,000 / ₱2,000 today). The amounts are remitted together to BDO by voucher and check, and BDO buys units of the Short Term Fund at that day’s NAVPU (the confirmation, COP, states the NAVPU and the units). Each employee owns a share of every remittance equal to their contribution ÷ the remittance, so they own that share of the units bought. Worth today = units × the latest NAVPU; interest = worth − contributions. The value moves with the NAVPU and can go down in a period (Mar→Apr 2026 did).

sections.h: Every month, Accounting does three things
steps: Months & remittances: type what was funded for each employee that month (blank = not funded; a partly funded month shows in amber).

+ Remittance / UITF purchase: the voucher date, check number and amount, and, when the COP arrives, its date, number, NAVPU and units (leave units blank to compute amount ÷ NAVPU). One remittance can cover two months (Aug–Sep 2025 did).

NAVPU history → + NAVPU: the month-end statement. Type the NAVPU if the statement prints it, or just the statement’s total value — Nexi divides it by the units held. The latest point values the whole fund and every employee statement. No bank connection is involved: these three entries are the whole monthly routine.

p: Overview: cash remitted, value at the latest NAVPU, earnings, units, outstanding; per employee their contributions, share of the fund, units, value, interest and what is still due; the fund by remittance.

Employee statement: pick the employee — what is saved for them, what it is worth today, their interest, their share of the fund, then every remittance with their contribution, share, entry NAVPU, units, worth and interest. 🖨 Print gives the employee a statement; ⬇ CSV exports it.
Members: name, link to the HR record, monthly entitlement, from / to month, active. Outstanding is counted from each member’s From month; the current month is due but not yet late.

sections.h: Where the opening figures came from
p: The first open seeds the 28-Sep-2026 BDO audit workbook: Aug-2025 → Jun-2026, 10 remittances, ₱219,000 remitted, 1,689.1159 units, NAVPU 132.0663 on 14-Sep-2026, ₱89,000 outstanding to Sep-2026 (Jul–Sep unfunded for all three, Taladtad short in Feb–Apr). Correct anything from the vouchers; the workbook stays the audit trail.

title: Accounting & Purchasing
summary: Comparing suppliers before buying, and the purchasing workflow behind a purchase order.

p: Every RFQ sent by ✉ Email or 📱 SMS ends with: reply to ATERETPAZ TECHNOLOGIES INC. — Accounting, mobile 09778572212, accounting@abapardes.com.ph. The SMS is a short version (items, need-by date, delivery point) so the contact line is never cut off. Since v21.79 the text says in capitals to reply ONLY to that number / e-mail, and every 📱 SMS also opens WhatsApp with a copy addressed to the Accounting number 09778572212 — press Send there so Accounting has the record.

sections.h: Committed drop-off point on an offer (v21.77)
p: A request can carry a fixed drop-off point (e.g. GH15 sand + gravel: “Side of GH15 ONLY — not the road, not anywhere else”). Each offer then has a red tick box “Supplier COMMITS drop-off”. Until it is ticked, the apple-to-apple table flags the offer “drop-off NOT committed” and cuts its score by 20%, and 🏆 Award is refused. Tick it only when the supplier has confirmed in writing and attach that confirmation as the offer file.

The canvas sheet of 6 Oct 2026 (4 suppliers, 8 options) is already loaded as PR-GH15-SAND and PR-GH15-GRAVEL at Quotation Evaluation. Every option is shown as the price for 12 m³, so truck packages that deliver more (16–18 m³) are compared on what you pay for 12.

Every Accounting screen that reads QuickBooks (dashboard snapshot, the five 12-month matrices, cash-flow, the FS auto-fill, bank reconciliation, customers) now goes through the nexi-qb worker, the same link Administration → Sales Intelligence uses. Nothing to set up on a device that already has that link; a device without it keeps using the old bridge until the admin enters the link.

If QuickBooks does not answer, Nexi waits 10 minutes before asking for that report again and never asks for the same report twice at once, so a broken link can no longer flood the worker. A screen that shows “waiting 10 minutes” is that guard, not a lost connection.

sections.h: 🏗 Assets — the 2026 lapsing recon and the JEs (v21.22)
p: Accounting → 🏗 Assets → ➕ New Asset. The 28-Sep-2026 lapsing schedule is built in: press “Load the 28-Sep-2026 lapsing schedule” once and its 34 assets are registered (₱10.1M). Importing a newer version of the schedule with ⬆ Choose Excel file updates the rows already registered (matched by PO# or by description + cost) and adds the new ones; nothing is doubled.

The recon summary at the top counts every asset acquired this year by where its purchase sits in QuickBooks: ✓ fixed-asset account (only the depreciation entries are needed), booked as inventory or as expense (post JE 1 to reclassify it from that account to the asset’s cost account), or not in QB at all (post JE 1 to record it). Each asset’s package below lists the accounts to open, JE 1, JE 2 catch-up depreciation to the last month-end and the recurring monthly JE; the file’s own monthly amortization and months depreciated are shown beside Nexi’s figures for the cross-check.

Supplier 360° opened from a request (v21.55) lists the purchases that match the item first — 🎯 Relevant to this request — and says when the supplier never sold us that kind of item; other purchases are folded below.

Supplier Sourcing (v21.54) shows only suppliers that fit the item — a past purchase of a similar product, a matching Category on the vendor card (e.g. Construction materials), or the item words in the supplier name — then Nexi's own web-found suggestions for that item family marked WEB · VERIFY (phone them first; ➕ save to suppliers keeps the one you pick), an inline ➕ Add supplier with a category, and every unrelated vendor folded under Other known suppliers. Give each vendor a Category so the right ones surface next time.

On the 🛒 Purchasing request form the Department is a drop-down of every department — Construction, Projects, Purchasing, R&D, Compliance, Administration and Safety included (v21.53); the eight workflow tabs stay on screen and never fold into an All tools picker.

🛒 Purchasing is built around a 3-supplier comparison: log the product, add up to three quotes with unit, specification and quantity, and the comparison is there in writing when the decision is questioned later.

Apple to apple (v21.64). Purchasing (Joshane) logs each supplier's offer at the RFQ stage of the request — ➕ Log offer on the supplier row: quantity offered, unit price, VAT included or not, delivery charge, brand / spec, valid until, lead days, payment terms, warranty, notes and the offer itself (photo or PDF). The total is computed, never typed. ➡ Proceed to evaluation then shows every offer on the same footing: normalised to the request's quantity, VAT-exclusive, delivery included — ₱ per unit landed and the total for the quantity needed — with the gap against the cheapest in ₱ and %, lead time against the need-by date, flags when an offer is for fewer units, a different spec, expired, late or has VAT still to add, the supplier's record (RFQs answered, deliveries on time) and a score out of 100. Weights (price, lead time, terms, record) are editable and saved; ⬇ Excel comparison files it; the award stage pre-selects the best score and choosing another supplier needs a written reason.

Accounting ▸ 🛒 Purchasing is the only purchasing module. Its tabs: 🎯 Mission Control, 📝 Purchase Requests, 📥 From Inventory, 📨 RFQs, 📄 Purchase Orders, 📦 Receiving, 🧾 Invoices, 🧰 Suppliers & tools (the former Quick Tools: comparisons, SOS purchase history, supplier master, outreach), 🏭 Scorecard and 📈 Analytics. Quick Tools is no longer a separate sidebar entry.

📥 From Inventory lists the purchase needs raised elsewhere — Inventory ▸ 📝 Requests of type Purchase and 🛒 Purchase Engine draft POs. ➡ Make Purchase Request turns one into a Purchase Request here (already Submitted, linked both ways); approval, sourcing, offers, the PO and receiving then happen in Purchasing, never in Inventory.

Who may change things: creating, submitting, advancing, RFQs, offers, receipts and invoices need Accounting or Purchasing EDIT (or the Purchasing department / manageInventory); approving, awarding and issuing a PO stay with the Purchasing / Accounting managers and Admin. Everyone else can read.

Local or import (v21.65). Supplier Sourcing first decides the kind of item. A local material — cement, gravel, sand, hollow blocks, rebar, lumber, plywood, concrete pipes, fuel, nails, paint, PVC, sacks, crates… — shows only suppliers near the farm; importing makes no sense, so overseas suppliers and Alibaba are not offered. An item we imported before (the purchase history or the supplier card says Alibaba, China, import, Israel, Netherlands…), or an import kind of item (NFT pipes, grow lights, rockwool, EC / pH meters, dosing), shows 🌏 Imported before — our overseas suppliers for that item family — first, then links to search Alibaba, Made-in-China and 1688 for new ones (add the one you find with category Import), with local alternatives below. Anything else shows local suppliers first and Alibaba as a check. The dropdown on the banner overrides the decision for that item and Nexi remembers it.

Every request (v21.67) states its Department, its Project — a drop box with the Projects module's projects, the Accounting projects matrix and anything added here with ➕ Add a project — and its Classification (construction materials, greenhouse structure, irrigation, agri inputs, packaging, spare parts, electrical, fuel, fleet, tools, IT & office, safety, services, capex, or one you add). Classification is required. All purchase orders go out from APTI and carry the project.

Numbers and sync: PR / RFQ / PO / GRN numbers are the highest number already in the synced records plus one, so two computers cannot both issue PR-2026-000007; every change is stamped and uploaded within seconds.

A purchase that starts as a need on the shelf should start in Inventory → 🛒 Purchase Engine or as a Purchase Request in 📝 Requests, so the approval chain and the budget check happen before the money is committed. A goods receipt then raises the stock.

sections.h: The payroll figures on the dashboard
p: 📊 Accounting Dashboard shows Labor Payroll (latest) and Office Payroll (latest): the net of the most recent APPROVED run of each kind, and how many approved runs are on file. A draft run is not counted — it is not money that has left the company.
So a figure that looks low usually means the run has not been approved yet, not that the run is wrong. Check Payroll → 📊 History before chasing the number.

Accounting → 📂 Reports → 🧾 BIR Alphalist shows the live alphalist for the statement year, from APPROVED payroll runs only. Columns: gross; non-taxable (HR-card de minimis plus + Allowance de minimis); taxable (gross pay less SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG); tax withheld on compensation (not the EWT the company pays on management fees). The figures equal the BIR Center, the Full Alphalist and the 1601-C.

title: Licenses & Compliance
summary: Every licence and permit, when it expires, and whether the company is compliant today.

p: A licence that lapses can stop the business. Since v21.08 the old LICENSES screens open the real Compliance (CEA) screens: Registry and Expiring open 🏛 CEA ▸ 📜 Regulatory, and Dashboard and Compliance open the 🏛 CEA Command Center.

steps: Every new or renewed permit goes into 🏛 CEA ▸ 📜 Regulatory the day it arrives, with its expiry date.
Check the renewals there once a week, or open 📅 Follow-up Desk ▸ Renewals. Renewals take longer than people expect.
Attach the document, not just the date. A date with no paper behind it cannot be shown to an inspector.

p: Visa and immigration, BPI seeds, FPA fertiliser and the rest of the follow-up sit in 👔 Executive Assistant → 🛂 Gov Registrations, with their requirement checklists and renewal reminders.

title: Projects
summary: What is being built, what is planned, and what is finished.

head: Screen
What it holds
rows: 🚧 Active
What is being built right now, with its phases and progress.
📋 Planning
What is agreed but not started — the material lists and the schedule.
✅ Completed
Finished projects, kept for the record and for the next build.

p: The day is the unit of record on a build. Open 📓 Daily Site Reports and write one for each day: the weather, who was on site and for how many hours, the equipment, what was done against each activity, anything that went wrong, and a photograph of it.
steps: ➕ New day and pick the date — one report per day, and never a future date.

👷 Add PRJ15 contractors — the list is everyone whose employee card says they are a contractor on this project, and it marks who scanned that morning. Type ALL to take everyone who scanned, or pick by number for anyone who was there without scanning. Use ➕ Other trade only for people who are not on the project roster.
Give the hours each worked. That is what the productivity is measured against.
Record the work: pick the activity and the quantity done. Only an activity that is In Progress, Delayed or under Rework can take it.
Log any problem on the day it happened, and add at least one photo.
✅ Submit. From that moment it is the record for that day and cannot be edited — only an administrator can reopen it, with a reason.

note.k: THE REPORT AND THE CLOCK ARE COMPARED
note.t: Under the crew there is a line saying whether the two agree: who scanned but is not on the report, and who is on the report with no scan. Neither is wrong by itself — a man can work without scanning and a scan can be a visit — but the day should say which. A contractor only appears in that list once somebody has set “Contractor on project” on their employee card in HR.

p: The contractor labour tile on the project counts the days those contractors actually scanned, at their daily rate, plus any bonus and minus any penalty — and only between the project’s start date and today. Days worked before they joined the project, or on other work, are not billed to it.

note.t: A work line on the daily report credits the activity directly and owns that entry: change the line and the credit changes with it, delete the line and the credit goes. Do not also record the same work on the activity itself, or the project will count it twice. Quantity per manhour is worked out for you — never type it.

p: Work is not accepted by a manager typing “Accepted”. It is accepted by an inspection, and only for the quantity the inspector signs for.
steps: When an activity has completed quantity waiting, open 🔍 Inspections and offer it — the amount offered is what has been completed but not yet accepted.
Name the inspector and the day it is planned for.
The inspector walks each check and marks it pass, fail or n/a, with a note on what he saw, and adds photos.
✅ Pass & accept, then type the quantity accepted — never more than was offered. Or ❌ Fail, with the reason and the quantity to be redone.

note.t: A pass credits only the quantity signed for, and the inspection owns that credit — withdraw the inspection and exactly that acceptance goes. Accept less than was offered and the activity stays In Progress for the rest. A fail sends the activity to Rework Required and takes the rejected quantity back off the completed figure, so it has to be done again before it can be offered a second time.

p: A plan week can be closed, and closing it freezes it. The strip on the week says whether it is ready and, if not, exactly what is missing: a day inside the week with no submitted report, or an activity still open.
If work genuinely stopped — rain, a holiday, no materials — mark that day a no-work day with the reason. That counts as covered, and the reason stays on the record.

note.t: Only an administrator can reopen one, and the reason is kept. That is deliberate: a week nobody can quietly rewrite is what makes the site record worth anything.

p: GH15 and GH16 share one plan of nine weeks. Each week card shows its stage, how many line items it holds and how many pieces — and those two figures are COUNTED FROM THE LIST, so a line added to a week is counted the moment it is added.

Open a week to see its items-to-build list: what is planned, what is already in open requests, what has been issued, what is installed, and what is still to do. Item Requests are raised from the week itself, so the request carries the week and the material-list line it came from.
The two greenhouses split every line — GH15 takes its share and GH16 takes the rest — so a line added to the plan appears on both.

note.k: A DRAWING IS NOT A QUANTITY
note.t: An item added from a supplier drawing carries the drawing’s name in its remarks, and says so where the section or length was not on the drawing. Confirm the size before ordering against it.

p: A project that needs items raises them through Inventory → 📝 Requests like any other movement, so the stock leaves the shelf with a record and the project carries its real cost. Do not take material off a shelf without a request.

title: Reports
summary: Run any report on live data, and have the ones you need regularly arrive by e-mail.

steps: Open 🔎 Browse Reports.
Pick the module and the group.
Run it on the live data — it is not a saved copy.
Take the AI executive summary, or export CSV or PDF, or e-mail it.

p: 📨 Scheduler sends a report daily, weekly or monthly to @abapardes.com.ph recipients, so the people who need it stop asking for it.

note.t: If you find yourself asking someone for the same figures every Monday, that is a schedule, not a conversation.

sections.h: A zero in a report is a claim, not a shrug
p: Each block in a scheduled report reads the live store behind that screen, so a line saying “Today’s deliveries: 0” is asserting that nobody delivered anything. Where nothing has ever been recorded the block now says so in words — “No delivery has been logged in Nexi yet” — because “none today” and “none ever” are different problems and only one of them is about today.

note.k: IF A FIGURE LOOKS TOO GOOD
note.t: A clean zero on a busy day is worth thirty seconds on the screen it came from. Report it if the screen disagrees with the report.

title: Executive Assistant — government registrations
summary: Visa and immigration, BPI seeds, FPA fertiliser and the permits, with their requirement checklists and renewal reminders.

p: Each registration carries the list of requirements it needs and the date it must be renewed by. Work the checklist rather than remembering it — the reminders are there so a renewal is never discovered late.
Scan and attach what was submitted and what came back. When an agency asks what was filed in March, the answer should be one click, not a search through a drawer.

title: Administration
summary: Users and rights, approvals, the cloud sync, the audit log, the integrations, and the things that cannot be undone.

p: Everyone except Eyal and Dr Amy sees only the modules they were given: a per-user override in Administration ▸ Users (🔎 Access ▸ Grant), a department-head seat, their home department, the owner's standing grants, and the three everyone has — Overview, Tasks and Nexi Assistant. Role defaults no longer open extra modules. To give one person the wide role defaults again, press Lift Strict on their 🔎 Access card (that writes an explicit "wide" mark). 🔎 Audit all access compares against this regime.

sections.h: Someone cannot see a module — 🔎 Access (v21.56)
p: Administration ▸ Users ▸ 🔎 Audit all access (v21.60) checks everyone at once: for each active user the modules their role, home department and department-head seats should give them against what they get today; Grant on a row or ✅ Fix everyone writes the overrides. The button turns red with the count when someone is missing something.

Administration ▸ Users ▸ 🔎 Access on the person's row lists every module with what they get today (EDIT / VIEW / NONE) and the reason in one line: Strict is on, a per-user override, a role default an admin edited, the home department, or the role simply has no permission. Grant View or Edit there (a per-user override that beats the role default), Reset to remove it, or Lift Strict. The person sees it after a sync and a refresh.

A home department typed as an employee department (PROD_TRAINEES, APTI_REGULAR, APAC_PACKAGING…) now counts as the matching module, so a production supervisor whose card says a production department gets Production without an override.

Standing grants written into the app by the owner (Ederlyn, Jomel, Mea — v21.57/59/61) reach every computer with a refresh and beat Strict, overrides and role defaults; 🔎 Access shows them as "owner's standing grant".

sections.h: Your admin access cannot be taken away by a sync (v21.42)
p: It happened more than once: a computer with a stale copy of the user list uploaded it, the merge took the newer copy, and the primary admin found Administration locked on his own machine. Since v21.42 the admin record is guarded: it can lose the admin role or be deactivated ONLY through a deliberate change made by a signed-in primary admin on Administration ▸ 👥 Users (the change is stamped with who and when).

Any other path — a sync download, a migration, a restore, a stale device — is refused: the merge keeps the admin copy, the save puts the old role back and writes an audit line (admin_guard), and the merged list can never end with zero active admins.

If a copy still slips through, the admin’s own computer heals it on the next load: it remembers the admin login, restores the record, uploads it and shows “🛡 Your admin access was restored”. Hard refresh (Cmd+Shift+R) is enough; no emergency reset is needed.

sections.h: Rights are the first answer to most questions
p: 👥 Users is where a person gets view or edit on each module. Most "the button does nothing" reports are a missing edit right, not a bug.
✅ Approvals sets who may approve what, per position and per user, and drives the electronic signatures across every module.

head: Screen
What it is for
rows: ☁️ Cloud Sync
The backup and sync between the machines.
🛡 Old screens cannot upload

Since v21.33, a Nexi screen left open on an old version cannot upload anything. When a newer version is live, a red bar says so and uploads from that screen pause until you press ↻ Load the new version. Downloads keep working. This stops a forgotten tab from putting old data back over everyone's work.
🛡 Data Safety

Since v21.28 the sync engine carries three guards so one computer can never overwrite the company's records again: an empty device takes the cloud copy first (nothing it wrote before its first download is uploaded), an upload that would remove or rewrite a large share of a store is HELD here until an admin presses Upload anyway or Take the cloud copy, and a download that rewrote many records keeps the previous copy for 14 days with an Undo. The screen also lists the cloud version history once the hnx-sync worker carries the versions route, and the merge journal (why did my data change). Since v21.49 Data Safety is the primary admin's only (Admin-2 does not see the tab or the banner). Since v21.51 the owner decides for every computer from his own: ☁ Take the cloud copy on EVERY computer stores a dated decision that each computer applies when it next syncs — the cloud copy is taken for every upload it was holding at that moment, the hold is cleared, and an audit line names the stores. Uploads held after that moment stay held until the next decision. Since v22.18 the hold looks at WHICH COPY IS NEWER for the trips (the trip log and its safety journal): a logistics ✔ Check all of 61 trip days, an approval run or any other trip edit made on this computer goes up at once, however many days it touches, because each day is newer here by its own stamp. A trip upload is still held when it would remove many days, put an OLDER copy over many newer days, or send many checked or approved days back to pending (a re-open is never counted as ordinary work). Every other store, the employee roster above all, keeps the rule it had: a rewrite of a large share is held whatever its stamps say. A computer whose trip upload was held first takes in the newer days from the cloud — exactly what a normal download does — and is released by itself when what is left are its own newer edits, with an audit line; this also releases holds made before v22.18. The owner’s ☁ Take the cloud copy on EVERY computer always comes first: a hold that existed when he pressed it is never released or uploaded before the cloud copy is taken, and it keeps the date it was first made. When an upload is held on the computer of anybody but the owner, that person sees a small notice — “🛡 Your changes to … are waiting for the owner’s OK before they reach other computers” — and the owner gets ONE inbox alert per held store per day on his own computer, naming the person and the store; for the trips the safe choice is ☁ Take the cloud copy. The trip journal is no longer held on every start.
📂 Backups

Daily automatic backups, plus one before anything risky. Since v21.36 every signed-in computer also uploads its daily backup to the cloud archive (kept 30 days per computer), so the 🛡 Roster time machine and 🩹 Recover employee details can put a store back from the cloud even when the computer that made the backup is gone. Restore from here. Since v21.27 a normal restore is stamped with the backup's own time, so newer edits made on the other computers still win; 🛟 Roster only (admin) takes just the employee roster from a backup and makes it the truth on every computer — the way to undo a roster that came back with old departments and rates (1 Oct 2026).
